questions.control_topic: GxP intended use and system boundary
questions.audit_question: Walk through the proposed intended use, the patient, product-quality and data decisions it will support, and the evidence used to draw the GxP system boundary before funding was approved.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reconcile the business-case boundary with the process map, data-flow diagram, application inventory and any functions described as merely administrative; explain every mismatch.
questions.rationale_risk: An understated intended use or boundary can exclude regulated functions and records from validation and oversight.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved concept statement; end-to-end process and context diagrams; preliminary GxP assessment; named process/system/data owners; QA approval. Boundaries include interfaces, infrastructure, reports, records and supporting services and are internally consistent.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one release decision, one quality event and one regulatory record expected from the system; trace each from business process to system/component and accountable owner.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Regulatory/Compliance; Enterprise Architecture
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§1, 4.3; Guidance: WHO §§4-5 and 11.1.
questions.red_flags: No approved intended use; boundary omits reports, interfaces or infrastructure; GxP classification conflicts with process use; QA engaged only after funding.

questions.audit_question: Show how the concept team identified the predicate records, signatures, retention duties and inspection-access obligations for every jurisdiction and regulated business process in scope.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose a record the business case labels non-GxP and demonstrate why no batch, laboratory, complaint, stability, training or quality decision relies on it, including downstream exports.
questions.rationale_risk: Part 11 applies through predicate-rule records; missed jurisdictions or record duties create invalid scope and retention assumptions.
questions.expected_evidence: Jurisdiction/predicate-rule matrix; record inventory; Part 11/e-signature applicability assessment; EU/other market assessment; legal and QA review. Each conclusion cites the governing requirement and downstream use. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare three proposed records against URS drafts, SOP retention schedules, existing paper records and regulatory submission commitments.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; Regulatory Affairs; Legal/Privacy; Records Management; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1-11.2 and 211 Subpart J; Binding EU legal framework: Directive (EU) 2017/1572 Art. 9; Guidance: FDA Part 11 Scope and Application.
questions.red_flags: Applicability based only on technology label; no predicate-record mapping; enforcement discretion treated as exemption; markets or retention laws omitted.

questions.audit_question: Describe the proposed data lifecycle from first capture through processing, review, reporting, retention and destruction, and show where the concept explicitly protects attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring and available data.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one value that is transformed more than once and identify the original data, metadata, excluded or invalidated values, reviewer visibility and final record at every stage.
questions.rationale_risk: A benefits-led concept may automate outputs while leaving metadata, intermediate data or vulnerable manual steps outside governance.
questions.expected_evidence: Preliminary data-flow and lifecycle map; data criticality register; ALCOA+ assessment; proposed technical/procedural controls; QA-approved gaps and funding. All transformations and review points are visible.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample a manual entry, instrument/interface result and calculated value; compare process maps, prototype screens, reporting requirements and retention assumptions.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Business Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Solution Architect; Records Management
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68 and 211.180/188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §4.1; Guidance: MHRA §§3-5 and PIC/S §5.
questions.red_flags: Only final reports considered records; metadata/intermediate data absent; manual transcriptions not mapped; ALCOA+ cited without funded controls.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the concept distinguishes source data, raw data, metadata, official records, convenience copies and hybrid components, and how the authoritative version will be identified during an inspection.
questions.follow_up_probe: For a proposed printout or PDF, show why it preserves—or does not need—the dynamic data and metadata required to reconstruct the GxP activity.
questions.rationale_risk: Misidentifying a static report as the complete record can conceal changes, reprocessing or context needed for review.
questions.expected_evidence: Preliminary record catalogue; record-of-truth decisions; hybrid-system map; dynamic/static assessment; true-copy strategy; ownership and inspection retrieval requirements, approved by QA and records management.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Triangulate one electronic record, one printout and one interface export against the legacy SOP and proposed archival design. Triangulation: the auditor selects at least one routine item and one exception from the source population and reconciles them to an independent record.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Data Owner; Quality Assurance; Business Process Owner; Legal
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c) and 211.180/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.1, 4.10; Guidance: FDA DI Q9-Q10 and MHRA §§6.6-6.11.
questions.red_flags: Final output declared the sole record without rationale; raw data/metadata ownership unclear; hybrid links absent; inspector-copy capability unfunded.

questions.audit_question: Explain how preliminary risk assessment differentiated patient-safety, product-quality and data-integrity harm, and how that analysis changed scope, controls, budget or schedule.
questions.follow_up_probe: Present the highest-rated data element and the highest-rated workflow; show the causal chain to harm and why a lower-rated neighboring item received less control.
questions.rationale_risk: Risk scoring without causal reasoning can become a device for reducing assurance rather than focusing it.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved risk method; hazard statements; severity/probability/detectability rationale where used; critical data/process list; control decisions; residual-risk owners. Formality and evidence are proportionate to uncertainty and risk.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reperform two ratings with SMEs; compare them with deviation history, complaints, recalls, legacy failure modes and funding decisions.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Risk Lead; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Patient/Product SME; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
questions.red_flags: Generic risk statements; unexplained low scores; detectability credited without a control; high risk accepted by project management alone; risk used to waive a binding requirement. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how the business case funds documented evidence that the system will remain fit for intended use across configuration, testing, release, operation, change and retirement.
questions.follow_up_probe: Identify an assurance activity removed for cost or speed and demonstrate, through risk and alternative evidence, why confidence in the intended use was not reduced.
questions.rationale_risk: An underfunded lifecycle strategy creates paper compliance, weak testing and an inability to maintain the validated state.
questions.expected_evidence: Concept validation plan; lifecycle deliverables; risk-based assurance rationale; independent review; resource/skill estimates; environments and tools; acceptance gates; operational validation budget. Drug-GMP strategy meets predicate rules and Annex 11/15; device-only CSA is clearly scoped.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare the validation estimate with configuration count, interfaces, migrations, critical workflows and supplier evidence actually planned.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Quality Assurance; System Owner; Project Sponsor; Test Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4 and Annex 15 §§1-3; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §III and V.
questions.red_flags: Validation is a single pre-go-live test; no operational-state funding; CSA used to waive drug-GMP controls; estimates ignore interfaces/migration; QA approval not budgeted.

questions.audit_question: Walk through the proposed shared-responsibility model and show which GxP controls remain with the regulated company when infrastructure, administration, backup or release activity is outsourced.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one supplier statement that says a control is included and locate the contractual deliverable, customer configuration, monitoring evidence and named internal owner that make it effective.
questions.rationale_risk: Outsourcing execution does not transfer regulatory accountability; unclear boundaries create unowned controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Sourcing model; preliminary RACI; architecture and tenancy model; data location/ownership; supplier criticality; quality-agreement plan; audit/access/exit requirements; internal service owner. No critical control is unassigned. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Triangulate the business case, request-for-proposal, draft contract, architecture diagram and supplier marketing/security claims for five critical controls. Triangulation: the auditor selects at least one routine item and one exception from the source population and reconciles them to an independent record.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Quality; Procurement; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Information Security; Legal
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.1-3.4; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: Supplier certification treated as qualification; shared responsibility absent; internal owners unnamed; data or administrator location unknown; audit/regulator access excluded.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the concept and procurement timetable allow risk-based supplier evaluation, technical assessment, audit where warranted, and remediation before supplier lock-in.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show how the team would proceed if the preferred supplier refuses SDLC evidence, audit-trail design details, subcontractor visibility or regulator access.
questions.rationale_risk: Commercial selection before qualification can force acceptance of evidence gaps and unsuitable controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Supplier pre-screen; risk tier; due-diligence plan; audit criteria; evidence list; disqualification thresholds; remediation budget/timeline; approved exceptions. Contract award is gated by quality review.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare three bidder scorecards with their proposed contracts, security attestations, product roadmaps and known audit findings.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Quality; Procurement; Quality Assurance; IT Architecture; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3 and 4.5; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.3 and 10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: Preferred vendor exempted from qualification; no evidence-access criterion; audit scheduled after go-live; unresolved findings omitted from cost; price overrides critical quality criteria.

questions.audit_question: Describe the proposed identity lifecycle and authorization model from onboarding through role change, periodic review, emergency access and termination, and show how it supports attribution and least privilege.
questions.follow_up_probe: Map a contractor, service account and temporary elevated user from authoritative identity source to system record; explain who detects an orphaned or excessive entitlement.
questions.rationale_risk: Weak identity governance undermines attribution, confidentiality and the reliability of audit trails and signatures.
questions.expected_evidence: Concept IAM model; role families; joiner/mover/leaver process; service-account ownership; review cadence; authentication and federation assumptions; funding for logs and monitoring. Unique identities and accountable owners are explicit. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare proposed roles with legacy access lists, HR/contractor processes, supplier administrator model and segregation matrix.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Information Security; IAM Owner; Quality Assurance; Human Resources
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.100 and 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §12; Guidance: MHRA §6.16, PIC/S §9.5 and WHO §§11.6-11.9.
questions.red_flags: Shared/generic accounts; service accounts without owners; access review omitted from operating cost; supplier admins invisible; termination depends on informal notice.

questions.control_topic: Privileged administration and segregation of duties
questions.audit_question: Explain the proposed separation between business processing, record review, security administration, configuration and audit-trail oversight, including how a small operating team will control unavoidable conflicts.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the most powerful role and demonstrate how its holder is prevented from changing data or configuration and then concealing or approving the same activity.
questions.rationale_risk: Concentrated privileges can permit undetectable alteration of GxP data and control settings.
questions.expected_evidence: Preliminary segregation matrix; privileged-access design; break-glass process; independent log review; conflict approvals; supplier-admin oversight; compensating controls with owners and funding. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare proposed staffing, role catalogue, support model and audit-log ownership; simulate one emergency and one routine administrative activity.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Security Officer; Quality Assurance; Business Process Owner; Internal Audit
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), (e), (g); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§9 and 12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.13, 6.16 and WHO §§4.4, 11.6-11.12.
questions.red_flags: Administrator can alter records and logs; no independent reviewer; project assumes one person can own incompatible roles; break-glass use is not logged or reviewed.

questions.audit_question: Show how the concept determines which actions require electronic signatures, their meaning, identity proofing, credential controls and permanent linkage to the signed record.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace a proposed remote approval through identity proofing, authentication, signature manifestation, record version and later export; explain how reassignment or record change is prevented.
questions.rationale_risk: A workflow approval is not automatically a compliant electronic signature; weak linkage or meaning can invalidate accountability.
questions.expected_evidence: Signature applicability matrix; intended meanings; identity-proofing and credential lifecycle; signature/record linkage design; manifestation and copy requirements; jurisdictional assessment; policy and certification needs. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare three approval types with predicate requirements, prototype screens, IdP design and printed/exported record representations.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; Legal/Regulatory; IAM Owner; Business Process Owner; Solution Architect
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200 and 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §14; Guidance: FDA DI Q11 and MHRA §6.14.
questions.red_flags: Approval click treated as signature without assessment; signature meaning absent; record can change after signing; shared credentials; signature missing from human-readable copy.

questions.audit_question: Walk through every proposed inbound and outbound interface, identifying the authoritative source, transformation, timing, error owner, reconciliation point and retained evidence for each critical data element.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose an interface labeled one-way and show how duplicates, delayed messages, partial payloads, replay and downstream rejection would be detected without silently changing the source record.
questions.rationale_risk: Interface failures and transformations can lose context or create inconsistent records across systems.
questions.expected_evidence: Context/data-flow diagrams; preliminary interface register; data ownership matrix; transformation catalogue; reconciliation/error-handling concept; monitoring and support ownership; retention of transmission evidence.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace three critical fields across source schema, middleware, target record and report; compare timestamps, units, identifiers and error queues.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Integration Architect; System Owners; Quality Assurance; Operations Support
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8 and 5; Guidance: WHO §9 and PIC/S §9.4.
questions.red_flags: Unlisted middleware/manual transfer; target treated as authoritative without reconciliation; transformations undocumented; error queue owner absent; interface logs not retained.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the business case accounts for migrating or preserving legacy records, metadata, audit trails, signatures and relationships while maintaining value and meaning.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a corrected or reprocessed legacy record and show how its full history and signature linkage would survive the proposed conversion or archival approach.
questions.rationale_risk: Migration can produce complete-looking but contextually incomplete records and break traceability or retention duties.
questions.expected_evidence: Legacy inventory; migration/archival options analysis; data-quality profile; mapping and reconciliation concept; exception handling; retention and read-only access; resource estimate; QA acceptance criteria.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Profile three years/record types including exceptions; compare legacy schema, sample exports, target model, retention schedule and decommission plan.
questions.primary_roles: Data Migration Lead; Records Manager; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Business Process Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §4.8 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.8, 6.17, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
questions.red_flags: Budget covers only current master data; audit trails/signatures excluded; rejected records ignored; sampling proposed without population reconciliation; legacy reader has no support plan.

questions.control_topic: AI/analytics intended use and human oversight
questions.audit_question: Define each proposed algorithmic use, the decisions it may influence, the authoritative inputs and outputs, and the point at which a qualified human remains accountable for a GxP decision.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take the highest-impact use case and explain what happens when the model gives a plausible but wrong output, the source data changes, or the provider silently updates the model.
questions.rationale_risk: Opaque or adaptive functions can introduce uncontrolled transformations, drift and automation bias into regulated decisions.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved AI use-case inventory; intended-use boundaries; prohibited uses; data provenance; model/version ownership; human-review design; performance and drift criteria; change/incident controls; fallback. No draft EU Annex 22 is represented as current law.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare business-case benefit claims with prototype prompts/models, vendor terms, data-flow diagrams and proposed SOP/accountability statements.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Data Science/Model Owner; Quality Assurance; Information Security; Legal/Privacy
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding controls where electronic records are implicated: 21 CFR 11.10 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4, 10-13; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and WHO §§4-5, 11.
questions.red_flags: AI described only as productivity aid despite GxP influence; model/version not controlled; human review is rubber-stamping; training/input provenance unknown; supplier may change model without notice.

questions.audit_question: Explain how the concept identifies auditable events, preserves who/what/when/why, prevents audit-trail disablement, and resources risk-based review within the business process rather than as a technical afterthought.
questions.follow_up_probe: Estimate the review workload for the highest-volume record type and demonstrate that staffing, exception reports and review timing can detect issues before the related quality decision or release.
questions.rationale_risk: An audit trail that exists but is disabled, inaccessible or unreviewed does not provide effective oversight.
questions.expected_evidence: Preliminary audit-event matrix; review use cases/frequency; ownership and independence; volume/capacity estimate; retention/search/export requirements; administrator-event oversight; exception handling. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare proposed event coverage with legacy deviations, prototype capabilities, supplier documentation and batch/review timelines for two critical workflows.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; Data Reviewer; System Owner; Security Administrator; Business Process Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e) and 211.192/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: FDA DI Q7-Q8, MHRA §6.13, PIC/S §9.6 and WHO §§11.10-11.12.
questions.red_flags: Review effort absent from operating model; only log availability discussed; administrators can disable trails; reason-for-change not captured; review occurs after disposition/release.

questions.audit_question: Show how the concept identifies infrastructure and platform services that must be qualified or controlled to support the validated application, including clocks, databases, identity, networks and monitoring.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a managed platform service assumed to be supplier-controlled and demonstrate the evidence, configuration baseline and change notification needed to rely on it.
questions.rationale_risk: Unqualified or uncontrolled infrastructure can invalidate application evidence and affect record integrity or availability.
questions.expected_evidence: Preliminary architecture; service/component inventory; qualification responsibility; environment strategy; configuration and time-source concept; monitoring/patching ownership; evidence-access requirements. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare architecture layers with the supplier RACI, CMDB, cloud service catalogue and validation budget; trace one dependency not shown in the business case.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Owner; Cloud Architect; Validation Lead; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§3-4; Annex 15 §§3.2-3.14; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68.
questions.red_flags: Application-only validation; platform services omitted; no environment separation; time source uncontrolled; supplier responsibility asserted without evidence.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how required retention periods, readable retrieval, metadata/audit-trail preservation, legal holds and inspector access were converted into lifecycle cost and architecture assumptions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Retrieve a comparable legacy record near the end of retention and use the result to challenge the proposed format, index, viewer, migration and response-time assumptions.
questions.rationale_risk: Long-lived records can become unreadable, contextless or inaccessible even when backup copies exist.
questions.expected_evidence: Retention matrix tied to record type/jurisdiction; archival concept; format/viewer strategy; index/search requirements; legal-hold and deletion rules; periodic readability tests; inspection-copy service levels; funded ownership. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample short-, medium- and long-retention records; compare regulatory matrix, records schedule, supplier retention defaults, proposed storage tiers and decommission plan.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Quality Assurance; Legal; System Owner; Infrastructure Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c) and 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §6.17 and WHO §§11.15-11.19.
questions.red_flags: Retention based on vendor default; backup confused with archive; audit trails/metadata excluded; no supported viewer; deletion or legal-hold ownership unclear.

questions.audit_question: Explain how proposed recovery objectives were derived from product, patient, data and operational impact, and show that exact and complete backup plus restoration verification are included in cost and responsibilities.
questions.follow_up_probe: For a corruption event discovered after several backup cycles, show which recovery point preserves both records and audit history and how post-restore reconciliation would detect lost transactions.
questions.rationale_risk: A successful backup job does not establish recoverability, completeness or an acceptable loss window.
questions.expected_evidence: Business impact analysis; justified RTO/RPO; backup scope/frequency/immutability; restoration test plan; reconciliation and decision criteria; dependency map; supplier/internal responsibilities; periodic testing budget.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace one database, one file/object store and one external dependency through backup inventory, supplier SLA, recovery design and proposed test evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Business Continuity Lead; Infrastructure Owner; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b) and 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7 and 16; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
questions.red_flags: RPO/RTO copied from supplier tier; restore never planned; audit trails/configuration omitted; backup cannot survive tenant/account compromise; no reconciliation after recovery.

questions.audit_question: Walk through the proposed business-continuity process during prolonged system or interface loss, including controlled manual records, approvals, inventory/status control and reconciliation after service restoration.
questions.follow_up_probe: Simulate an outage spanning a batch, laboratory result and quality approval; identify where duplicate identifiers, back-dating or conflicting status could arise and how each is prevented.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled fallback can generate unattributable, duplicate or irreconcilable GxP records.
questions.expected_evidence: Critical-process BIA; continuity workflow; controlled forms/logs; authority and communication rules; offline numbering/time controls; reconciliation and QA review; periodic exercise plan; maximum tolerable outage.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare continuity assumptions with actual transaction volumes, site staffing, supplier SLA, paper-form controls and prior outage deviations.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Business Continuity; Quality Assurance; Site Operations; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §§5.1, 6.20 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
questions.red_flags: Fallback stated as use paper without controlled forms; no reconciliation owner; outage records can be entered later without event time; continuity capacity untested.

questions.audit_question: Show how the operating model will assess supplier releases, configuration and infrastructure changes, perform proportionate regression, approve deployment and periodically confirm the system remains fit for intended use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take a mandatory SaaS release scenario and explain how the company can obtain notice, assess GxP impact, test, reject or mitigate it before production exposure.
questions.rationale_risk: A compliant initial release can quickly lose its validated state without funded change and periodic-review controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Lifecycle support model; change categories and gates; supplier-release process; configuration baseline; regression approach; emergency-change control; periodic evaluation scope/cadence; backlog and ownership. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare the supplier roadmap/release frequency with internal change-board capacity, test environments, SOP lead times and periodic-review budget.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Change Manager; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance; Supplier Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-11; Guidance: ICH Q10 §§3.2.3-3.2.4 and Q9(R1) §4.6; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(k) and 211.68.
questions.red_flags: Go-live funding excludes operations; supplier releases bypass QA; no production baseline; periodic review is document expiry only; emergency changes remain unretrospectively approved.

questions.control_topic: Deviation, incident and regulatory escalation model
questions.audit_question: Describe how technical alerts, user errors, data-integrity concerns, security events and supplier incidents will enter the pharmaceutical quality system for impact assessment, investigation, CAPA and timely escalation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Walk one hypothetical clock drift or audit-trail outage from monitoring alert to affected-record identification, batch/product impact, root cause, CAPA effectiveness and regulator/customer notification decision.
questions.rationale_risk: IT ticket closure alone can miss GxP impact, affected data populations and systemic remediation.
questions.expected_evidence: Integrated incident/deviation workflow; severity and GxP impact criteria; data population analysis; investigation/CAPA requirements; supplier notification SLAs; security/quality handoff; management and regulator escalation thresholds. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare ITSM fields, PQS deviation requirements, cybersecurity playbooks, supplier contract drafts and historical incident response times.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; System Owner; IT Service Management; Information Security; Pharmacovigilance/Regulatory as applicable
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §13; Binding: 21 CFR 211.192; Guidance: FDA DI Q15/Q18, MHRA §§3.8-3.9, PIC/S §12 and WHO §13.
questions.red_flags: Only service tickets planned; no affected-record search; supplier notification after root cause only; DI/security events excluded from QA; CAPA effectiveness not funded.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the business case identifies the competencies and capacity needed for process ownership, configuration, validation, data review, administration, supplier oversight and support throughout the lifecycle.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reconcile the named future-state roles with current headcount and training records, then show how coverage is maintained during turnover, absence and vendor transition.
questions.rationale_risk: Controls fail when qualified independent personnel and sustainable operating capacity are absent.
questions.expected_evidence: Role/competency matrix; workload and segregation analysis; training curriculum and qualification criteria; succession/coverage plan; super-user limits; contractor oversight; recurring training and effectiveness measures; approved funding.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five critical roles and compare business-case assumptions with job descriptions, LMS history, support roster, segregation matrix and projected transaction/review volumes.
questions.primary_roles: Project Sponsor; Human Resources; Quality Assurance; Training Owner; System/Process Owners
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(i), 211.25 and 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §2; Guidance: FDA DI Q16, WHO §8 and ICH Q10 §2.
questions.red_flags: Key roles part-time with no workload analysis; training ends at go-live; supplier staff assumed qualified without evidence; incompatible duties assigned to one person; no backup personnel.

questions.audit_question: Present the major compliance assumptions and trade-offs in the approved business case and show how changes to cost, schedule or scope trigger independent quality reassessment and go/no-go decisions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the largest cost reduction and shortest schedule assumption and trace their effect on supplier qualification, requirements, migration, testing, training, continuity and operational controls.
questions.rationale_risk: Commercial pressure can silently convert constraints into accepted GxP risk without appropriate authority or evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: Decision log; assumptions register; quality gates; contingency and remediation reserves; independent QA approvals; escalation thresholds; benefits/schedule baseline; documented residual-risk acceptance by accountable management.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare steering minutes, finance model, validation estimate, risk register, procurement milestones and QA gate criteria for conflicting dates or exclusions.
questions.primary_roles: Project Sponsor; Quality Unit; Finance; Programme Manager; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding quality-unit authority: 21 CFR 211.22; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and ICH Q10 §§2, 4; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1.
questions.red_flags: QA lacks veto; launch date fixed before evidence; risk acceptance owned only by project; compliance contingency absent; critical deliverables removed without traceable decision.

questions.audit_question: Explain how proposed benefits and performance indicators avoid incentivizing delayed recording, data exclusion, unofficial testing, inappropriate reprocessing or closure of exceptions without adequate investigation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take the most financially important KPI and demonstrate how a user could game it through data timing, status changes or exclusions, then show the preventive and detective controls funded.
questions.rationale_risk: Poorly designed incentives can drive data-integrity failures even when technical controls exist.
questions.expected_evidence: Benefits/KPI catalogue; behavioral risk assessment; balanced quality metrics; definitions and data lineage; anti-gaming controls; escalation and speak-up channels; management review plan; culture/training actions. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare KPI formulas and targets with workflow permissions, audit events, deviation trends and bonus/contract terms for affected roles.
questions.primary_roles: Senior Management; Quality Culture Lead; Process Owner; Human Resources; Data Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: MHRA §§3.2-3.8, PIC/S §§6.1-6.7, WHO §§4.3-4.8 and ICH Q10 §2.
questions.red_flags: Benefits depend on fewer deviations or faster closure without quality balance; excluded data improves KPI; audit data used punitively without culture controls; speak-up path absent.

questions.audit_question: Show how the concept funds an exit strategy that preserves readable GxP records, metadata, audit trails, signatures, configurations and retrieval capability after contract termination or technology obsolescence.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume immediate supplier insolvency or account suspension and demonstrate how the company would obtain a complete, usable and verified record set plus the software, keys or viewer needed to inspect it.
questions.rationale_risk: Vendor lock-in or unsupported formats can make retained records unavailable and prevent compliant retirement.
questions.expected_evidence: Exit and decommission concept; data/export specifications; contractual assistance; escrow/viewer/key strategy where justified; verification and reconciliation; retention ownership; destruction authorization; budget and trigger points.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare draft contract termination clauses, sample supplier export, record catalogue, retention schedule, architecture dependencies and business-continuity plan.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Supplier Manager; Legal; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.17, 6.20, PIC/S §§9.9-10 and WHO §§7, 11.15-11.19; ICH Q10 §3.1.4.
questions.red_flags: Exit cost omitted; proprietary export without metadata; supplier owns encryption keys; destruction may occur before QA approval; no supported long-term viewer or reconciliation criterion.

questions.audit_question: Explain how business, quality, technical and data owners converted the approved intended use into the URS, and show how conflicts, assumptions, exclusions and unresolved requirements are governed before design begins.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select five requirements written or modified by the supplier and demonstrate the regulated-company SME who verified each business need, risk and acceptance criterion independently.
questions.rationale_risk: A supplier-led or copied URS can omit company-specific regulated workflows and turn solution features into unchallenged requirements.
questions.expected_evidence: Controlled URS; author/reviewer competence; comments and resolution log; requirements governance/RACI; glossary; assumptions, constraints and exclusions; QA approval. Requirements are uniquely identified, versioned, unambiguous and owned. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare URS revision history with workshop minutes, concept approval, process maps, supplier proposal and open-decision log; interview one author and one approver.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Business Analyst; Data Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding quality oversight: 21 CFR 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 4.4 and Annex 15 §§2-3; Guidance: ICH Q10 §2.
questions.red_flags: Supplier copied its product specification into the URS; requirements lack owners or unique IDs; exclusions are implicit; approval predates workshops; QA comments were closed without evidence. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Intended use, predicate records and scope traceability
questions.audit_question: Trace each intended use and predicate-record obligation into specific URS requirements for creation, review, approval, retention, retrieval and inspection, including functions outside the primary application boundary.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose one downstream report used for release or quality disposition and demonstrate the requirement chain back to its source data, metadata, reviewer and governing record obligation.
questions.rationale_risk: Missing traceability between regulated purpose and requirements can leave legally required controls unimplemented while the URS appears complete.
questions.expected_evidence: Intended-use statement; GxP/Part 11 assessment; predicate-rule matrix; record/signature inventory; bidirectional concept-to-URS traceability; system-boundary diagram. Every regulated use and record has testable requirements or approved rationale.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one batch, laboratory, quality and training/competence record where applicable; compare regulatory matrix, URS, record inventory and process SOP.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; Regulatory/Compliance; Business Process Owner; Records Manager; Business Analyst
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1-11.2, 11.10 and 211 Subpart J; Binding EU framework: Directive (EU) 2017/1572 Art. 9; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §4.4.
questions.red_flags: Part 11 assessment not linked to requirements; reports/exports omitted from boundary; predicate records unnamed; requirements cover storage but not review, retrieval or inspection.

questions.audit_question: Show how critical process steps, data elements, metadata, calculations, reports and configurations are identified in the URS and linked to preliminary risk decisions without using priority labels as a substitute for compliance.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take a requirement marked low priority that handles a critical identifier or status and reconcile the rating with its downstream use and failure consequence.
questions.rationale_risk: Commercial prioritization can conceal GxP criticality and drive insufficient design or testing.
questions.expected_evidence: Critical data/process inventory; requirement attributes for GxP impact and criticality; risk references; rationale and owners; rules separating business priority from quality risk; approved traceability.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Recalculate classifications for a stratified sample of critical, medium and low requirements using process FMEA, data-flow maps and actual decision use.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Risk Lead; Data Owner; Process SME; Quality Assurance; Business Analyst
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1 and 4.4; Guidance: MHRA §§4-5, PIC/S §5 and WHO §5.
questions.red_flags: MoSCoW priority used as risk; metadata/configuration not classified; low ratings lack causal rationale; criticality differs between URS and data inventory; mandatory controls marked optional.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how each URS statement expresses an observable outcome, boundary condition and acceptance criterion that can establish fitness for intended use rather than merely repeating policy words such as secure, compliant or user-friendly.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select three high-risk requirements and show the positive, negative, boundary and failure-recovery evidence that could objectively prove each one before design is known.
questions.rationale_risk: Untestable requirements create subjective release decisions and weak traceability from risk to assurance evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: Requirement quality checklist; measurable acceptance criteria; risk/test attributes; traceability conventions; verification method and responsible reviewer; approved ambiguity resolutions. Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all critical requirements and a random sample of noncritical ones; compare their wording with planned test methods, supplier capabilities and deviation-acceptance rules.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Quality Assurance; Business Analyst; Test Lead; Process Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.1, 4.4, 4.7 and Annex 15 §2; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.
questions.red_flags: Subjective adjectives without measures; multiple controls bundled into one requirement; negative/error cases absent; acceptance delegated solely to supplier; CSA cited outside device scope to reduce evidence.

questions.audit_question: Describe the URS requirements that preserve the full record context—originator, event time, system time, units, status, method, version, reason and relationships—from first capture through every transformation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose one displayed value and show every metadata element needed to reconstruct who did what, when and under which configuration; identify where the URS requires each element to be retained and reviewable.
questions.rationale_risk: A value without its metadata may be accurate-looking but not attributable, reconstructable or reviewable.
questions.expected_evidence: Data/metadata dictionary; ALCOA+ requirement mapping; time-zone and clock rules; contemporaneous capture; provenance and lineage; completeness rules; review and retention requirements; controlled rationale for any excluded metadata.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace a manual entry, instrument result and imported value through screen mockups, interface mappings, report requirements and retention specifications.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Quality Assurance; Business Analyst; Solution Architect; Records Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e) and 211.188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q1, MHRA §§6.1-6.7 and WHO §4.
questions.red_flags: Only visible fields specified; event and entry times conflated; time zone absent; metadata may be overwritten; lineage ends at report; ALCOA+ appears only in a generic preamble.

questions.audit_question: Walk through the URS audit-event matrix and show how requirements capture secure, computer-generated, time-stamped who/what/when/why history for record, configuration, security and critical master-data changes without obscuring the prior value.
questions.follow_up_probe: For a delete, overwrite, reprocess and administrator action, identify the required trail entry, reason capture, prior/new values and the user who can view but cannot alter the trail.
questions.rationale_risk: Generic logging requirements may omit regulated events, reasons or protection against privileged alteration.
questions.expected_evidence: Audit-event/use-case matrix; event content and reason rules; automatic enablement; immutable/protected storage; clock source; search/export and retention; disablement prohibition; independent access; supplier capability gaps resolved. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare the matrix with every editable field/status in three critical workflows, the role catalogue and supplier data model; trace one configuration change and one record deletion.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; Data Reviewer; Security Architect; System Owner; Business Analyst
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: MHRA §6.13, PIC/S §9.6 and WHO §§11.10-11.12.
questions.red_flags: Requirement says audit trail available without event definition; prior values/reasons absent; privileged users can disable/delete logs; configuration/security events excluded; time source unspecified.

questions.control_topic: Risk-based audit-trail review and exception reporting
questions.audit_question: Show how the URS turns audit-trail review into a usable control by specifying reviewer views, context, filters, exception logic, review timing, evidence of completion and escalation before the associated quality decision.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use expected transaction volume to demonstrate that the proposed review method can detect repeated changes, unusual times, privilege use and deleted/reprocessed data without relying on an unreadable raw log dump.
questions.rationale_risk: Audit-trail review can be nominal if the system cannot present meaningful, timely, contextual exceptions.
questions.expected_evidence: Review-use-case requirements; event criticality; frequency/timing; exception reports and drill-down; reviewer independence; completion/signature evidence; retention and escalation; workload/usability criteria. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample three record types and compare review requirements with batch/release timing, event volume, role conflicts, prototype reports and historical DI deviations.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Quality Reviewer; Quality Assurance; Product Owner; Test Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.192/194 and 11.10(e); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: FDA DI Q7-Q8, MHRA §6.13 and PIC/S §9.6.
questions.red_flags: Review frequency stated as periodic with no trigger; no completion evidence; raw technical logs only; reviewer cannot see source record; review follows release; workload exceeds capacity.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the URS specifies unique attribution, role-based least privilege, joiner/mover/leaver timing, periodic review and ownership for human, service, interface and robotic identities.
questions.follow_up_probe: Map the full lifecycle of one external contractor and one nonhuman account, including creation approval, credential storage, allowed transactions, monitoring, review and revocation.
questions.rationale_risk: Unowned or shared identities break attribution and allow excessive access to persist.
questions.expected_evidence: Identity classes; authentication requirements; role/permission matrix; account lifecycle SLAs; service-account owner and secret controls; periodic review; inactive/terminated lockout; federation dependencies; traceable approvals.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare requirements with HR/contractor sources, proposed IdP, supplier administrator model, interface register and three legacy access exceptions.
questions.primary_roles: IAM Owner; System Owner; Information Security; Quality Assurance; Human Resources
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.100 and 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §12; Guidance: MHRA §6.16, PIC/S §9.5 and WHO §§11.6-11.9.
questions.red_flags: Shared accounts allowed by convenience; nonhuman accounts omitted; role change SLA absent; supplier admins outside review; permissions described only by job title; inactive accounts persist.

questions.control_topic: Privileged access, segregation and emergency control
questions.audit_question: Explain how requirements separate record creation, approval, configuration, security administration, audit review and release, and how unavoidable conflicts and emergency access are independently authorized, logged and reviewed.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show every action available to the most privileged role and identify the independent evidence that would reveal alteration of data, audit settings, clocks, roles or configuration.
questions.rationale_risk: Privileged users can bypass application controls and conceal changes unless the URS designs effective separation and oversight.
questions.expected_evidence: Segregation-of-duties rules; privileged access management; just-in-time/break-glass requirements; prohibition or control of direct database access; immutable admin logs; independent review; conflict approval/expiry; remote-support restrictions. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Cross-check the permission matrix against workflow approvals, database/cloud roles, support model and audit-event requirements; test a small-site staffing scenario.
questions.primary_roles: Information Security; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Database/Cloud Owner; Internal Audit
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), (e), (g); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§9, 12; Guidance: MHRA §6.16 and WHO §§4.4, 11.6-11.12.
questions.red_flags: System admin may approve own changes; direct database access unaddressed; emergency account is shared; no independent admin-log review; conflicts have permanent approval.

questions.control_topic: Signature manifestation, meaning and record linkage
questions.audit_question: Trace each regulated approval into URS requirements for signer identity, date/time, signature meaning, authentication, non-repudiation and permanent linkage to the exact record version and human-readable copy.
questions.follow_up_probe: Change one field after a simulated signature and explain the required system behavior—invalidating, re-signing or preserving versions—and how an inspector would see the history.
questions.rationale_risk: A signature detached from the exact record version or without manifested meaning may not establish accountable approval.
questions.expected_evidence: Signature-use matrix; manifestation fields; controlled meanings; identity/credential rules; reauthentication; version/linkage behavior; post-signature change handling; copy/export display; certification/policy needs. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample three signature meanings across workflow and compare predicate requirement, URS, record model, IdP design and report/export specification.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; Regulatory/Legal; IAM Owner; Business Process Owner; Business Analyst
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §14; Guidance: FDA DI Q11 and MHRA §6.14.
questions.red_flags: Signature meaning inferred from button label; record editable without re-signature; exported record omits signature; shared credentials; timestamp source unclear; approval and authorship conflated.

questions.audit_question: Walk through each critical workflow and show how the URS requires permitted sequence, prerequisite evidence, role authority, status transitions and prevention or controlled override of out-of-order processing.
questions.follow_up_probe: Attempt to approve before required data exist, repeat a completed step, use an unauthorized role and reopen a released record; identify the specified response and retained evidence for each.
questions.rationale_risk: Weak workflow requirements permit bypass of procedural controls and ambiguous record status.
questions.expected_evidence: State-transition and use-case requirements; prerequisite/operational checks; authority matrix; override reasons/approval; duplicate/replay prevention; status visibility; exception/audit behavior; acceptance criteria.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare workflow diagrams with current SOP, role matrix, prototype, audit-event matrix and intended test cases for two critical and one exceptional path.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Business Analyst; Validation Lead; End-user SME
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(f)-(h) and 211.68(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§5, 6, 12; Guidance: PIC/S §9 and WHO §11.
questions.red_flags: Happy path only; override unlogged; roles can self-approve; prerequisites described only in SOP despite configurable enforcement; released records can be reopened silently. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Input, device, correction and error-handling requirements
questions.audit_question: Explain how the URS differentiates input sources and requires validity, completeness, range, format, unit, identifier and duplicate checks while preserving rejected attempts and controlled corrections where they are GxP-relevant.
questions.follow_up_probe: For a critical result, inject wrong units, future time, duplicate sample ID, truncated precision and device mismatch; show the required response, user message, audit evidence and escalation.
questions.rationale_risk: Poor input and device controls allow plausible but wrong data to enter records or cause invalid attempts to disappear.
questions.expected_evidence: Input/source catalogue; validation rules and boundaries; device/interface identification; error and reject handling; correction/reason rules; contemporaneous event time; review/escalation; testable messages and logging. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace five critical fields from data dictionary through screen/interface requirement, validation rule, audit event and report; compare with historical entry errors.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Process SME; Business Analyst; Integration Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), (h), 211.68 and 211.194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§5-6 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q2-Q3.
questions.red_flags: No unit/source validation; rejected values vanish; corrections overwrite originals; device identity not recorded; data-entry time substituted for event time; errors can be bypassed without reason.

questions.audit_question: Show how each interface requirement defines source and target records, field-level transformations, units/precision, identifiers, sequencing, acknowledgements, retries, duplicate control, reconciliation and retention of transmission evidence.
questions.follow_up_probe: Create a partial payload followed by retry and out-of-order delivery; explain how the requirements prevent duplicate or inconsistent records and make unresolved differences visible to a named owner.
questions.rationale_risk: Silent transformation, replay or partial failure can create divergent authoritative records.
questions.expected_evidence: Interface requirements/specification inputs; source-to-target mapping; transformation rules; control totals; error queues; retry/idempotency; time synchronization; monitoring/alerts; reconciliation frequency/owner; log retention.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select three high-criticality fields and compare URS, data-flow diagram, source/target dictionaries, middleware capability and record-retention matrix.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Lead; Data Owners; System Owners; Quality Assurance; Operations Support
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8 and 5; Guidance: MHRA §§6.8-6.9, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
questions.red_flags: Mappings omit metadata; no control totals; retries create duplicates; rejected messages can be deleted; ownership changes at middleware; interface evidence retained shorter than records.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the URS defines each GxP calculation or rule, authoritative inputs, version, units, precision, rounding, boundary behavior, invalid/missing-data handling and reproducible output.
questions.follow_up_probe: Recalculate a boundary case and a value that changes after source correction; show which version applies, how prior output is retained and when downstream decisions must be reassessed.
questions.rationale_risk: Unspecified algorithms and rounding can produce irreproducible results or hide changed inputs.
questions.expected_evidence: Calculation/rule catalogue; approved formulas and references; input provenance; precision/rounding/time-zone rules; version/effective dating; error behavior; explainability and traceability; independent verification criteria.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample all release-critical calculations plus a stratified sample of others; compare formulas in SOPs/spreadsheets, URS, prototype outputs and data dictionary.
questions.primary_roles: Process Scientist/SME; Data Owner; Business Analyst; Quality Assurance; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68 and 211.194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.4, 6; Guidance: FDA DI Q3 and WHO §§9, 11.
questions.red_flags: Formula source absent; spreadsheet result differs from URS; rounding defined only in code; version not stored with output; missing data treated as zero; recalculation overwrites history.

questions.audit_question: Explain how the URS identifies critical configuration and master data, assigns creation/change/approval authority, preserves effective versions and prevents unapproved values from influencing records.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one limit, workflow rule and product/specification value; trace who may propose, verify, approve, activate, backdate and retire it and which existing records remain linked to the prior version.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled configuration can change system behavior without code changes or visible record history.
questions.expected_evidence: Critical configuration/master-data inventory; lifecycle and approval requirements; segregation; effective dating/versioning; dual verification where risk warrants; audit trail; migration/reconciliation; rollback and impact assessment.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare URS with role matrix, configuration workbook, data dictionary, change SOP and three high-impact legacy master-data changes.
questions.primary_roles: Data Steward; Configuration Manager; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), (g), (k) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4, 10, 12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.12-6.16.
questions.red_flags: Critical parameters not inventoried; same user creates and approves; effective version not retained; changes bypass formal change control; backdating possible; records do not identify applied version.

questions.control_topic: Original/dynamic records, reports and accurate copies
questions.audit_question: Show how requirements identify the complete original electronic record and specify accurate, complete, human-readable and electronic copies that preserve needed metadata, audit history, relationships and dynamic review capability.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare a proposed PDF, printout and native export for one reprocessed or graphically reviewed record; explain which is sufficient for routine review, retention and FDA/EU inspection and why.
questions.rationale_risk: Static outputs may omit dynamic context, hidden data or audit history and therefore fail as originals or complete copies.
questions.expected_evidence: Original-record/true-copy assessment; report/export content; metadata and audit-trail inclusion; dynamic-data preservation; checksum/version controls; inspector search/filter/export; format readability and copy verification. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one chromatographic/graphical or other dynamic record, one workflow record and one aggregate report; compare URS to record inventory and supplier export demonstration.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Data Reviewer; Quality Assurance; Regulatory Inspection Lead; Product Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c), 211.180 and 211.194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§8, 17 and Chapter 4 §§4.1, 4.10; Guidance: FDA DI Q9-Q10 and MHRA §§6.10-6.11.
questions.red_flags: PDF declared complete without metadata assessment; inspector export requires vendor; native data unreadable outside production; filters hide excluded data; copy completeness not verified.

questions.audit_question: Describe how the URS requires preservation or justified archival of legacy values, metadata, audit trails, signatures, status, links and record meaning, including reconciliation and handling of invalid or unmappable data.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a legacy record with corrections, attachments and signatures and trace each component to the target or archive, including how a user proves completeness after migration.
questions.rationale_risk: A migration can preserve final values while destroying history, context and signature relationships.
questions.expected_evidence: Data-scope and mapping requirements; source/target counts and control totals; metadata/history/signature rules; transformation approval; exception/quarantine; repeatability; verification sampling rationale; legacy access and cutover reconciliation.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Stratify samples by record type, age, status, correction history and complexity; compare source queries, mapping, target records, exception logs and retention schedule.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Owner; Records Manager; Quality Assurance; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §4.8 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c); Guidance: MHRA §§6.8, 6.17, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
questions.red_flags: Only row counts required; unmappable data may be dropped; audit/signature history excluded; sampling population undefined; target can go live before reconciliation; legacy access unowned. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Retention, archive, legal hold and destruction requirements
questions.audit_question: Trace every record category to a requirement for retention start event, period, archive format, metadata/audit history, readability test, legal hold, authorized destruction and documented evidence of disposition.
questions.follow_up_probe: Apply two different jurisdictional retention rules and a legal hold to the same linked record set; show how the URS prevents premature deletion of the record or its dependent metadata.
questions.rationale_risk: Ambiguous retention logic can delete records too early or retain unusable fragments without context.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved retention matrix; event-based rules; archive/search/readability; linkage preservation; hold and purge authorization; destruction evidence; anonymization where applicable; supplier/default conflicts resolved.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five record classes across short/long retention and linked objects; compare URS, legal matrix, record schedule, vendor purge settings and decommission assumptions.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Legal/Privacy; Quality Assurance; Data Owner; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §6.17 and WHO §§11.15-11.19.
questions.red_flags: Retention period has no start event; child objects purge earlier; audit trails omitted; legal hold is manual and untested; vendor default overrides law; deletion leaves no evidence.

questions.control_topic: Backup integrity and verified restoration requirements
questions.audit_question: Show how the URS specifies exact and complete backup scope, frequency, protection, separation, monitoring and periodic restoration with reconciliation to justified RPO and RTO.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume latent corruption, compromised administrator credentials and loss of the primary region; demonstrate the required recovery source, integrity proof and transaction-level reconciliation.
questions.rationale_risk: Backup availability alone does not prove completeness, restorability or resilience to common-mode compromise.
questions.expected_evidence: Backup objects include data, metadata, audit trails, configuration, keys and dependencies; justified RPO/RTO; immutable/offline protection where risk warrants; restore frequency; acceptance/control totals; alerts and retained test evidence.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace one database, file store, audit-log store and encryption key through architecture, URS, supplier SLA, backup catalogue and restore-test plan.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Owner; Business Continuity Lead; System Owner; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b) and 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 16; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
questions.red_flags: Audit trail/configuration/keys omitted; no restore acceptance criteria; RPO exceeds business impact; backup shares compromised credentials; supplier restore evidence cannot be obtained.

questions.control_topic: Manual fallback and post-outage reconciliation requirements
questions.audit_question: Walk through URS requirements for controlled offline operation during application, interface, identity or site outages and for complete, duplicate-free reconciliation when service returns.
questions.follow_up_probe: Simulate two sites creating the same identifier offline while an interface queues messages; identify the required numbering, timestamp, approval, conflict resolution and QA review behavior.
questions.rationale_risk: Poor fallback design creates backdated, duplicate and inconsistent records after restoration.
questions.expected_evidence: Outage scenarios; controlled fallback records; unique/offline identifiers; event versus entry time; authority and approval; queued-interface handling; reconciliation/control totals; exception/QA review; exercise and capacity criteria.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare URS to BIA, current paper forms, identifier rules, supplier SLA, interface design and actual peak transaction volume.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Business Continuity; Quality Assurance; Integration Lead; Site Operations
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §5.1, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
questions.red_flags: Fallback is an uncontrolled spreadsheet; no offline numbering; event time lost; queued messages can replay; reconciliation lacks totals/owner; exercise requirement absent.

questions.control_topic: Security logging, time synchronization and data protection
questions.audit_question: Explain how the URS converts the GxP threat model into requirements for authentication, encryption, secure configuration, vulnerability handling, event logging, clock synchronization, monitoring and protection of data at rest and in transit.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace a compromised support account changing the system clock and exporting data; show which requirement prevents, detects, timestamps, contains and investigates each action without losing GxP evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Cyber compromise can alter availability, attribution, chronology or record integrity even when application functions test correctly.
questions.expected_evidence: Risk-linked security requirements; trusted time source and drift tolerance; security/audit log scope and retention; encryption/key ownership; secure baseline; vulnerability/patch SLAs; monitoring alerts; forensic preservation; remote-support controls. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Cross-check threat model, architecture, IAM roles, supplier controls, NIST/ISO mapping and GxP audit-event matrix; sample three high-risk threats.
questions.primary_roles: Information Security; System Owner; Infrastructure Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding GxP controls: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e) and 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 9, 12-13; Supplementary non-GxP: NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001.
questions.red_flags: Security requirements are a generic policy reference; clocks can be changed locally; SIEM logs do not link to GxP records; keys owned only by supplier; patch risk has no QA path.

questions.control_topic: Service levels, shared controls and data access
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how customer requirements define supplier versus company responsibilities for validation evidence, configuration, access, backup, incidents, changes, subcontractors, data location, inspection support and exit.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a control listed as supplier responsibility and identify the measurable SLA, evidence delivered, customer monitoring, escalation and remedy when it fails.
questions.rationale_risk: A feature-oriented URS can omit service and evidence requirements essential to outsourced GxP control.
questions.expected_evidence: Shared-responsibility and service requirements; evidence/deliverable catalogue; availability and notification SLAs; audit/regulator access; subprocessor/location controls; data ownership/export; validation package; exit assistance; internal owners. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare URS with RFP, proposed contract/quality agreement, supplier documentation, architecture and internal operating model for ten critical controls.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Quality; Procurement; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Legal; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 4.5; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: URS covers only application functions; supplier evidence optional; no subprocessor/location requirement; regulator access subject to vendor discretion; customer has no monitoring or exit data specification.

questions.control_topic: Change, release, incident and periodic-review requirements
questions.audit_question: Show how the URS specifies control and evidence for configuration/code changes, supplier releases, emergency changes, incident detection, affected-record analysis, CAPA and periodic evaluation of validated state.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use a forced supplier release that also causes intermittent record loss; trace required notice, impact assessment, regression, deployment decision, detection, record-population analysis and CAPA effectiveness.
questions.rationale_risk: Lifecycle controls omitted from the URS may be discovered only after go-live, when the company has little leverage or technical capability.
questions.expected_evidence: Change categories/notice and approval; configuration baselines; version/release history; regression and rollback; incident/alert interfaces; GxP impact and record search; CAPA linkage; periodic-review data and export requirements. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare URS with supplier release policy, change SOP, ITSM/PQS fields, monitoring design, contract SLAs and periodic-review template.
questions.primary_roles: Change Manager; System Owner; Supplier Manager; Quality Assurance; IT Service Management
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(k), 211.68 and 211.192; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-13; Guidance: ICH Q10 §§3.2.2-3.2.4.
questions.red_flags: Supplier changes need no notice; production baseline unavailable; incidents remain IT tickets; no affected-record query; periodic review cannot obtain access/change/deviation metrics.

questions.control_topic: Usability, error prevention and role qualification
questions.audit_question: Explain how user and administrator requirements address workload, clear status, error prevention, accessibility, reviewer context, training environment and demonstrable competence for critical tasks.
questions.follow_up_probe: Observe a representative user interpreting an exception and correcting an error in the prototype; reconcile hesitations or workarounds with URS usability and training requirements.
questions.rationale_risk: Poorly designed interfaces and superficial training drive workarounds, transcription errors and ineffective review.
questions.expected_evidence: User profiles and task analysis; critical-screen/workload requirements; warnings and confirmation rules; accessible context; training/test environment; role-specific curricula and qualification; effectiveness and refresher criteria; help/support controls. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample novice, experienced, reviewer and administrator roles; compare task analysis, prototype observation, known legacy errors, URS and training-role matrix.
questions.primary_roles: Training Owner; Human Factors/UX; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; System Administrator
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(i), 211.25; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 6; Guidance: FDA DI Q16, WHO §8 and ICH Q10 §2.
questions.red_flags: URS says intuitive so training unnecessary; no administrator qualification; reviewer screens omit original context; workload requires shortcuts; competence measured only by attendance.

questions.control_topic: Algorithmic/AI requirements and controlled human oversight
