questions.audit_question: Define URS requirements for every AI-enabled function covering intended use, prohibited decisions, data provenance, model/version identity, performance limits, explainability, qualified human review, drift monitoring, change and fallback.
questions.follow_up_probe: Introduce an out-of-distribution input, prompt injection or silent model-version change and show the required detection, output labeling, quarantine, impact assessment and retraining or rollback decision.
questions.rationale_risk: Adaptive or opaque functionality can change behavior without traditional code changes and can bias regulated decisions.
questions.expected_evidence: AI use-case and risk classification; input/output provenance; approved model/version; performance and failure thresholds; human authority and override; drift/security monitoring; reproducibility/logging; supplier change notice; validation and fallback. No draft Annex 22 clause cited as current.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare URS with vendor terms/model card, data-flow and privacy assessment, prototype logs, risk assessment and SOP decision rights for the highest-impact uses.
questions.primary_roles: Model Owner/Data Science; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Information Security; Legal/Privacy; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding where GxP electronic records/functions are implicated: 21 CFR 11.10 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4, 10-13; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and WHO §§4-5, 11.
questions.red_flags: AI feature not inventoried; model can change without notice; inputs/outputs not retained; human approval is nominal; no drift or failure threshold; generated content enters records without provenance.

questions.audit_question: Walk through the risk-assessment method, decision rules and governance used for this system, and demonstrate how the level of formality and documentation is proportionate to uncertainty, complexity and potential harm.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reperform one high, one medium and one low decision with independent SMEs; explain score differences, assumptions and why the method would not allow an otherwise noncompliant control to be accepted.
questions.rationale_risk: Mechanical scoring and undocumented subjectivity can make risk assessment a retrospective justification for reduced assurance.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved QRM procedure; trained cross-functional team; defined scope, scales and decision rules; evidence-based hazards; documented assumptions/uncertainty; independent QA review; escalation and risk-acceptance authority. QRM does not waive binding controls.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare ratings with meeting minutes, prior hazards/deviations, URS criticality, validation plan and actual control effort; interview two assessors separately.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Risk Lead; Quality Assurance; Process Owner; System Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
questions.red_flags: One-person assessment; all scores cluster low; severity reduced because controls exist; detectability credited without evidence; project owner accepts quality risk; binding requirement risk-scored away. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the risk boundary follows the complete intended use across application, infrastructure, interfaces, records, people, procedures and external services rather than the procurement boundary.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one component labeled out of scope and trace whether its failure could alter a GxP decision, record, timestamp, access authorization or recovery capability.
questions.rationale_risk: A narrow boundary omits dependencies and produces falsely low residual risk.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved intended use; context and data-flow diagrams; component/service inventory; dependency map; in/out rationale; process and data owners; linked URS and supplier responsibilities; QA approval.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace a critical record end-to-end through source, identity, middleware, storage, reporting, backup and archive; compare all diagrams and inventories.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Enterprise Architect; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Infrastructure Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1, 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§1, 4.3; Guidance: WHO §§4-5, 11.1.
questions.red_flags: Boundary equals vendor application only; identity, middleware or reporting excluded; diagrams conflict; out-of-scope rationale has no failure analysis; owners cannot identify dependencies.

questions.audit_question: Explain the categorisation rationale for each software and infrastructure component and show how category, novelty, configurability and actual intended use influence—but do not replace—function-level risk and assurance decisions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose a nominally standard or nonconfigured product and demonstrate that scripts, rules, reports, workflows, integrations and local extensions do not make its actual use more complex than the category suggests.
questions.rationale_risk: Category labels can be misused to prescribe documentation or testing without considering how the component is used.
questions.expected_evidence: Component inventory; category rationale and approved terminology; configuration/customization evidence; intended-use link; supplier/product maturity; function-level risk overlay; lifecycle deliverables justified independently of category.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare category register with repository objects, configuration exports, interface list, custom reports and supplier product description; sample components from every category.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Solution Architect; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier SME
questions.regulatory_alignment: Industry guidance: ISPE GAMP 5, 2nd ed. (voluntary; official full text is not publicly clause-verifiable—no clause number asserted); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5.
questions.red_flags: Whole system assigned one category; category based on marketing label; configured workflows/custom reports omitted; category automatically dictates minimal testing; invented or unverifiable GAMP clause citation. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how the assessment decomposed the system into software modules, configurations, custom code, reports, interfaces, infrastructure and supplier services at a level where distinct failure modes and controls can be evaluated.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare the assessed inventory with the deployment bill of materials and identify every executable, scheduled job, low-code workflow or external service absent from the risk record.
questions.rationale_risk: Undecomposed systems hide high-risk custom elements inside a low-risk product label.
questions.expected_evidence: Versioned component/service inventory; architecture and software bill of materials where available; configuration/custom object list; ownership; category and criticality; traceability to functions, suppliers and environments.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile risk inventory to CMDB/cloud catalogue, repositories, deployment manifest, interface register and supplier invoice for a production-like baseline.
questions.primary_roles: Solution Architect; Configuration Manager; Validation Lead; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), (k) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.3-4.7, 10; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.2-9.3.
questions.red_flags: Inventory at application-name level only; versions absent; low-code/custom objects unlisted; production differs from assessed baseline; supplier services and dependencies omitted.

questions.control_topic: Failure modes and causal link to harm
questions.audit_question: For each critical function, explain the credible failure modes and causal path from incorrect, missing, delayed or unauthorized system behavior to patient safety, product quality or supply impact.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take the top-rated and a low-rated failure mode and challenge both against worst credible use, existing detection time and the possibility of correlated failures across batches or sites.
questions.rationale_risk: Abstract harms without causal chains produce arbitrary severity and miss systemic consequences.
questions.expected_evidence: Function-level hazard analysis; affected process/record/product; causal chain; severity rationale; failure detectability and timing; current/proposed controls; cross-batch/site exposure; residual risk and owner.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Triangulate risk statements with complaints, recalls, deviations, process FMEA, batch disposition steps and URS; follow one common-cause dependency. Triangulation: the auditor selects at least one routine item and one exception from the source population and reconciles them to an independent record.
questions.primary_roles: Process SME; Patient Safety/Product Quality SME; Quality Risk Lead; Quality Assurance; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Binding quality controls: 21 CFR 211.68 and 211.192; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1.
questions.red_flags: Hazard is system failure with no consequence; severity lowered due to backup; correlated/batch-wide impact ignored; no product/process SME; risk inconsistent with release dependency.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the assessment combines data criticality with lifecycle vulnerability and detectability for raw data, metadata, audit trails, derived results, master data and reports.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one critical result and compare vulnerability at manual capture, interface transfer, calculation, review, archive and destruction; explain why the highest-risk stage received its controls.
questions.rationale_risk: Risk based only on final data importance misses vulnerable transformations and weak detection points.
questions.expected_evidence: Data inventory and lifecycle map; criticality rationale; vulnerability/control analysis by stage; detectability evidence; ALCOA+ impact; residual risk; links to URS, audit trail, review and retention controls. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace one manually entered, one interfaced and one calculated element; compare assessment with data-flow, metadata dictionary, role matrix and historical errors.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Quality Assurance; Process SME; Data Integrity Lead; Solution Architect
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and Annex 11 §1; Guidance: MHRA §§4-5, PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §§4-5.
questions.red_flags: Only final values assessed; metadata/audit trails excluded; detectability assumed from review not demonstrated; manual steps omitted; residual risk ignores cumulative lifecycle exposure.

questions.audit_question: Show how the assessment distinguishes predicate-rule risk, Part 11 electronic-record controls and electronic-signature controls, and how each applicable clause maps to functions and risks without treating compliance as a negotiable score.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose one approval and one retained electronic record; trace their regulatory basis, risk scenarios, mandatory controls and evidence, including any claimed enforcement discretion.
questions.rationale_risk: Conflating legal applicability with risk prioritization can omit mandatory controls or misuse FDA enforcement discretion.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved Part 11/predicate assessment; clause-to-function/control matrix; signature-use inventory; record-retention basis; scope/enforcement-discretion rationale reviewed by QA/legal; risk informs assurance depth, not requirement applicability.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare assessment with URS, signature matrix, record inventory, FDA Scope guidance and actual workflow use for three records.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Assurance; Regulatory/Legal; Validation Lead; Records Manager; IAM Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1-11.300 and 211 Subpart J; Guidance: FDA Part 11 Scope and Application and FDA DI Q11; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §14.
questions.red_flags: Enforcement discretion cited as exemption; Part 11 applicability based on vendor claim; signature risks absent; predicate records missing; mandatory control assigned low risk and removed.

questions.audit_question: Explain how the risk assessment evaluates impersonation, orphaned access, excessive privilege, conflicting duties, direct database access, service accounts and supplier administration across the identity lifecycle.
questions.follow_up_probe: Model misuse of the most powerful account and demonstrate which preventive and independent detective controls limit alteration of records, logs, clocks, roles and configuration.
questions.rationale_risk: Privileged access can compromise attribution and multiple control layers simultaneously.
questions.expected_evidence: Threat/failure scenarios by identity type; role/segregation matrix; privilege paths; control effectiveness evidence; compensating-control rationale; review frequency; residual risk and accountable owner. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare assessment with actual proposed roles, cloud/database privileges, support contract, IAM process and audit-event coverage; inspect three conflict scenarios.
questions.primary_roles: Information Security; IAM Owner; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Database/Cloud Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), (e), (g), 11.100, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §12; Guidance: MHRA §6.16, PIC/S §9.5 and WHO §§11.6-11.9.
questions.red_flags: Shared/service accounts unassessed; admin risk rated low because staff trusted; direct access excluded; SoD conflicts lack expiry/review; supplier privilege invisible.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how risk determines auditable events, protection, reason capture, review timing and reviewer context for data, configuration, access and administrative actions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use past deviations to test whether the proposed event set and review frequency would detect repeated edits, unofficial testing, clock changes, audit-trail disablement and post-approval alteration before impact.
questions.rationale_risk: A technically present audit trail may not detect critical behavior if event coverage or review design is risk-blind.
questions.expected_evidence: Audit-event risk matrix; event criticality; who/what/when/why and prior/new value requirements; protection/enablement; review method/frequency; exception logic; workload; residual gaps and compensating controls. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Map a critical workflow field-by-field to event coverage; compare with supplier capability, role privileges, review SOP draft and historical DI signals.
questions.primary_roles: Data Integrity Lead; Quality Reviewer; System Owner; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), 211.192/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: FDA DI Q7-Q8, MHRA §6.13, PIC/S §9.6 and WHO §§11.10-11.12.
questions.red_flags: Only record edits assessed; admin/config events omitted; review frequency has no risk basis; trail can be disabled; huge log volume makes control infeasible; past DI modes not tested.

questions.control_topic: Signature identity, linkage and repudiation risk
questions.audit_question: Walk through failure scenarios for identity proofing, credential sharing, signature meaning, authentication, record-version linkage, timestamp and post-signature change, and show how risk controls each scenario.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume a signer denies an approval after the record was amended; reconstruct the evidence that attributes the act and proves exactly what was signed.
questions.rationale_risk: Weak identity or linkage can make approvals legally and scientifically unreliable.
questions.expected_evidence: Signature threat/failure analysis; signer/use inventory; credential controls; manifestation/linkage/version behavior; reauthentication; timestamp; post-change handling; detection and investigation evidence; residual risk. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample three signature workflows; compare risk assessment, Part 11 assessment, IdP design, URS, record/export model and access roles.
questions.primary_roles: Regulatory/Legal; IAM Owner; Quality Assurance; Process Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §14; Guidance: MHRA §6.14 and FDA DI Q11.
questions.red_flags: Workflow approval assumed equivalent to signature; post-signature change not assessed; shared/federated credential risk omitted; exports break linkage; no denial/repudiation scenario.

questions.audit_question: For every interface, show how the assessment addresses partial, duplicate, delayed, out-of-order, corrupted, unmapped and unauthorized transfers plus transformation, precision and time-zone errors.
questions.follow_up_probe: Interrupt a multi-record transfer after acknowledgement and reason through source/target states, retry, reconciliation, retained evidence and decision impact.
questions.rationale_risk: Interface failure can create internally consistent but divergent regulated records that routine review will not detect.
questions.expected_evidence: Interface risk register; field criticality; failure modes; source/target authority; controls for validation, acknowledgements, idempotency, reconciliation and alerts; error-queue ownership; residual risk and recovery.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace three critical fields and one metadata field through schemas, mappings, middleware, target and report; compare with historical interface incidents.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Lead; Data Owners; System Owners; Quality Assurance; Operations Support
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8, 5; Guidance: MHRA §§6.8-6.9, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
questions.red_flags: Interfaces assessed as one function; metadata/units omitted; retries and error queues unassessed; target assumed correct; reconciliation is manual without capacity evidence. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Explain how migration risks cover selection, extraction, transformation, mapping, load, reconciliation and preservation of metadata, audit trails, signatures, links and record meaning.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose the most complex legacy record and show how duplicates, invalid data, orphaned attachments, character conversion and unmapped statuses would be detected and dispositioned without silent loss.
questions.rationale_risk: Migration can conceal systematic data loss behind successful row counts.
questions.expected_evidence: Migration risk assessment by data class and transformation; data profiling; control totals; mapping risks; exception/quarantine; repeatability; sampling rationale; legacy access; rollback/cutover risk; owners and acceptance authority.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile source profile, mapping, mock-migration results, exception trends, target samples and retention requirements across at least three strata.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Owner; Records Manager; Quality Assurance; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §4.8 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.8, 6.17, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c).
questions.red_flags: Risk based only on volume; metadata/history excluded; bad data dropped; no rollback; sampling ignores exceptions/rare records; source is decommissioned before reconciliation.

questions.control_topic: Supplier product, process and evidence risk
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how supplier criticality is derived from reliance, product complexity, evidence transparency, regulated experience, quality-system maturity, support model and ability to remediate defects.
questions.follow_up_probe: Challenge the preferred supplier using one unavailable SDLC artifact, one unresolved vulnerability and one adverse customer/regulatory event; show how risk and controls change.
questions.rationale_risk: Brand reputation or certification can mask evidence gaps and dependency on poorly controlled supplier processes.
questions.expected_evidence: Supplier risk model; due-diligence evidence; audit/assessment results; product and SDLC maturity; defect/security history; evidence gaps; remediation/contract controls; internal verification; residual risk and approval. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare supplier questionnaire claims with audit evidence, sample lifecycle records, contract, security reports and public/known incident history.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Quality; Procurement; Validation Lead; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 4.5; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.3, 10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: Questionnaire self-attestation only; certifications treated as GxP proof; evidence gaps not risked; supplier criticality reduced due to market share; no internal control for reliance.

questions.audit_question: Map each GxP control to provider, subprocessor and regulated-company responsibilities, then show how tenancy, location, concentration, privileged support, evidence access and service termination affect risk.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume a regional cloud failure and simultaneous loss of supplier support; demonstrate the control ownership, data access, recovery and decision path without relying on the failed provider.
questions.rationale_risk: Cloud dependency can create common-mode failures and unobservable control gaps across multiple services.
questions.expected_evidence: Shared-responsibility control matrix; subprocessor/dependency map; data and admin locations; tenancy/isolation analysis; SLA/evidence/audit rights; concentration and exit scenarios; internal monitoring; residual risk. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace five critical controls across URS, architecture, supplier contract, assurance reports and internal SOP; identify any circular dependency.
questions.primary_roles: Cloud Architect; Supplier Quality; Business Continuity; Information Security; Quality Assurance; Legal
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: Shared responsibility copied from marketing material; subprocessors unknown; one provider hosts production, backup and identity without concentration analysis; exit/recovery depends solely on vendor.

questions.control_topic: Threats to GxP integrity and availability
questions.audit_question: Show how cybersecurity threats are translated into GxP harm scenarios involving unauthorized change, loss of chronology, unavailable records, corrupted backups, altered configuration or compromised interfaces.
questions.follow_up_probe: Model ransomware with stolen administrator credentials and delayed detection; trace impact to records, audit trails, product decisions, recovery evidence and batch/customer actions.
questions.rationale_risk: A separate security risk register may miss pharmaceutical-quality consequences and evidence needs.
questions.expected_evidence: GxP-linked threat model; asset/data criticality; attack paths; preventive/detective/recovery controls; log/forensic needs; patch/vulnerability decisions; supplier dependencies; residual risk and quality escalation. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare security assessment, GxP risk register, architecture, privileged roles, backup design and incident playbooks; follow three attack paths.
questions.primary_roles: Information Security; Quality Assurance; System Owner; Infrastructure Owner; Business Continuity
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding GxP: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e), 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 12-13; Supplementary non-GxP: NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001.
questions.red_flags: Cyber risk declared out of GxP scope; backups assumed immune; security logs cannot identify affected records; patch deferral has no quality assessment; forensic evidence retention absent.

questions.audit_question: For each critical calculation or rule, demonstrate analysis of wrong formula/version, precision, rounding, unit, boundary, missing input, stale reference data and nonreproducible result.
questions.follow_up_probe: Perturb one input at a decision limit and one master-data version; show whether the outcome changes, how the risk was rated and which independent control detects an error.
questions.rationale_risk: Small algorithmic errors can systematically affect many records while appearing plausible.
questions.expected_evidence: Calculation inventory; formula/source approval; version and input provenance; boundary/precision failure analysis; scale of exposure; independent verification; monitoring; change control; residual risk. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Recalculate all release-critical algorithms and sample other rules; compare URS, legacy reference calculations, design source and risk ratings.
questions.primary_roles: Process Scientist; Data Owner; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance; Solution Architect
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68, 211.194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4, 6; Guidance: FDA DI Q3 and WHO §11.
questions.red_flags: Calculations treated as standard feature; systemic exposure not considered; boundary cases absent; output version not traceable; independent oracle uses same formula/code.

questions.control_topic: Model uncertainty, drift and human-oversight risk
questions.audit_question: Explain how the assessment evaluates data provenance, model limitations, bias, nondeterminism, drift, prompt/input manipulation, silent provider change, explainability and automation bias for each GxP use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Present the most credible confidently wrong output and demonstrate how a qualified user detects it, how affected records are found, and what threshold triggers rollback, revalidation or model suspension.
questions.rationale_risk: AI failure can be plausible, scalable and difficult to reconstruct without model/input/output evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: Use-case-specific model risk assessment; intended/prohibited uses; training/reference data provenance; performance by relevant strata; uncertainty/failure thresholds; human-control effectiveness; version/logging/drift/change controls; fallback and residual risk. No draft Annex 22 treated as current.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Challenge model on boundary/adversarial/rare cases; compare vendor claims, validation data, user observation, monitoring design and change terms.
questions.primary_roles: Model Owner/Data Science; Quality Assurance; Process SME; Information Security; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding where GxP records/functions are implicated: 21 CFR 11.10 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4, 10-13; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and WHO §§4-5, 11.
questions.red_flags: Generic AI risk score; wrong-output scenarios absent; human review assumed effective without study; model version/input/output not retained; provider updates unassessed; drift threshold undefined.

questions.audit_question: Show how risks from operating systems, databases, networks, time services, identity, virtualization, orchestration and monitoring are assessed in relation to application controls and validated state.
questions.follow_up_probe: Remove or misconfigure the shared time or identity service and explain which GxP functions fail, which records become suspect and how the event is detected and bounded.
questions.rationale_risk: Shared infrastructure can create systemic failures not visible in application-only assessment.
questions.expected_evidence: Dependency-level risk analysis; critical service inventory; qualification/control status; configuration baseline; redundancy/monitoring; patch/change ownership; supplier evidence; failure/recovery impact and residual risk. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile architecture and CMDB/cloud inventory with risk register, qualification plan and monitoring catalogue; trace one shared service across systems.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Owner; Enterprise Architect; Information Security; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§3-4; Annex 15 §§3.2-3.14; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68.
questions.red_flags: Infrastructure excluded as qualified by policy without evidence; shared services not assessed; configuration drift risk absent; application controls depend on uncontrolled clocks/identity.

questions.audit_question: Derive maximum tolerable outage, RTO and RPO from GxP process impact and analyze failure of application, interface, identity, site and supplier, including risks introduced by manual fallback and reconciliation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Simulate an outage at the worst process point and quantify records, batches, sites and decisions exposed before detection and recovery.
questions.rationale_risk: Generic availability ratings overlook the data-integrity risk created during workaround and catch-up.
questions.expected_evidence: BIA linked to GxP processes; outage scenarios; justified objectives; fallback hazards; duplicate/backdate/status risks; reconciliation controls; capacity/dependency analysis; residual risk and exercise needs.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare risk assumptions with peak volumes, current outage deviations, supplier SLA, continuity procedures and recovery-test results from predecessor services.
questions.primary_roles: Business Continuity; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; System Owner; Site Operations
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §§5.1, 6.20, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
questions.red_flags: RTO/RPO copied from IT tier; manual fallback assumed low risk; interface/identity outage omitted; affected population not quantified; reconciliation capacity unavailable.

questions.control_topic: Retention, archive, backup and restore risk
questions.audit_question: Distinguish archive and backup risks and show how the assessment covers retention duration, readability, metadata/audit-history completeness, legal holds, obsolescence, corruption, restore and authorized destruction.
questions.follow_up_probe: For a record late in retention, assume both format obsolescence and latent corruption; demonstrate detection, alternate recovery and proof that the reconstructed record is exact and complete.
questions.rationale_risk: Treating backup as archive can preserve bytes without usable, contextual or inspectable records.
questions.expected_evidence: Record-class risk analysis; retention/format/viewer dependencies; backup scope and threat isolation; restore/reconciliation; archive readability tests; hold/destruction controls; supplier/exit dependency; residual risk.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample short- and long-retention records, audit logs and attachments; compare retention matrix, archive design, backup catalogue, restore evidence and supplier defaults.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Infrastructure Owner; Quality Assurance; Business Continuity; Legal
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c), 211.68(b), 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 16-17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §6.17.
questions.red_flags: Archive/backup conflated; format and viewer risk absent; audit trail not backed up/archived; restore success based on job status; supplier purge conflicts with retention.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how each function/data risk determines the type, rigor, independence and retained evidence of assurance activities while all applicable requirements remain verified.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select two similarly rated risks with different assurance approaches and show why the evidence gives equivalent confidence; then identify a low-risk requirement that still requires verification.
questions.rationale_risk: A risk score applied only to test-script quantity can leave critical failure modes unchallenged or mandatory functions unverified.
questions.expected_evidence: Risk-control-requirement-test traceability; assurance rationale; supplier evidence leverage criteria; scripted and exploratory/error-case activities where appropriate; reviewer independence; acceptance/deviation rules; lifecycle maintenance. CSA caveat explicit.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare risk register, RTM, validation plan, supplier evidence and proposed tests for all critical risks plus a random low-risk sample.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Quality Assurance; Test Lead; Process Owner; Supplier Quality
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §4 and Annex 15 §§1-3; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.2-V.A.6.
questions.red_flags: Testing depth based solely on GAMP category; low-risk requirements not verified; supplier evidence accepted without applicability review; exploratory testing undocumented; CSA used outside scope as exemption.

questions.control_topic: Human error, workload and competence risk
questions.audit_question: Show how the assessment considers task complexity, interface design, workload, fatigue, ambiguous roles, training effectiveness, staff turnover and dependence on manual detective controls.
questions.follow_up_probe: Observe or simulate the highest-risk review task with a novice and experienced user; reconcile missed cues and workarounds with the assumed probability and detectability ratings.
questions.rationale_risk: Risk models often over-credit trained users and second-person review without evidence that controls work under real conditions.
questions.expected_evidence: Task/human-error analysis; role competence and workload data; usability findings; training/qualification needs; independent-review feasibility; staffing/coverage; procedural-control effectiveness and residual risk. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare assessment assumptions with error/deviation history, prototype observation, training records, staffing plan and expected transaction/review volume.
questions.primary_roles: Human Factors/UX; Training Owner; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Quality Risk Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(i), 211.25; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 6; Guidance: FDA DI Q16, WHO §8 and ICH Q10 §2.
questions.red_flags: Probability reduced because users trained; no workload/usability evidence; same person performs and detects error; turnover/absence ignored; training effectiveness assumed from attendance.

questions.audit_question: Explain how defects, deviations, security events, audit findings, recalls, workarounds and prior changes from this product, supplier and predecessor system informed failure likelihood and control selection.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a recurring legacy incident and demonstrate where its causal mechanism appears in the new risk assessment, URS, design control and planned effectiveness check.
questions.rationale_risk: Ignoring operational history makes risk ratings theoretical and allows known failure modes to recur.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence review of deviations/incidents/CAPAs/complaints/audits; supplier defect history; lessons-learned traceability; change scenarios; affected controls; monitoring and effectiveness measures; justified exclusions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five historical events across data, access, interface, backup and change; trace each to assessment and planned control, interviewing event owners.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; IT Service Management; Quality Assurance; Change Manager; Supplier Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.192 and 11.10(k); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-13; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §4.6 and ICH Q10 §§3.2.2-3.2.4.
questions.red_flags: Risk workshop starts from blank template; known deviations absent; supplier defect history unavailable; lessons listed but not tied to controls; change risk only assessed after deployment.

questions.audit_question: For every high or critical inherent risk, demonstrate that selected controls are specific, implemented by a named owner, testable, sustainable in operation and sufficient to justify the residual-risk conclusion.
questions.follow_up_probe: Remove the primary control for one high risk and show whether independent layers detect the failure before harm; explain any single-point dependence and monitoring threshold.
questions.rationale_risk: Risk can be understated when planned, vague or dependent controls are credited as fully effective.
questions.expected_evidence: Control descriptions linked to requirements/design/SOP; owner and timing; preventive/detective nature; effectiveness evidence/acceptance criteria; dependencies and common cause; residual rationale; appropriate quality/management approval; open actions gated.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample all critical/high residual risks and a selection of downgraded risks; compare risk record with URS, design, validation plan, staffing, contract and budget.
questions.primary_roles: Risk Owner; Control Owner; Quality Assurance; Process Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§4.4-4.6 and ICH Q10 §§2, 4; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: WHO §5.
questions.red_flags: Future control credited as effective; owner is a department not person/role; residual score drops without evidence; single detective control acts after release; project manager accepts quality risk.

questions.control_topic: Dynamic reassessment and periodic risk review
questions.audit_question: Define the events and evidence that will trigger risk reassessment—requirements/design changes, supplier releases, incidents, drift, new threats, performance trends, periodic evaluation and retirement—and show how prior assumptions remain traceable.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use a hypothetical supplier acquisition and security architecture change to demonstrate who detects the trigger, which risks reopen, how affected evidence is identified and who approves continued use.
questions.rationale_risk: A static pre-release assessment becomes obsolete as systems, suppliers, data and use evolve.
questions.expected_evidence: Risk-review procedure; trigger catalogue and owners; links to change/incident/periodic review; version history; trend inputs; overdue-action escalation; reapproval and communication; retirement/legacy risks; scheduled cadence based on risk. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare trigger rules with supplier contract, change SOP, incident workflow, periodic-review template, threat process and product roadmap; test three past changes.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Risk Lead; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Change Manager; Supplier Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §4.6 and ICH Q10 §§3.2.3-3.2.4, 4; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-11, 13; Guidance: PIC/S §5.6.
questions.red_flags: Review only at fixed document expiry; supplier/security/AI changes not triggers; prior rationale overwritten; risk actions can remain overdue through release; no owner monitors assumptions.

questions.audit_question: Explain how supplier criticality was determined from intended use, control reliance, data access, service substitutability, complexity and failure impact, and show how that rating set the depth of due diligence and approval.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare two suppliers with the same questionnaire score but different GxP reliance; demonstrate why their audit, evidence and ongoing-monitoring plans differ.
questions.rationale_risk: A generic vendor tier can under-qualify suppliers that operate critical controls or hold the only usable records.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved supplier-risk method; intended-use/control reliance map; criticality rationale; due-diligence/audit plan; evidence gaps; remediation and approval authority; requalification triggers. Assessment depth is risk-based and independent of spend or brand.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reperform ratings for the provider, a key subprocessor and a low-spend critical service; compare risk record, architecture, URS, RACI and contract.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Quality; Quality Assurance; System Owner; Procurement; Quality Risk Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 3; Guidance: PIC/S §§10.1-10.3, WHO §7, ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: Tier based on annual spend; SaaS automatically low risk; subprocessor not rated; questionnaire determines approval without verification; remediation deferred until after contract/go-live.

questions.audit_question: Walk through the supplier QMS from leadership oversight through document control, training, deviation/CAPA, change, internal audit and management review, and demonstrate its effectiveness with recent records rather than policy statements.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a repeated defect or audit finding and trace investigation, root cause, CAPA, effectiveness check and management escalation; reconcile any recurrence with the supplier's closure decision.
questions.rationale_risk: A documented QMS may be ineffective, especially when software quality and customer-impact processes are disconnected.
questions.expected_evidence: Current QMS scope/certificates; procedures and organization; management-review metrics; internal audit; deviations/CAPA and effectiveness; training; document/record control; customer-impact escalation; quality independence. Sample records show timely, sustained control.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one recent major change, defect, security event and CAPA; compare procedures, tickets, release notes, customer notices and management metrics.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Quality Leader; Supplier Audit Lead; Quality Assurance; Product Owner; Procurement
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.2-3.4, 4.5; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.3, 10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §§2, 2.7, 4.
questions.red_flags: Certificate scope excludes product/service; CAPAs close without effectiveness; repeat findings hidden in separate systems; quality reports to sales/project; customer-impact assessment undocumented. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Supplier SDLC and product lifecycle controls
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the supplier controls requirements, architecture, secure coding, code review, configuration, testing, release, maintenance and retirement for the exact product and version proposed.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one high-impact requirement from backlog through code/configuration, review, test, defect disposition, build and released version; explain every missing link.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled development and release practices weaken the reliability of supplier evidence leveraged by the regulated company.
questions.expected_evidence: Lifecycle procedures; version control and branch/review rules; requirements/design/test traceability; build/release integrity; environment segregation; defect/change records; support/EOL policy; sample end-to-end trace for current version.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select a critical feature, security fix and emergency hotfix; compare repository metadata, tickets, reviews, tests, build manifest and release notes.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Engineering; Supplier Quality; Validation Lead; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding customer validation duty: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 4.5-4.7, 10; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.2-9.3.
questions.red_flags: Policies not applied to sampled release; no code review; production build not traceable to tested artifact; hotfix bypasses lifecycle; custom/configured components excluded; EOL surprise.

questions.control_topic: Regulated experience, performance history and viability
questions.audit_question: Show how regulated-domain competence, inspection/customer history, defect trends, organizational stability, financial viability and product roadmap were evaluated against the required service life and retention horizon.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume acquisition, key-person loss or product discontinuation within two years; demonstrate which evidence and contractual/technical controls preserve support and GxP records.
questions.rationale_risk: A technically capable but unstable supplier can create unsupported systems and inaccessible long-lived records.
questions.expected_evidence: Relevant customer/use references; regulatory or audit history disclosures; defect/service metrics; staffing/turnover; financial/continuity review; roadmap and support dates; source/knowledge escrow or transition controls where risk warrants; monitored triggers. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Verify claims against sample support metrics, staff competence, release history, financial/ownership information and contract/EOL clauses; contact references where authorized.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Manager; Procurement; Finance/Risk; Quality Assurance; Legal; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: ICH Q10 §2.7, PIC/S §10 and WHO §7.
questions.red_flags: Regulated experience asserted without comparable use; adverse history undisclosed; one expert owns critical knowledge; product support ends before retention; no monitoring of ownership/viability.

questions.control_topic: Product architecture, configuration and customization transparency
questions.audit_question: Walk through the deployed architecture and identify standard functions, tenant configuration, custom code, low-code components, reports, integrations and shared services, showing which lifecycle evidence and owner covers each.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reconcile the supplier's standard-product claim with the actual object inventory and demonstrate how hidden extensions or customer-specific scripts are versioned, tested and supported.
questions.rationale_risk: Opaque product boundaries can hide custom behavior and invalidate categorisation, change impact and test leverage.
questions.expected_evidence: Current architecture; component/version inventory; standard/configured/custom classification; extension repositories; supported configuration rules; dependency/bill-of-material evidence; ownership and support boundaries; customer-specific baseline.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare proposal, demonstration tenant, production-like export, repository/object listing, deployment manifest and support catalogue.
questions.primary_roles: Solution Architect; Supplier Product Architect; Validation Lead; Configuration Manager; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.4, 4.3-4.7; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), (k), 211.68; Industry guidance: GAMP 5 2nd ed. without unverifiable clause claims.
questions.red_flags: Architecture is marketing-level; tenant customizations unlisted; production baseline cannot be exported; unsupported scripts used; component versions unknown; supplier/customer ownership overlaps.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how supplier specifications, testing, certifications and release evidence are evaluated for relevance to the customer's exact version, configuration, intended use and risk before being leveraged.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a supplier test claimed as coverage for a critical customer requirement and show matching preconditions, configuration, data, expected result, execution evidence, reviewer independence and unresolved defects.
questions.rationale_risk: Supplier testing may establish product quality but not fitness for a specific regulated use or tenant configuration.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence-leverage assessment; document provenance/version; supplier QMS basis; requirement/configuration applicability; test records and deviations; gap analysis; customer verification plan; controlled access and retention; QA approval. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five critical requirements across standard, configured, interface and security functions; compare supplier evidence with customer URS, risk and target baseline.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Supplier Quality; Supplier QA; Process Owner; Customer Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.3-3.4, 4.5-4.7; Guidance: WHO §§7, 11.1-11.5.
questions.red_flags: Certificate or summary replaces execution evidence; wrong version/configuration; supplier tests unverifiable; open defects omitted; customer relies on product validation claim; evidence inaccessible during inspection. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Test integrity, deviations and defect transparency
questions.audit_question: Trace how test data, expected results, execution identity/time, environment, actual outcomes, deviations and defects are controlled so that passing status cannot be created by excluding failed or repeated runs.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose a test with multiple executions and reconcile every run, failure, changed expected result, defect and final release decision from immutable source evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Selective testing or opaque defect disposition can overstate product assurance and conceal known limitations.
questions.expected_evidence: Controlled test management; original execution evidence and audit history; environment/build identity; all runs retained; deviation/defect linkage; retest prerequisites; severity/customer-impact rationale; release acceptance and known-issue disclosure.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample failed, repeated, blocked and passed tests from a current release; compare test system, defect tracker, repository/build and release notes.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Test Lead; Supplier Quality; Validation Lead; Customer Quality Assurance; Product Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding customer duty: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.6-4.7; Guidance: FDA DI principles Q2-Q3 and WHO §§11.1-11.5.
questions.red_flags: Failed runs deleted; expected result changed after execution; environment/build absent; defects closed as user error without investigation; customer-impacting known issues withheld; screenshots are sole evidence.

questions.audit_question: Explain how the supplier's security governance, risk management, independent assessments and certifications apply to the exact service, regions and subprocessors, and how gaps are translated into GxP risk rather than accepted by badge.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one certification control exception and one penetration-test finding; trace remediation, residual exposure, customer notification and the GxP functions that depend on the control.
questions.rationale_risk: Security certifications provide scoped assurance but do not prove GxP validation or eliminate service-specific weaknesses.
questions.expected_evidence: Security governance/RACI; current independent reports and scope; statement of applicability; penetration/vulnerability results; remediation evidence; incident metrics; customer control dependencies; risk acceptance and ongoing evidence schedule.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare certificate/report scope with architecture, regions, services, subprocessors and contract; sample exceptions to remediation tickets and technical evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Information Security; Supplier Security Officer; Quality Assurance; Cloud Architect; Supplier Quality
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding GxP: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e), 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 7, 12-13; Supplementary non-GxP: NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001.
questions.red_flags: Certificate scope excludes service/region; exceptions unavailable; pen-test summary is stale; security evidence treated as GxP validation; remediation dates conflict with risk acceptance.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how supplier employees, contractors, service accounts and emergency users are identity-proofed, authorized, segregated, monitored, periodically reviewed and revoked for customer environments.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one terminated supplier engineer and one emergency production access event through HR source, approval, MFA, session record, actions, review and revocation across all regions.
questions.rationale_risk: Supplier privileged access can bypass tenant controls and compromise attribution if customers cannot see or govern it.
questions.expected_evidence: Supplier IAM/PAM procedures; unique identity/MFA; role and tenant isolation; joiner/mover/leaver evidence; just-in-time/break-glass; session/action logs; independent review; customer notification; service-account ownership and secrets. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample active, transferred and terminated staff plus emergency access; compare HR, IAM, PAM, ticketing, tenant logs and customer reports.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier IAM/PAM Owner; Customer Security; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier Quality
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), (e), (g), 11.100, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §12; Guidance: MHRA §6.16, PIC/S §9.5 and WHO §§11.6-11.9.
questions.red_flags: Shared support IDs; customer cannot see privileged actions; leaver evidence sampled only locally; emergency access permanently enabled; subcontractors outside access review; direct database access unlogged.

questions.control_topic: Native audit-trail capability and tenant control
questions.audit_question: Show how the product automatically captures and protects who, what, when and why for relevant record, configuration, master-data, access and administrator events, including prior/new values and customer control over enablement.
questions.follow_up_probe: In a sandbox, alter, delete, reprocess and restore data, change a role and attempt to disable logging; reconcile every action to the resulting trail and immutable backend evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Supplier claims of logging may cover security telemetry but omit regulated record history or permit privileged alteration.
questions.expected_evidence: Event catalogue; field-level demonstrations; reason rules; trusted timestamps; immutable/protected storage; enablement/defaults; privileged-event coverage; retention/export/search; trail configuration baseline; known limitations and remediation.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test representative data, configuration, access and administrative events; compare demo results with documentation, database/log architecture and customer URS.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Product Owner; Data Integrity Lead; Customer Quality Assurance; Security Architect; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: MHRA §6.13, PIC/S §9.6 and WHO §§11.10-11.12.
questions.red_flags: Logs show only current value; no reason; supplier admin can disable/delete; audit trail off by default; tenant cannot export; configuration/access events missing; timestamps differ across services.

questions.control_topic: Tenancy, shared responsibility and control observability
questions.audit_question: Walk through the shared-responsibility model and demonstrate how tenant isolation, configuration boundaries, monitoring, backup, encryption, changes and evidence delivery operate for the proposed service architecture.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume a neighboring tenant exploit and a provider control failure; show how customer data exposure or corruption is prevented, detected, bounded, reported and evidenced.
questions.rationale_risk: Multi-tenancy and opaque provider layers can create unobservable common-control failures.
questions.expected_evidence: Detailed architecture/data-flow; responsibility matrix to control level; tenant-isolation evidence; control-plane access; configuration boundaries; monitoring and evidence catalogue; regions/dependencies; customer controls and residual gaps. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace five controls through supplier architecture, independent report, configuration screen/API, customer SOP and contract; inspect one control failure scenario.
questions.primary_roles: Cloud Architect; Supplier Security; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier Quality
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10 and WHO §7; Supplementary: NIST SP 800-53 SA-9 and access/audit control families.
questions.red_flags: RACI at provider/customer level only; tenant-isolation evidence absent; customer cannot observe control performance; shared control assigned to both or neither; hidden regional dependency.

questions.audit_question: Identify every subprocessor that can host, access, change, transmit, back up or support GxP data/services, and demonstrate risk-based qualification, contractual flow-down and ongoing change control.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the least visible fourth-party service and trace its access, location, control evidence, incident/change obligations and removal contingency to the customer agreement.
questions.rationale_risk: Critical controls may be performed by unqualified fourth parties outside audit and notification rights.
questions.expected_evidence: Complete subprocessor register; service/data/access mapping; qualification evidence; flow-down of quality/security/retention/audit/incident/change duties; advance notice and objection rights; monitoring and exit alternatives.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile subprocessor list across contract, privacy/security disclosures, architecture, network endpoints, invoices and independent assurance report.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Management; Legal/Privacy; Supplier Quality; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: Supplier says no subcontractors but cloud services exist; list is incomplete or marketing-only; no advance notice/objection; flow-down excludes inspection access; fourth-party incidents need not reach customer.

questions.control_topic: Data location, ownership, jurisdiction and control
questions.audit_question: Map where primary data, metadata, audit trails, backups, support copies and telemetry reside and who owns or controls each throughout active service, suspension, dispute and termination.
questions.follow_up_probe: Follow one customer record through backup replication, support extraction and log aggregation; reconcile actual locations and deletion/return rights with the contract and regulatory assumptions.
questions.rationale_risk: Unknown locations and ambiguous ownership can obstruct inspection, retention, confidentiality and recovery.
questions.expected_evidence: Data-location/flow map by artifact and region; ownership and controller/processor terms; encryption/key control; access jurisdictions; retention/deletion; suspension and lien protections; regulatory access; verified export/return rights. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare architecture, cloud configuration, subprocessor list, privacy documents, contract, sample logs and backup design for three data types.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Legal/Privacy; Records Manager; Supplier Manager; Quality Assurance; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.1-3.4; Binding record availability: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c), 211.180.
questions.red_flags: Location described only as global; logs/backups omitted; supplier can withhold data; customer lacks keys/export during suspension; deletion schedule conflicts with retention; support copies ungoverned.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the supplier specifies, tests and controls interface schemas, transformations, authentication, acknowledgements, retries, idempotency, error handling, version compatibility and retained transmission evidence.
questions.follow_up_probe: Recreate a breaking API change, partial payload and repeated retry; show customer notification, version coexistence, detection, reconciliation and records retained for investigation.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled interface changes or silent failures can create divergent GxP records across organizations.
questions.expected_evidence: Versioned interface/API specifications; field mappings; security; compatibility/deprecation policy; test evidence; monitoring/error queues; control totals/reconciliation; change notice; log retention; support ownership.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample a critical API, batch/file interface and manual export; compare documentation, test results, observed payloads, release notes, tickets and contract.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Architect; Supplier Engineering; Data Owner; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8, 5; Guidance: PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
questions.red_flags: API can change without notice; mapping omits metadata; no idempotency/reconciliation; supplier deletes error logs quickly; authentication relies on shared credential; deprecation shorter than change cycle.

questions.audit_question: Show the exact backup scope, schedules, retention, isolation, encryption, monitoring and restoration process for tenant data, metadata, audit trails, configuration, files and keys.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a completed restoration test and reconcile source and restored counts, hashes, relationships, audit history, application usability and exceptions rather than relying on job success status.
questions.rationale_risk: Backup procedures may omit critical artifacts or never prove application-level recoverability.
questions.expected_evidence: Backup architecture/inventory; RPO coverage; immutable/separate protection where justified; monitored jobs; tenant-level and regional restore; periodic test plan/results; data integrity reconciliation; failure CAPA; customer evidence and responsibilities.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace database, object/file store, audit logs, configuration and keys through backup catalogue and a restore test; compare with customer record inventory.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Infrastructure; Business Continuity; Customer System Owner; Quality Assurance; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b), 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §7; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
questions.red_flags: Audit trails/configuration/keys excluded; restore tests are infrastructure-only; tenant restoration unavailable; backup shares admin domain; test exceptions not investigated; customer receives no evidence.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the supplier derived and tested availability, capacity, RTO and RPO across application and external dependencies, and how customers are informed and supported during regional or prolonged disruption.
questions.follow_up_probe: Walk through the most recent exercise or real outage from detection to failover, data reconciliation, customer communication, return to normal and corrective actions, reconciling actual times with SLA claims.
questions.rationale_risk: Paper designs and aggregate uptime can mask inability to recover a tenant, dependent service or complete GxP record set.
questions.expected_evidence: BIA; dependency and failure-mode analysis; capacity/load evidence; DR architecture; exercise results with actual RTO/RPO and reconciliation; communication/escalation; deviations/CAPA; customer continuity inputs and recurring schedule.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one exercise and one incident; compare monitoring timestamps, status communications, tickets, recovered data, SLA report and CAPA.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Business Continuity; Operations; Customer Business Continuity; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §§9.9-10 and WHO §§7, 11.15-11.19; ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: Only tabletop exercise; no tenant/data reconciliation; actual RTO exceeds contract but reported as pass; hidden dependency not exercised; customer notifications delayed; CAPA absent.

questions.control_topic: Retention, archive, export and inspector access
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the service can retain and retrieve complete readable records—including metadata, audit trails, attachments, signatures and relationships—for customer-defined periods and provide accurate human-readable and electronic copies promptly.
questions.follow_up_probe: Retrieve an old, corrected and signed record from a nonproduction archive into both native and inspection formats; reconcile content, history, timing and searchability to the active record model.
questions.rationale_risk: Supplier retention defaults or proprietary archives can make required records incomplete or inaccessible.
questions.expected_evidence: Configurable retention; archive design/viewer; metadata/audit/signature preservation; legal hold and purge control; retrieval SLAs; export schemas and completeness verification; inspector/regulator access; format migration and readability tests.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample oldest available records, deleted/held records and complex attachments; compare service configuration, contract, export, restoration and retention matrix.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Supplier Product Owner; Customer Quality Assurance; Regulatory Inspection Lead; Legal
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c), 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§8, 17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.17, 6.20.
questions.red_flags: Vendor retention is shorter; exports omit audit/signature history; archive requires unsupported client; inspector retrieval depends on paid professional service; purge can bypass customer QA; old data unreadable. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how the supplier implements signer identity, date/time, meaning, reauthentication and inseparable linkage to the exact record version across user interface, API, export, archive and disaster recovery.
questions.follow_up_probe: Change the identity-provider attribute or signed record after approval and demonstrate how history, attribution, invalidation/re-signing and exported manifestation behave.
questions.rationale_risk: Federated identity or workflow approval may not preserve signature evidence and linkage across versions and exports.
questions.expected_evidence: Signature architecture and data model; supported meanings; identity/credential integration; version/linkage rules; post-signature change controls; manifestation in copies; timestamp; test evidence; IdP outage/migration and archive behavior. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample three signature workflows and one archived record; compare product demo, database/export, API, IdP logs, specifications and Part 11 assessment.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Product Owner; Customer Regulatory/Quality; IAM Architect; Validation Lead; Records Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §14; Guidance: FDA DI Q11 and MHRA §6.14.
questions.red_flags: Record changes without signature invalidation; meaning not stored; exported signature is image only; IdP account reassignment alters display; archive loses linkage; supplier calls any approval Part 11 compliant.

questions.control_topic: Supplier release, configuration and notification control
questions.audit_question: Trace the supplier's change process from request and impact assessment through design, test, approval, deployment, rollback and customer notification, including emergency changes and tenant configuration.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select an unplanned hotfix and reconcile code/build, risk, tests, approvals, deployment time, customer notice, regression and retrospective review; explain any undocumented interval.
questions.rationale_risk: Forced or opaque supplier changes can place the customer production system outside its validated state.
questions.expected_evidence: Change/release procedures; risk/customer-impact assessment; segregation and approvals; exact release content; advance notice and release notes; sandbox/test access; rollback; emergency retrospective review; configuration baselines; customer evidence/SLA. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample routine, major and emergency releases; compare tickets, repository/build, tests, approvals, production logs, release notes and customer notifications.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Change Manager; Product Engineering; Customer System Owner; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-11; Guidance: ICH Q10 §§3.2.3-3.2.4.
questions.red_flags: Production change precedes approval; customer notification after deployment; emergency label used routinely; release notes omit defects/config changes; no exact tenant baseline or rollback evidence.

questions.control_topic: Incident transparency, impact assessment and notification
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the supplier identifies GxP-relevant service, data-integrity and security incidents, preserves evidence, determines affected tenants/records, performs root cause and CAPA, and notifies customers in time for product decisions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose an incident initially classified as no customer impact and independently reconstruct the affected population from logs, code/configuration and timestamps; reconcile the result with the notification decision.
questions.rationale_risk: Supplier incident classification may minimize customer impact or provide insufficient detail for regulated investigations.
questions.expected_evidence: Incident criteria and 24/7 detection; tenant/record impact methodology; evidence preservation; notification content/timelines; root cause/CAPA/effectiveness; linkage to changes/defects; customer/regulator support; trend and escalation metrics. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample major, near-miss and security incidents; compare monitoring, tickets, source evidence, status pages, customer notices, RCA/CAPA and management review.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Incident Manager; Supplier Quality; Customer Quality Assurance; Information Security; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding customer investigation duty: 21 CFR 211.192; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §13; Guidance: FDA DI Q15/Q18, MHRA §§3.8-3.9, PIC/S §12 and WHO §13.
questions.red_flags: Notification only after root cause; no record-level affected-population method; near misses excluded; logs expire before investigation; CAPA summary unavailable; incident reclassified to avoid SLA.

questions.audit_question: Walk through vulnerability intake, GxP/security impact assessment, prioritization, patch testing, deployment, exception, monitoring and end-of-support planning for all product dependencies.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a critical vulnerability whose patch was delayed and trace compensating controls, quality approval, exposure monitoring, affected versions/tenants and closure evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Unpatched or unsupported components can compromise records, while rushed patches can disrupt validated functions.
questions.expected_evidence: Asset/version/SBOM evidence where available; vulnerability sources and SLAs; risk including GxP impact; patch validation/regression; approved exceptions with expiry; compensating monitoring; customer notice; supported-version/EOL roadmap.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample critical, exploited and aged vulnerabilities; reconcile scanner/advisory, product inventory, tickets, change records, deployment logs and customer communications.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Security; Engineering; Customer Information Security; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding GxP change/protection: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e), (k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-13; Supplementary: NIST SP 800-53 SI-2/SI-7.
questions.red_flags: Component inventory incomplete; critical patches indefinitely deferred; exceptions lack QA/expiry; patch testing undocumented; unsupported dependency hidden; customer cannot determine exposure.

questions.control_topic: Remote support, direct access and service records
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how remote support is requested, authorized, time-limited, supervised, recorded and reviewed, including direct database/file access, data extracts, diagnostic copies and actions performed outside application controls.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one support case involving data correction from customer approval through privileged session, commands, before/after evidence, audit record, independent review and deletion of diagnostic copies.
questions.rationale_risk: Support channels can bypass application audit trails and create ungoverned copies or changes.
questions.expected_evidence: Support-access procedure; customer authorization; unique PAM/session recording; approved tools; direct-change prohibition/exception; before/after and reason; data-minimization/copy disposal; ticket-to-audit linkage; independent review and customer report.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample routine, emergency and data-fix tickets; compare customer request, PAM logs, database/audit events, exports, change/deviation records and closure approval.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Support Manager; PAM Owner; Customer System Owner; Quality Assurance; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d)-(g) and 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 12-13; Guidance: MHRA §§6.16, 6.20 and PIC/S §10.
questions.red_flags: Shared support login; direct SQL change absent from audit trail; customer approval after action; session recording unavailable; data copied to unmanaged device; ticket says fixed without before/after evidence.

questions.audit_question: Show how the supplier defines, verifies and maintains competence for developers, testers, quality reviewers, administrators, incident responders and support personnel whose work affects customer GxP controls.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a recently transferred contractor who executed a production change and trace prerequisite training, supervised qualification, authorization date and effectiveness evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Unqualified or rapidly changing supplier staff can undermine lifecycle evidence and production controls.
