questions.expected_evidence: Role/competency matrix; job and qualification criteria; controlled curricula; training before access/work; practical assessment; refresher/change training; contractor equivalence; records; turnover/coverage and succession; quality oversight. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample staff across roles, sites, employment types and tenure; compare HR roster, LMS, access grants, work records, deviations and supervisor interviews.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Training Owner; Supplier Quality; Engineering/Operations Managers; Customer Quality Assurance; Supplier Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding customer reliance context: 21 CFR 11.10(i), 211.25; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2-3; Guidance: WHO §8 and ICH Q10 §§2, 2.7.
questions.red_flags: Access precedes training; contractor records unavailable; attendance equals qualification; role changes not retrained; quality reviewers lack independence/competence; single expert with no backup.

questions.control_topic: Supplier AI/model lifecycle and change transparency
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate the supplier's control of AI intended use, training/reference data provenance, model development, evaluation, versioning, prompts/configuration, monitoring, human oversight, security and customer notification of behavioral change.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose a model update and trace dataset/version, evaluation by relevant strata, known limitations, approvals, deployment, rollback, customer notice and ability to reproduce a pre-update output.
questions.rationale_risk: AI behavior may change through data, model or provider updates that traditional release documentation does not reveal.
questions.expected_evidence: AI feature inventory; intended/prohibited uses; data rights/provenance; model and prompt/version records; performance/failure criteria; bias/drift/security tests; human-review design; change/incident/CAPA; reproducibility, rollback and customer evidence. No draft Annex 22 represented as current.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample a major model update, drift alert and adverse output; compare model registry, data lineage, evaluations, tickets, release notes and customer contract.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Model Owner; Supplier Quality; Customer Process Owner; Validation Lead; Information Security; Legal/Privacy
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding where GxP functions/records implicated: 21 CFR 11.10 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 3-4, 10-13; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and WHO §§4-5, 7, 11.
questions.red_flags: AI feature hidden in standard release; training data provenance unavailable; model update not customer-notifiable; evaluations use nonrepresentative data; outputs cannot be reproduced; no drift or rollback evidence.

questions.control_topic: Quality agreement, audit rights and service exit
questions.audit_question: Reconcile the qualification findings with the executed contract and quality agreement, showing enforceable ownership, evidence delivery, change/incident notice, audit/regulator access, retention, CAPA, subprocessor and exit obligations.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume serious breach, supplier insolvency and immediate service termination; demonstrate the legal and technical path to complete usable records, keys, configuration, audit history, transition support and verified destruction.
questions.rationale_risk: A strong assessment has little control value if gaps are not contractually remediated and exit is impractical.
questions.expected_evidence: Signed quality/technical agreements; control-level RACI; SLAs and evidence; audit and regulator access; deviation/CAPA and notification; subprocessor flow-down; data ownership/location; export specification; exit/escrow/transition; destruction certificate; approved residual exceptions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select ten critical assessment controls and trace each to contract clause, operating procedure, monitoring evidence and named owner; test a sample export and termination scenario.
questions.primary_roles: Legal; Procurement; Supplier Quality; System Owner; Records Manager; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7; Binding record access: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c), 211.180.
questions.red_flags: Quality agreement unsigned at go-live; audit right limited to questionnaires; regulator access or raw evidence excluded; SLA has no remedy/escalation; exit export proprietary/incomplete; supplier may delete before QA authorization.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how every approved URS requirement and risk control is allocated to functional, configuration, technical and procedural design, with bidirectional traceability through unresolved decisions and approved exclusions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select five critical URS requirements and two risks with compensating controls; reconstruct each design decision, reviewer challenge, supplier assumption and verification method without relying on a traceability status alone.
questions.rationale_risk: A complete-looking traceability matrix can mask ambiguous, partially designed or procedurally displaced controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved functional/design specifications; unique IDs and revision control; URS/risk-to-design bidirectional traceability; decision/comment log; interface/procedure allocations; test method and acceptance links; independent QA/SME approval; no unexplained orphan or many-to-one mappings.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample all critical requirements plus random noncritical and procedural ones; compare URS, risk register, design sections, configuration workbooks, supplier backlog and planned tests.
questions.primary_roles: Solution Architect; Business Analyst; Validation Lead; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), (k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.1, 4.4-4.7 and Annex 15 §§2-3; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5.
questions.red_flags: Traceability populated before design review; requirements mapped to headings not mechanisms; procedural controls have no SOP owner; supplier backlog conflicts with approved design; orphan risks or tests.

questions.control_topic: System boundary, dependencies and qualified infrastructure
questions.audit_question: Walk through the logical and physical design from user and instrument to identity, application, middleware, databases, monitoring, backup and archive, showing how every GxP dependency is controlled and qualified where applicable.
questions.follow_up_probe: Remove the shared identity, time or network service from the diagram and demonstrate which controls fail, how the failure is detected and which records or decisions become suspect.
questions.rationale_risk: Application-centric designs omit infrastructure dependencies that determine attribution, chronology, availability and validated state.
questions.expected_evidence: Current logical/physical/data-flow diagrams; component/version and service inventory; trust zones; environments; responsibility/qualification status; redundancy/monitoring; time and identity dependencies; data locations; failure modes and linked requirements.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile design diagrams with CMDB/cloud inventory, supplier RACI, deployment manifest, network flows and qualification plan; trace three shared dependencies.
questions.primary_roles: Enterprise/Solution Architect; Infrastructure Owner; Cloud Architect; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§3-4; Annex 15 §§3.2-3.14; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68.
questions.red_flags: Marketing diagram used as design; versions/services missing; qualification boundary undefined; production dependencies absent; clocks/identity unmanaged; diagram contradicts actual cloud regions.

questions.control_topic: Data model, metadata, provenance and lifecycle
questions.audit_question: Explain how the design model represents raw/source data, metadata, event and entry times, units, status, method/configuration versions, relationships, provenance and invalidated values throughout the data lifecycle.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose a derived result with a later source correction and reconstruct both versions, all inputs, metadata, transformation, reviewer actions and downstream records from the proposed schema.
questions.rationale_risk: A schema focused on current values can destroy provenance and prevent reconstruction of regulated activity.
questions.expected_evidence: Entity/data model and dictionary; field definitions and ownership; immutable identifiers; lineage/provenance; event versus system time; version/effective dating; status and invalidation; relationship/cardinality; lifecycle state/retention; mappings to screens/interfaces/reports. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace a manual, interfaced and calculated value field-by-field through model, UI, interface, audit history and report; compare with URS and Chapter 4 record needs.
questions.primary_roles: Data Architect; Data Owner; Process SME; Quality Assurance; Records Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), 211.188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.1, 4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q1 and MHRA §§6.1-6.11.
questions.red_flags: Only current values modeled; event time overwritten by entry time; units/configuration not stored; invalid data hard-deleted; lineage stops at interface; relationships inferred from filenames.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate at field and event level how the design creates secure computer-generated time-stamped history showing who, what, when and why, including prior/new values, failed or prohibited actions where relevant, and changes by privileged or automated actors.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use the design to predict exact audit records for create, correction, deletion, reprocessing, configuration change, role change, clock change and attempted trail disablement; identify any event visible only to the supplier.
questions.rationale_risk: High-level logging designs often omit critical fields, reasons, automated actors or privileged operations.
questions.expected_evidence: Audit-event matrix tied to data/workflow model; event schemas and actor identity; trusted time; reason rules; prior/new value; append-only/immutable controls; automatic enablement; privilege/disablement protection; retention and export; supplier-visible events exposed to customer. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Map every editable field/status in two critical workflows and all privileged functions to event specifications; compare with supplier product capabilities and database/log design.
questions.primary_roles: Data Integrity Lead; Security Architect; Product Owner; Quality Assurance; Database/Cloud Architect
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: MHRA §6.13, PIC/S §9.6 and WHO §§11.10-11.12.
questions.red_flags: Audit design at table level only; previous value/reason missing; service/admin actors generic; trail shares mutable database privileges; clock source absent; supplier-only events inaccessible.

questions.control_topic: Review views, exception logic and completion evidence
questions.audit_question: Show how the design converts raw audit events into contextual, risk-based reviewer views with source-record drill-down, filters, exception logic, review period, reviewer identity, completion evidence and escalation before disposition or release.
questions.follow_up_probe: Run expected event volumes through the proposed exception rules and demonstrate how repeated edits, unusual times, privilege use, deletion, reprocessing and configuration changes appear without false-positive overload or hidden exclusions.
questions.rationale_risk: An immutable trail is ineffective if reviewers cannot interpret it completely and on time.
questions.expected_evidence: Reviewer workflow and screen/report design; event-to-exception rules with version control; filters and completeness indicators; source context/drill-down; reviewer independence/signoff; timing gates; escalation; retained review evidence; workload/performance criteria.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use historical or synthetic events from three critical processes; reconcile raw events, exception output, review evidence and batch/quality timing; inspect all default filters.
questions.primary_roles: Quality Reviewer; Process Owner; Data Integrity Lead; Product Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), 211.192/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: FDA DI Q7-Q8, MHRA §6.13 and PIC/S §9.6.
questions.red_flags: Raw CSV/log is sole review tool; default filter excludes admin/failed events; no completeness total; reviewer cannot see source data; completion can be backdated; review not linked to release.

questions.audit_question: Walk through the permission model from business role to object, action, data scope and workflow state, showing unique attribution, least privilege, inheritance, conflicting rights and default-deny behavior.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compose two benign roles into an excessive privilege path and explain how the design detects toxic combinations, site/data leakage and rights gained through groups or API scopes.
questions.rationale_risk: Role names alone conceal effective permissions and privilege escalation through inheritance or combinations.
questions.expected_evidence: Role/permission matrix at transaction/data level; role hierarchy and inheritance; data/site segregation; default and denied rights; service/API scopes; role-conflict rules; access approval/review data; versioned configuration and audit events. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Calculate effective access for five representative identities including contractor and service account; compare role design, IdP groups, application permissions, API scopes and workflow authority.
questions.primary_roles: IAM Architect; System Owner; Process Owner; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), (g), 11.100, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §12; Guidance: MHRA §6.16, PIC/S §9.5 and WHO §§11.6-11.9.
questions.red_flags: Permissions documented by role name only; broad default access; inherited rights unmodeled; API/service accounts bypass data scope; toxic combinations undetected; supplier admins excluded. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the design separates administration from GxP processing and approval, limits direct data access, controls emergency privilege and provides independent, tamper-resistant oversight of every privileged action.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume the primary administrator changes a result through the database and then edits role/log configuration; identify the independent technical evidence and control path that makes concealment infeasible.
questions.rationale_risk: Administrators can bypass application controls and compromise multiple evidence sources if privilege domains overlap.
questions.expected_evidence: Privileged-role matrix; PAM/just-in-time design; dual authorization where warranted; break-glass identity and expiry; session/command logging outside admin control; direct-data-change prohibition/controlled procedure; independent review; supplier access coverage. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace one routine, emergency and vendor support scenario through IAM/PAM, application, database/cloud and SIEM designs; challenge separation of log administration.
questions.primary_roles: Security Architect; PAM Owner; Database/Cloud Owner; Quality Assurance; Internal Audit
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), (e), (g); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§9, 12; Guidance: MHRA §6.16 and WHO §§11.6-11.12.
questions.red_flags: Shared emergency account; admin can alter data and evidence store; direct SQL lacks controlled record; supplier access bypasses PAM; conflict is accepted permanently; no independent reviewer.

questions.control_topic: Identity provider, credential and session design
questions.audit_question: Explain how identity proofing, unique identifiers, MFA, credential issuance/reset, lockout, session timeout, reauthentication and nonhuman secrets are designed across normal, offline, recovery and support modes.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take over a dormant session, reset a signer's credential and rotate an interface secret; show how identity, prior signatures, service continuity, logs and investigation evidence remain reliable.
questions.rationale_risk: Weak credential and session design permits impersonation or breaks attribution across federated dependencies.
questions.expected_evidence: Authentication flows and trust boundaries; identity source and immutable identifier; MFA/risk controls; reset/recovery; session/token lifetimes; lockout; service-secret vault/rotation; IdP outage/failover; authentication logs and time synchronization. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare application, IdP, PAM and API designs for employee, contractor, supplier, signer and service identity; trace reset and termination events.
questions.primary_roles: IAM Architect; Information Security; System Owner; Supplier IAM; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.100, 11.200, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §12; Guidance: PIC/S §9.5 and WHO §§11.6-11.9.
questions.red_flags: Email alone resets credentials; identity attribute can be reassigned; sessions persist after termination; service secrets hard-coded; failover enables shared local IDs; auth logs lack stable subject ID.

questions.control_topic: Signature transaction, manifestation and linkage design
questions.audit_question: Trace the signature transaction from record rendering and signer reauthentication through stored identity, date/time, meaning, record-version digest/linkage, manifestation, export and archival retrieval.
questions.follow_up_probe: Alter a signed field, attachment, signer display name and time zone in separate scenarios; demonstrate the required invalidation, version preservation, re-signing and inspector-visible history.
questions.rationale_risk: A signature can appear valid while being detached from changed content or mutable identity attributes.
questions.expected_evidence: Sequence/data model for signature; controlled meanings; immutable signer identifier plus displayed name; date/time/time-zone; reauthentication; record-version/content linkage; post-change behavior; human-readable/electronic copies; archive/migration and denial investigation. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample all signature meanings and one multisignature workflow; compare design, predicate assessment, IdP model, record schema, report/export and retention design.
questions.primary_roles: Regulatory/Legal; Quality Assurance; IAM Architect; Data Architect; Process Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, 11.300; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §14; Guidance: FDA DI Q11 and MHRA §6.14.
questions.red_flags: Signature stores display name only; no record digest/version; attachments excluded; exported copy omits meaning; time zone ambiguous; record remains signed after change; shared approval token.

questions.audit_question: Use the state model to demonstrate permitted transitions, prerequisites, role authority, status visibility, concurrency control, override conditions and audit behavior for normal and exceptional GxP workflows.
questions.follow_up_probe: Attempt simultaneous edits, approval before prerequisites, self-approval, reopening after release and duplicate execution; derive the exact system response and retained evidence from the specification.
questions.rationale_risk: Incomplete state design permits bypass, race conditions and ambiguous official status.
questions.expected_evidence: State-transition diagrams/tables; pre/postconditions; authority/segregation; locking/concurrency; duplicate/idempotency; override reason/approval; release gate; cancellation/reopen/version handling; event/audit and error specifications. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Walk all normal transitions and highest-risk exceptions for two workflows; compare current SOP, URS, roles, prototype, data model and planned tests.
questions.primary_roles: Process Owner; Business Analyst; Solution Architect; Quality Assurance; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(f)-(h), 211.68(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§5-6, 12, 15; Guidance: WHO §11.
questions.red_flags: Happy path only; race/concurrency undefined; privileged override bypasses audit; self-approval possible through role composition; released status reversible without new version; errors ignored. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Input, device, correction and invalidation design
questions.audit_question: Show how each input channel validates source, identity, format, unit, range, sequence, completeness and duplication while distinguishing original event time from later entry and preserving controlled corrections or invalidations.
questions.follow_up_probe: Inject an incorrect unit, duplicate identifier, future timestamp, truncated value and disconnected device; trace user feedback, stored attempt, audit event, review and escalation for each.
questions.rationale_risk: Channel-specific gaps can allow plausible wrong data or erase evidence of failed/changed input.
questions.expected_evidence: Input/channel specifications; device/source authentication; validation rules and boundaries; precision/units; event/entry time; error and rejected-attempt storage; correction/invalidation reason and prior value; second check where required; message/escalation behavior. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace five critical fields across UI, device/interface, data model, audit event and report; compare design rules with historical errors and URS.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Process SME; Device/Integration Engineer; Quality Assurance; Business Analyst
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), (h), 211.68, 211.194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§5-6 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q2-Q3.
questions.red_flags: Validation applies only to manual UI; rejected attempts discarded; event time defaults to entry time; corrections overwrite; device/source identity not stored; second checks cannot see original.

questions.control_topic: Formula, rule, precision and reproducibility design
questions.audit_question: For every critical formula and rule, identify authoritative inputs, source reference, version, units, precision, rounding, boundary/missing-data behavior, effective date and stored evidence needed to reproduce the result.
questions.follow_up_probe: Calculate just below, at and above a decision boundary, then change an input or rule version and show how prior and recomputed outcomes remain distinguishable and reviewable.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled formula and rounding details can cause systematic, irreproducible decision errors.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved calculation/rule specifications; exact formula/decision table; input provenance; unit and precision conventions; null/error behavior; version/effective dating; independent oracle; stored result lineage; recalculation and downstream-impact rules.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all release-critical calculations and a stratified sample of others; compare specification with scientific source, legacy verified result, code/configuration and test oracle.
questions.primary_roles: Process Scientist; Data Owner; Solution Architect; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68, 211.194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4, 6; Guidance: FDA DI Q3 and WHO §§9, 11.
questions.red_flags: Formula described in prose only; rounding in code but not spec; missing data treated silently; version absent from result; same implementation used as expected-value oracle; recalculation overwrites history.

questions.control_topic: Data contract, transformation, retry and reconciliation design
questions.audit_question: Walk each critical field and metadata element through the interface design, including schema/version, source authority, transformation, precision, authentication, sequencing, acknowledgement, retry, idempotency, error queue and reconciliation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Model partial delivery followed by timeout, replay and source correction; derive source/target states, duplicate prevention, retained evidence, alerts and resolution ownership.
questions.rationale_risk: Interfaces can create divergent yet plausible records unless failure and reconciliation behavior is designed explicitly.
questions.expected_evidence: Versioned interface/data-contract specification; source-target mapping; transformations; message IDs/control totals; authentication/encryption; acknowledgement/retry/idempotency; time semantics; error quarantine; monitoring/reconciliation; retention and change compatibility.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace three critical values and one audit/metadata element across source, middleware and target designs; compare with URS, API/product documentation and planned negative tests.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Architect; Data Owners; System Owners; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8, 5; Guidance: MHRA §§6.8-6.9, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
questions.red_flags: Mapping excludes units/metadata; retries not idempotent; error queue can be purged; no end-to-end control total; source/target authority differs by document; schema can change silently.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how critical configuration, specifications, limits, methods, templates and reference data are created, verified, approved, activated, versioned, linked to records, changed, rolled back and retired.
questions.follow_up_probe: Backdate a limit and modify a workflow parameter; show which permissions, effective-date constraints, audit events, impact assessment and existing-record links prevent silent retrospective behavior change.
questions.rationale_risk: Configuration changes can alter validated behavior without a software release and may affect historical interpretation.
questions.expected_evidence: Critical-item catalogue; data/configuration model; role/segregation; dual verification by risk; workflow and effective dating; version linkage to transactions; audit event; import/migration reconciliation; change/rollback; environment promotion and baseline controls.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one product limit, calculation parameter, workflow rule and report template; compare spec, role matrix, change process, audit design and record schema.
questions.primary_roles: Data Steward; Configuration Manager; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), (g), (k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4, 10, 12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.12-6.16.
questions.red_flags: Critical configuration not distinguished; creator self-approves; backdating unrestricted; records do not store applied version; direct import bypasses workflow; rollback erases intervening history.

questions.audit_question: Show how each report and export is derived from authoritative data and preserves required context, filters, units, versions, metadata, signatures and audit history so the output is accurate, complete and readily inspectable.
questions.follow_up_probe: Generate the same report with default, hidden and user-selected filters for a record containing corrections and excluded values; reconcile every difference to documented rules and visible report parameters.
questions.rationale_risk: Reports can silently omit data or context while appearing final and controlled.
questions.expected_evidence: Report/export catalogue; approved query and data lineage; filter/default visibility; template/version control; units/rounding; pagination/completeness totals; signature/audit metadata; native and human-readable formats; copy verification, performance and inspector access.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample release-critical, exception and ad hoc reports; compare specification, query/model, prototype output, raw records, retention and inspector-copy requirements.
questions.primary_roles: Reporting Lead; Data Owner; Records Manager; Quality Assurance; Regulatory Inspection Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c), 211.180/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§8, 17 and Chapter 4 §§4.1, 4.10; Guidance: FDA DI Q9-Q10.
questions.red_flags: Hidden/default filters; no population total; report query not versioned; audit/signature context omitted; ad hoc exports bypass access; supplier required to produce inspector copy.

questions.control_topic: Extraction, transformation, reconciliation and legacy access design
questions.audit_question: Explain how the migration design preserves value and meaning for data, metadata, audit trails, signatures, attachments, links and statuses, and how repeatable extraction, transformation, reconciliation, exception handling and rollback work.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take an invalid, corrected, signed and multiply linked legacy record through the mapping; show target/archival representation, rejected-data handling, control totals and evidence that no history was silently normalized away.
questions.rationale_risk: Migration design can convert diverse legacy states into superficially complete but scientifically incomplete records.
questions.expected_evidence: Source/target inventories and profiles; field/object mappings and transformation rules; history/signature/link preservation; repeatable controlled tooling; counts/hashes/control totals; exception/quarantine and approval; sampling strata; cutover/rollback; legacy read-only access and decommission gates. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile design with source schema/profile, target model, mock migration, exception catalogue, retention matrix and representative complex records.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Architect; Data Owner; Records Manager; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §4.8 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c); Guidance: MHRA §§6.8, 6.17, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
questions.red_flags: Row-count reconciliation only; normalization removes history; unmappable data dropped; signatures become images; tool/config not versioned; no rollback; legacy retired before QA acceptance.

questions.control_topic: Storage integrity, backup and restoration design
questions.audit_question: Trace the complete record set across transactional storage, files, indexes, audit stores, configuration, encryption keys and backups, showing integrity protection, failure detection, RPO and validated restoration/reconciliation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Restore to a point spanning an in-flight transaction and corrupted index; demonstrate how consistency, missing/duplicate records, audit chronology, links and key availability are proven before return to use.
questions.rationale_risk: Component-level recovery can yield an application that starts but contains inconsistent or incomplete regulated records.
questions.expected_evidence: Storage and consistency architecture; transactional boundaries; integrity/checksum controls; backup coverage/schedule/isolation; key recovery; RPO; restore sequence/dependencies; application-level reconciliation/control totals; acceptance, authorization and retained evidence.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace database, object store, search index, audit log, configuration and key service through design and proposed recovery test; compare supplier responsibilities.
questions.primary_roles: Database/Cloud Architect; Infrastructure Owner; Business Continuity; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b), 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 16; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
questions.red_flags: Search/index/file stores omitted; no point-in-time consistency; keys not recoverable independently; restore success equals service start; no transaction reconciliation; backups share compromised control plane.

questions.control_topic: Archive, retention, hold and destruction design
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how record-class retention start events, linked-object dependencies, archive format/viewer, readability checks, legal holds, authorized purge and destruction evidence are implemented without severing context.
questions.follow_up_probe: Apply a legal hold to one item within a linked record set while the normal retention period expires; derive which objects, audit history and indexes remain and how eventual release/destruction is approved.
questions.rationale_risk: Object-level purge and technology obsolescence can leave incomplete or unreadable records.
questions.expected_evidence: Retention-rule model; record-class mapping and start events; dependency graph; archive/index/viewer; format migration/readability test; hold inheritance; purge authorization/segregation; immutable destruction log; supplier/customer responsibilities and decommission compatibility. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five record types with attachments/signatures/audit history; compare retention matrix, data model, purge jobs, archive design, legal-hold process and supplier defaults.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Data Architect; Legal/Privacy; Quality Assurance; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(c), 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §6.17 and WHO §§11.15-11.19.
questions.red_flags: Retention begins at record creation regardless of rule; child objects purge independently; audit history excluded; legal hold does not propagate; purge admin self-approves; no long-term viewer/readability test.

questions.audit_question: Walk through design behavior during application, interface, identity, network and supplier outages, including controlled offline records, unique identifiers, event times, authority, queued transactions and complete reconciliation after recovery.
questions.follow_up_probe: Simulate two sites working offline while messages queue and a record is corrected in the source; show conflict resolution, chronology, duplicate prevention, approvals and QA-visible reconciliation evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Fallback and catch-up logic can introduce unattributable, duplicate, backdated or conflicting records.
questions.expected_evidence: Outage-mode state and data flows; controlled forms/local cache; identifier allocation; event versus synchronization time; degraded authentication/authority; message queue and idempotency; reconciliation totals/exceptions; QA release gate; capacity and exercise acceptance criteria.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Walk the worst outage scenario with process, integration, identity and recovery designs; compare actual peak volumes and current continuity procedure.
questions.primary_roles: Business Continuity; Process Owner; Integration Architect; Quality Assurance; Site Operations
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §5.1, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
questions.red_flags: Design says revert to paper without identifiers/controls; offline approvals share accounts; synchronization overwrites source; queued duplicates possible; no reconciliation gate before release.

questions.control_topic: Encryption, trusted time, monitoring and forensic design
questions.audit_question: Show how the design protects GxP confidentiality, integrity, chronology and availability through trust boundaries, encryption/key management, secure configuration, trusted time, security monitoring and preserved forensic evidence.
questions.follow_up_probe: Model stolen privileged credentials used to change clocks, configuration and records before exfiltration; identify exact preventive controls, correlated alerts, immutable evidence and affected-record query.
questions.rationale_risk: Security events can invalidate attribution and chronology unless controls are integrated with GxP records and investigation needs.
questions.expected_evidence: Threat-linked control architecture; network/trust zones; encryption in transit/at rest and key ownership/rotation/recovery; secure baseline; trusted time hierarchy/drift alerts; security log schema/correlation/retention; monitoring response; forensic preservation; GxP/PQS escalation. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace three high-risk attack paths across application, IdP/PAM, database/cloud, SIEM and backup designs; compare with NIST/ISO mapping and GxP audit events.
questions.primary_roles: Security Architect; Information Security Operations; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Infrastructure Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding GxP: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e), 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 9, 12-13; Supplementary non-GxP: NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001.
questions.red_flags: Encryption/key ownership vague; clocks independently editable; SIEM actor IDs cannot map to records; security logs retained too briefly; admin can alter evidence; incident design cannot query affected GxP data.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how specifications, code, configuration, master data, infrastructure and supplier releases are versioned, promoted through segregated environments, impact-assessed, tested, approved, deployed and rolled back while preserving the production baseline.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace an emergency configuration fix from detection to production and retrospective review, then prove which exact baseline was active for records created before, during and after the change.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled or unreconstructable configuration changes erode validated state and historical interpretability.
questions.expected_evidence: Configuration-item inventory; version/repository controls; environment and promotion design; segregation/approval; release manifest; impact/traceability/regression; deployment verification; rollback; emergency path; supplier notice; record-to-version association and periodic-evaluation data.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample standard, major and emergency changes; compare specification repository, change record, build/config export, test, approval, production log and record version.
questions.primary_roles: Change Manager; Configuration Manager; Validation Lead; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-11; Guidance: ICH Q10 §§3.2.3-3.2.4 and ICH Q9(R1) §4.6.
questions.red_flags: Configuration stored in uncontrolled workbook; production edited directly; environments share data/credentials; release manifest incomplete; rollback untested; records cannot identify applied baseline.

questions.control_topic: Detection, diagnostics and affected-record analysis design
questions.audit_question: Show how monitoring, application errors, audit events, interface queues, security alerts and user reports feed a design that preserves evidence, identifies affected records/batches, supports root cause and links incidents to deviations, CAPA and change.
questions.follow_up_probe: Create an intermittent calculation or interface defect that affects only certain versions; demonstrate the query, logs, configuration history and lineage needed to bound every impacted record and prove the remainder unaffected.
questions.rationale_risk: Without designed diagnostic and population-analysis capability, investigations rely on guesswork or incomplete logs.
questions.expected_evidence: Monitoring/event catalogue and thresholds; correlation identifiers; version/configuration and lineage links; error/retry evidence; immutable diagnostic retention; affected-population query/report; PQS/ITSM integration; privacy-controlled support data; root-cause/CAPA/change linkage. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace three failure scenarios from alert to affected-record report using design artifacts; compare log retention with detection/investigation timelines and supplier SLAs.
questions.primary_roles: IT Service Management; Quality Assurance; System Owner; Information Security; Data Architect
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.192 and 11.10(e), (k); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §13; Guidance: FDA DI Q15/Q18, MHRA §§3.8-3.9, PIC/S §12 and WHO §13.
questions.red_flags: Logs lack record/version correlation; diagnostics expire before trend detection; supplier has sole access; no query to bound affected population; error retries erase first failure; IT tickets cannot link to PQS.

questions.audit_question: Reconcile the technical design with the quality agreement and shared-responsibility matrix for tenant configuration, privileged access, audit evidence, change, backup, incidents, data location, subprocessors, inspection and exit.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose a control performed partly by supplier and customer and trace its complete data/evidence flow, monitoring threshold, failure escalation and fallback; identify any step assigned to neither party.
questions.rationale_risk: Shared controls often fail at handoffs even when each party's local design appears adequate.
questions.expected_evidence: Control-level RACI tied to architecture; tenant-isolation and configuration design; supplier/customer access; evidence APIs/reports; SLAs/alerts; data/subprocessor locations; release/incident interfaces; backup/exit design; contract/specification consistency and owner acceptance.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample ten critical shared controls and compare design, URS, supplier documentation, contract, internal SOP and test plan; verify tenant settings in a representative environment.
questions.primary_roles: Cloud Architect; Supplier Quality; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Legal/Procurement; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
questions.red_flags: RACI contradicts design/contract; shared control has no end-to-end owner; supplier-only evidence inaccessible; tenant defaults differ from specification; subprocessor/data location absent; exit not technically designed.

questions.control_topic: Model, prompt, data and oversight design
questions.audit_question: Explain the design for model and prompt/version control, input/output provenance, performance boundaries, nondeterminism, human review, drift, security, adverse-output handling, supplier updates, reproducibility and fallback for each GxP use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Inject an adversarial or out-of-distribution input and then change the provider model; show how the design labels uncertainty, blocks or escalates output, preserves evidence, detects drift and reconstructs the exact decision context.
questions.rationale_risk: Opaque and changing AI behavior can introduce scalable errors that are difficult to reproduce or attribute.
questions.expected_evidence: AI component/data-flow and threat model; approved model/prompt/configuration registry; input/output/context logging; data rights/provenance; performance/failure criteria; human authority/override; drift monitoring; model-change and rollback; deterministic controls where needed; incident and affected-record design. No draft Annex 22 cited as current.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Challenge highest-impact use cases across normal, boundary, rare and adversarial inputs; compare design with risk, vendor evidence, URS, model registry, monitoring and SOP decision rights.
questions.primary_roles: Model Owner/Data Science; Solution Architect; Process SME; Quality Assurance; Information Security; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding where GxP functions/records implicated: 21 CFR 11.10 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4, 10-13; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and WHO §§4-5, 11.
questions.red_flags: Model/provider version not stored; prompts/configuration uncontrolled; human reviewer sees no source context; outputs enter records automatically; no drift/failure threshold; affected records cannot be queried; draft Annex 22 misrepresented.

questions.control_topic: Design testability, error cases and training inputs
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the specifications expose observable outcomes, diagnostic evidence and controllable test conditions for critical normal, boundary, negative, recovery and misuse cases, and that design outputs define role-specific training and competence needs.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a control said to be tested indirectly and a control relying on trained behavior; show the independent evidence, failure injection, user observation and acceptance criteria that prove each works under realistic workload.
questions.rationale_risk: Unobservable controls and assumed user competence create tests that confirm scripts rather than system behavior and operating effectiveness.
questions.expected_evidence: Design-to-test traceability; test hooks/logs/data reset and environment controls; positive/negative/boundary/recovery use cases; objective acceptance criteria; independent oracles; usability/task analysis; error messages/help; role/competency and training-design inputs; residual procedural controls with effectiveness measures.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all high-risk controls plus a sample of low-risk and procedural controls; compare specifications, planned tests, prototype observation, historical errors, SOP drafts and training matrix.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Test Architect; Human Factors/UX; Training Owner; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), (i), 211.25, 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 4.7 and Annex 15 §§1-3; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.4-V.A.6.
questions.red_flags: Acceptance cannot be observed objectively; tests depend on production-only logs; negative/recovery cases omitted; expected oracle uses same code; trained users credited without usability evidence; CSA used outside device scope to avoid documentation.

questions.audit_question: Walk me through how every GxP-relevant configuration item in the implemented build is derived from an approved requirement or design decision and how unauthorized or undocumented settings are detected before testing.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one high-risk setting changed late in the build and trace it from requirement and risk assessment through design approval, repository history, deployment record, test evidence, deviation assessment, and the current configuration export.
questions.rationale_risk: An apparently validated application can contain unapproved parameters that change calculations, workflow, security, retention, or record meaning.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: configuration specification, approved baseline, parameter inventory, repository history, build/deployment manifests, review records, and variance report. Acceptance: every critical setting is uniquely identified, approved, reproducible, traceable, and reconciled to the tested build; unexplained drift is absent.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one security parameter, one workflow rule, one calculation parameter, and one recent late change; compare documents, repository, deployment tool, and live non-production export.
questions.primary_roles: Configuration Lead; Validation Lead; System Owner; Developer; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.6 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k), where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Spreadsheet-only baseline; settings maintained outside change control; production values cannot be reconstructed; repository and deployed export differ; late change lacks risk-based retest.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the regulated user established that internal and supplier development activities operated under an appropriate quality system, including defect control, review independence, records retention, and release discipline.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show the quality records for the component with the highest defect density and reconcile the supplier's stated process to actual commits, reviews, test failures, and released binaries.
questions.rationale_risk: A supplier certificate or questionnaire can mask ineffective development controls and leave the regulated company unable to justify reliance on supplier evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: supplier assessment, quality agreement, development plan, lifecycle procedures, audit report, defect metrics, review records, release records, and regulated-user acceptance. Acceptance: responsibilities are explicit, actual practice matches the assessed process, critical gaps are remediated or formally controlled, and evidence is available to inspectors.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Choose one supplier release and one internally developed extension; compare contractual commitments, supplier records, issue tracker, repository, validation plan, and QA review.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Quality; Development Lead; System Owner; Procurement; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3.1-3.4 and 4.5-4.6; ICH Q9(R1) quality risk management.
questions.red_flags: Generic supplier questionnaire; no right to evidence; material subcontractor unknown; supplier process not reconciled to actual records; unresolved critical audit observations.

questions.audit_question: Show how traceability proves both that every approved GxP requirement is implemented and tested and that every GxP-relevant code or configuration element has a justified upstream requirement and risk control.
questions.follow_up_probe: Starting from a randomly selected production-facing configuration rule, trace backward to intended use and risk, then forward to positive, negative, and regression tests without relying on manually curated hyperlinks alone.
questions.rationale_risk: One-way matrices can hide gold-plating, orphaned functionality, untested controls, and configuration introduced outside the approved scope.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: controlled requirements, design/configuration specifications, risk assessment, repository tags, traceability matrix, test cases/results, and orphan analysis. Acceptance: identifiers are stable; forward and reverse coverage is complete for GxP scope; exceptions are justified and approved; the matrix reconciles to source systems.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five high-risk requirements, two defects, and two configuration items; cross-check document links against repository and test-management records.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Validation Lead; Development Lead; Test Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.4, 4.6 and 4.7; 21 CFR 11.10(a), where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Trace matrix generated after testing; broken or circular references; orphan code/configuration; requirements marked tested by unrelated evidence; unexplained excluded requirements. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Explain how source code, scripts, configuration-as-code, and report definitions are protected so that the approved version can be attributed, reviewed, reproduced, and linked to the deployed release.
questions.follow_up_probe: Rebuild or independently hash one released artifact from its signed tag and reconcile the result to the artifact repository and deployment record; explain any binary difference.
questions.rationale_risk: Weak repository controls permit unreviewed changes, substitution of artifacts, loss of provenance, or inability to reproduce the validated version.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: repository access model, protected-branch settings, immutable tags, commit history, pull-request approvals, artifact hashes/signatures, build log, and retention controls. Acceptance: released artifacts are uniquely linked to reviewed source; histories are retained and tamper-evident; privileged bypass is restricted and monitored.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one routine and one emergency fix; compare ticket approvals, commit identity/time, peer review, build output, artifact checksum, and deployment evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Development Lead; DevOps Lead; Configuration Manager; Information Security; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.6 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k); NIST SP 800-218 is supporting secure-development guidance, not a GMP regulation.
questions.red_flags: Shared developer accounts; mutable release tags; direct commits to protected branches; artifact lacks hash/provenance; administrators can erase history without detection.

questions.audit_question: Walk me through the controlled promotion path from development to test to production and show how the process prevents developers or suppliers from introducing untested content directly into the production-bound package.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use the most recent urgent release to prove that the promoted artifact, configuration, database script, and approval set were identical to those tested, including any manual step.
questions.rationale_risk: A nominally segregated landscape fails when privileged users can bypass gates or when promotion reconstructs rather than moves the tested artifact.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: environment diagram, role matrix, pipeline controls, promotion logs, artifact identifiers, approvals, exception procedure, and privileged activity review. Acceptance: duties are segregated; the tested artifact is promoted without unauthorized mutation; bypass is exceptional, approved, logged, and retrospectively reviewed.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace two releases and one rejected promotion across change record, pipeline, repository, identity logs, and target-environment checksum/configuration export.
questions.primary_roles: Release Manager; DevOps Lead; System Administrator; Development Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.10(k), where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Developer production access; manual package replacement; environment-specific edits after testing; bypass has become routine; approvals occur after deployment. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Developer privilege and segregation of duties
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how development, administration, testing, release approval, and production deployment privileges are separated according to risk and how unavoidable conflicts are detected and independently reviewed.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the most privileged developer and reconstruct all repository, pipeline, vault, cloud, database, and application actions during the last release window.
questions.rationale_risk: Concentrated privileges permit a single person to alter logic, suppress evidence, approve the change, and deploy it without effective challenge.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: end-to-end entitlement model, named-user exports, privileged-access records, conflict rules, approvals, session logs, and review results. Acceptance: access is least-privilege and attributable; toxic combinations are prevented or time-bound with independent monitoring; leavers and role changes are promptly reflected.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile three named developers from HR/identity source through repository, CI/CD, cloud, database, and production; include one recent transfer or leaver.
questions.primary_roles: Development Lead; Identity and Access Manager; Platform Owner; Release Manager; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 10 and 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Shared accounts; persistent production access; no cross-platform conflict analysis; self-approval; privileged sessions not logged or reviewed.

questions.audit_question: Show how review depth and reviewer independence are determined from GxP risk and how the review establishes more than stylistic compliance for critical logic and configuration.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take a defect that escaped review and show what the reviewer examined, what evidence was recorded, why the defect was missed, and how the review method was improved.
questions.rationale_risk: A tick-box peer review may not challenge failure modes, data integrity, security, calculations, or unintended paths in high-risk software.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: review standard, risk-based review criteria, reviewer competence, annotated pull requests, static-analysis results, defect records, and closure evidence. Acceptance: critical changes receive independent, technically competent review; findings are resolved before release; rationale exists for review depth and tool reliance.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one algorithm, one security control, one audit-trail change, and one configuration-only change; compare review evidence with subsequent defects and tests.
questions.primary_roles: Development Lead; Independent Reviewer; Validation Lead; Information Security; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.5-4.7; ICH Q9(R1); NIST SP 800-218 is supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Reviewer is the author; blanket approvals; no evidence of logic review; critical static-analysis findings waived without risk assessment; repeated escaped defects.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the organization establishes provenance for each production-bound artifact, including source revision, dependency versions, build environment, compiler or interpreter, build identity, and integrity verification.
questions.follow_up_probe: Attempt a controlled rebuild of a sampled release or explain every difference between the reproduced and deployed artifact using retained, attributable evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled build environments and opaque binaries can introduce malicious, obsolete, or simply different code than the version that was reviewed and tested.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: immutable build definition, locked dependency manifest, runner identity, build log, artifact repository metadata, checksum/signature, and deployment verification. Acceptance: provenance is complete; builds are repeatable to a justified level; artifacts are protected from substitution and trace to approved source.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select the latest major release and one patch; compare repository tag, dependency lock, build-runner log, artifact signature, deployment record, and target checksum.
questions.primary_roles: DevOps Lead; Development Lead; Cybersecurity; Release Manager; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.5-4.7 and 10; NIST SP 800-218 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Mutable artifacts; unpinned dependencies; developer workstation builds; no checksum at deployment; unavailable build logs; release cannot be reproduced.

questions.audit_question: Explain how third-party libraries, containers, plugins, and embedded components are inventoried, approved, monitored for vulnerability and obsolescence, and assessed for GxP impact before inclusion in a release.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose a component with a known critical vulnerability or end-of-support date and trace detection, exploitability assessment, compensating control, validation impact, decision authority, and remediation deadline.
questions.rationale_risk: A validated application inherits defects, vulnerabilities, licensing constraints, and unsupported behavior from ungoverned dependencies.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: component inventory or SBOM, approved-source policy, scanning records, vulnerability triage, support status, risk acceptance, change and regression evidence. Acceptance: inventory matches the built artifact; critical issues are timely resolved or formally controlled; GxP and data-integrity impact are assessed.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare SBOM for two releases with artifact scan, vulnerability feed, risk register, patch change, and current deployed version.
questions.primary_roles: Development Lead; Cybersecurity; Supplier Manager; System Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 3, 4.5 and 10; NIST SP 800-218 supporting guidance; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: No component inventory; SBOM differs from binary; unsupported library ignored because system is validated; indefinite risk acceptance; vulnerability scan excludes production package.

questions.control_topic: Secure defaults and hardening in configuration
questions.audit_question: Show how insecure defaults, sample accounts, diagnostic functions, unnecessary services, and excessive permissions are identified and removed or justified in the configured solution before qualification.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare a fresh vendor installation to the approved hardened build and account for every retained default account, open port, debug function, and elevated permission.
questions.rationale_risk: Default or diagnostic features can bypass validated workflows, expose regulated data, or permit unauthorized changes without obvious application evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: hardening standard, vendor baseline, configuration delta, threat/risk assessment, scan results, exception approvals, and regression tests. Acceptance: unnecessary capability is disabled; residual exposure is justified and monitored; hardening is reproducible and included in the controlled baseline.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect one application, database, operating-system, and cloud/SaaS control layer; reconcile approved baseline with automated scan and deployed configuration.
questions.primary_roles: Platform Engineer; Application Owner; Cybersecurity; Configuration Manager; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g), where applicable; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Vendor defaults accepted without assessment; dormant admin or sample accounts; debug mode enabled; hardening exists only as an unverified checklist; exceptions lack expiry. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the audit-trail design identifies all GxP-relevant create, modify, delete, approve, invalidate, configuration, security, and administrative events and preserves the prior value, actor, time, object, and reason where required.
questions.follow_up_probe: Create a controlled record correction, privileged configuration change, and failed deletion attempt, then trace each event from user action through application, database, and centralized logs without relying on screenshots.
questions.rationale_risk: Selective logging can make material changes invisible, non-attributable, or impossible to interpret during batch review or investigation.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: audit-trail requirements, event catalogue, data model, configuration, retention design, access controls, test cases, and readable export. Acceptance: risk-relevant events are complete and time-stamped; prior data are not obscured; audit records are protected, retained, searchable, and interpretable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Map ten critical data/configuration events to requirements and code/configuration; compare generated entries to database history, application record, and security log.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Development Lead; Database Administrator; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA data-integrity guidance; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Critical event absent; overwrite without old value; editable audit table; shared actor identity; reason not captured; administrator can disable or purge logging without independent alert.

questions.audit_question: Show how the configured electronic-signature function preserves signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, record linkage, credential control, and prevention of signature reuse across every regulated signing context.
questions.follow_up_probe: Demonstrate attempted copying, post-signature record change, session reuse, and signature by an unauthorized role; explain the resulting controls and retained evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: A visual approval mark may appear compliant while being transferable, weakly authenticated, detached from content, or silent about later record change.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: signature requirements, design/configuration, role matrix, identity-proofing process, signature event/audit data, test evidence, and human-readable copy. Acceptance: signatures are unique, attributable, meaning-defined, time-stamped, permanently linked, and protected against unauthorized use or ordinary transfer.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test at least three signature meanings and two user roles; reconcile signed record, audit trail, identity source, and printed/electronic copy.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Identity Manager; Development Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200 and 11.300, where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Signature is an image or status field; meaning missing; record can change silently after signature; shared credentials; signature absent from copy; linkage depends on editable key.

questions.audit_question: Explain how critical inputs are validated at every entry path and how invalid, incomplete, out-of-sequence, duplicate, or malicious inputs are rejected or quarantined without loss of the original attempt and context.
questions.follow_up_probe: Inject a boundary value, invalid unit, duplicate transaction, late-arriving message, and unavailable downstream dependency; trace how each is handled and reconciled.
questions.rationale_risk: Validation limited to the user interface leaves APIs, imports, jobs, and direct data paths able to create plausible but incorrect regulated records.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: data dictionary, validation rules, error taxonomy, interface contract, exception queue design, test cases, logs, and reconciliation. Acceptance: rules are consistent across entry paths; failures are attributable and recoverable; no silent truncation, coercion, or record loss occurs.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select five critical fields across UI, API, import, and instrument/device input; compare specification, code/configuration, test result, and stored record/audit evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Development Lead; Integration Lead; Test Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5 and 6 and Section 4.7; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f) and 11.10(h); 21 CFR 211.68(b), as applicable.
questions.red_flags: UI-only validation; silent defaulting or truncation; exception queue lacks ownership; rejected input not logged; duplicate processing possible; direct database load bypasses controls.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how each regulated interface proves completeness, correct sequence, uniqueness, authenticity, and reconciliation from source creation through final processing, including retries and partial failures.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use one failed and retried transaction to prove that no record was lost, duplicated, reordered, or altered in value or meaning across source, middleware, target, and business record.
questions.rationale_risk: Successful transport acknowledgements can conceal semantic transformation, duplicate posting, partial commits, or records stranded between systems.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: interface specification, field mapping, control totals, identifiers, retry/idempotency design, error queue, reconciliation logic, security design, and tests. Acceptance: end-to-end status is visible; duplicates and gaps are detected; transformations preserve meaning; failed records have controlled recovery.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace three successful, two failed, one duplicate, and one late transaction across source data, middleware logs, target record, reconciliation report, and incident/change records.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Lead; Data Owner; Application Owners; Middleware Administrator; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5 and 4.8; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f) and 11.10(h), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: No business reconciliation; message success equated with record success; reused identifiers; manual replay can duplicate data; error queue can be cleared without trace.

questions.audit_question: Show how GxP calculations, rounding, unit conversion, limits, status logic, and decision rules are specified, independently reviewed, and verified against authoritative reference results.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the calculation most capable of changing a release or quality decision and independently recompute boundary, null, negative, precision, and unit-conversion cases from raw data.
questions.rationale_risk: A small logic or rounding defect can systematically misclassify product, laboratory, process, or quality records while outputs remain plausible.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved algorithm/specification, units and precision rules, code/configuration review, independent oracle, test data/results, version trace, and change impact. Acceptance: results match authoritative calculations over normal and boundary conditions; rounding and missing-data behavior are explicit; logic is traceable to approved requirements.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reperform at least ten cases using an independent method; reconcile raw input, intermediate value, stored result, report output, and audit trail.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Data Scientist or Calculation SME; Development Lead; Test Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.7 and 6; 21 CFR 11.10(a); applicable predicate-rule record requirements such as 21 CFR 211.194 for laboratory records.
questions.red_flags: Unapproved spreadsheet used as oracle; no precision/rounding rule; only happy-path tests; logic embedded in report without version control; result cannot be reconstructed from raw data.

questions.control_topic: Database schema and stored-procedure change control
questions.audit_question: Explain how database schemas, stored procedures, triggers, views, retention jobs, and direct data-fix scripts are versioned, reviewed, tested, and reconciled to the approved application release.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the last production data-fix or schema migration and prove who authored, reviewed, approved, executed, verified, and could roll it back, including before-and-after record evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Database logic can bypass application controls, alter history, suppress audit events, or change calculations while remaining outside the apparent software release.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: schema repository, migration scripts, access controls, review records, test results, backup/rollback plan, execution log, reconciliation, and audit record. Acceptance: all database logic is controlled and traceable; direct fixes are exceptional, approved, attributable, verified, and preserve original data/history.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare repository schema to two environments; trace one migration and one data-fix through ticket, script hash, privileged session, database log, and business verification.
questions.primary_roles: Database Administrator; Development Lead; Data Owner; Change Manager; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(e), 11.10(g) and 11.10(k); FDA data-integrity guidance.
questions.red_flags: Unversioned SQL; direct production fixes without before/after evidence; triggers absent from design; DBA can alter audit tables; rollback untested; schema differs from approved release.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how credentials, API tokens, encryption keys, and certificates used by the configured system are generated, stored, rotated, recovered, revoked, and prevented from entering source code, test evidence, or logs.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one compromised or expired-secret scenario through detection, revocation, replacement, dependent-service recovery, validation impact, and evidence that old credentials no longer work.
questions.rationale_risk: Exposed or unmanaged secrets permit unauthorized access, record manipulation, service interruption, or irreversible loss of encrypted regulated data.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: secret inventory, ownership, vault configuration, access logs, rotation/expiry monitoring, backup/recovery design, code scan, and incident/change records. Acceptance: secrets are not hard-coded; access is least-privilege and attributable; lifecycle and emergency rotation are tested; key recovery does not compromise control.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one service credential, database secret, signing certificate, and encryption key; compare inventory, vault, code scan, target configuration, and rotation records.
questions.primary_roles: Cybersecurity; Platform Owner; Development Lead; Key Custodian; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.30 for open systems where applicable; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Hard-coded production secret; shared vault access; certificate expiry not monitored; key recovery untested; secret visible in logs/test script; revoked credential remains usable.

questions.audit_question: Show how the design preserves trustworthy event chronology across clients, servers, databases, interfaces, cloud services, and devices when time zones, daylight-saving changes, offline operation, or clock drift occur.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reconstruct a cross-system transaction spanning a time-zone or clock-offset condition and explain which timestamp is authoritative, how drift is detected, and how sequence is preserved.
questions.rationale_risk: Inconsistent time can obscure data sequence, make audit trails misleading, misapply expiry or hold rules, and frustrate investigation of contemporaneous actions.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: time architecture, authoritative source, timezone/storage rules, sync monitoring, tolerance, event sequence identifiers, offline reconciliation design, and tests. Acceptance: chronology is unambiguous; offsets are retained or derivable; drift is alerted; correction does not overwrite historical meaning.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Correlate one record through application, database, middleware, identity, and infrastructure logs; include DST/timezone and simulated sync-loss cases. Triangulation: the auditor selects at least one routine item and one exception from the source population and reconciles them to an independent record.
questions.primary_roles: Solution Architect; Infrastructure Lead; Integration Lead; Data Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e), where applicable; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Local time stored without offset; clocks not monitored; audit and business records disagree; administrators can reset time without trace; sequence relies only on timestamp.

questions.audit_question: Explain how the configured solution makes processing failures visible, preserves diagnostic and business context, prevents silent continuation, and supports controlled recovery without altering original regulated records.
questions.follow_up_probe: Force a mid-transaction dependency failure and show the resulting user message, technical log, alert, partial-commit prevention, retry behavior, audit entry, and reconciliation path.
questions.rationale_risk: Systems may appear available while silently dropping, partially processing, or repeatedly reprocessing regulated transactions.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: exception taxonomy, transaction design, logging specification, alert mapping, retry/dead-letter controls, runbook, test evidence, and reconciliation.
