Acceptance: failures are attributable and actionable; partial states are controlled; recovery is idempotent and documented; evidence cannot be casually purged.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test application, database, interface, storage, and identity failure modes; compare user outcome, log, monitoring alert, incident ticket, and data reconciliation.
questions.primary_roles: Development Lead; Operations Lead; Integration Lead; Data Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.7, 5 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(f), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Silent exception; generic success after partial failure; logs lack record/user identifiers; uncontrolled manual replay; dead-letter queue unowned; error evidence expires before record retention.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the build identifies every component and datum required for a consistent recovery, including application, database, files, configuration, audit trails, keys, interfaces, and scheduler state.
questions.follow_up_probe: Starting from a blank recovery environment, show which versioned artifacts and dependencies recreate the tested state and how cross-component consistency is verified at the recovery point.
questions.rationale_risk: Backing up the primary database alone can restore an internally inconsistent system that loses configuration, signatures, audit history, or encryption capability.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: recovery inventory, dependency map, backup scope, consistency method, versioned deployment/configuration artifacts, key recovery, restore procedure, and development test. Acceptance: no critical component is omitted; recovery point consistency is defined; restored records remain readable, complete, and attributable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Map three critical workflows to stored components; compare architecture, backup configuration, artifact repository, key inventory, and latest restore evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Solution Architect; Backup and Recovery Lead; Database Administrator; Development Lead; Data Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Recovery inventory excludes audit trail or keys; configuration not versioned; components restored to incompatible points; procedure assumes unavailable vendor service; readability not verified.

questions.audit_question: Show how migration or conversion tooling preserves the value, context, metadata, relationships, audit history, signatures, and meaning of regulated records and produces independently verifiable reconciliation evidence.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one transformed record, one rejected record, one duplicate, one signed record, and one historical audit entry from source through staging and target, including rerun behavior.
questions.rationale_risk: A migration can reconcile row counts while changing units, precision, timestamps, relationships, signatures, or record meaning.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: mapping and transformation rules, approved scripts, source/target data profiling, control totals, hashes or field-level comparison, exception handling, rerun design, test evidence, and sign-off. Acceptance: reconciliation covers completeness and meaning; exceptions are resolved; repeat execution is controlled and idempotent; original evidence is retained.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use stratified samples across record types, ages, statuses, signatures, attachments, nulls, and boundary values; independently compare source, staging, target, and reconciliation output.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Owner; Database Administrator; Business Process Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8 and Sections 7, 9, 14 and 17 as relevant; 21 CFR 11.10(b), 11.10(c) and 11.70.
questions.red_flags: Count-only reconciliation; signed/audit records excluded; manual edits in staging; rerun duplicates data; rejected records lack disposition; original source retired before acceptance. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how automated test tools, frameworks, scripts, simulators, and test environments were assessed as adequate for their intended use and how false passes, stale scripts, and unverified test data are prevented.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one automated test that provides sole evidence for a critical requirement and independently reproduce its setup, inputs, expected result, raw output, assertion logic, and failure behavior.
questions.rationale_risk: Automation increases volume but can systematically produce credible-looking false assurance when the oracle, harness, environment, or result parser is wrong.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: intended-use assessment, tool/version control, script review, environment qualification, positive control and induced-failure checks, raw logs, result integrity controls, and maintenance process. Acceptance: tool reliance is justified; critical assertions are independently challenged; results are attributable and protected; changes trigger impact assessment.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Re-run three critical automated cases and one deliberately failing case; compare requirement, script, test data, raw log, summarized result, defect, and approval.
questions.primary_roles: Test Automation Lead; Validation Lead; Development Lead; Tool Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.7; Annex 15 Sections 1.7-1.8 and 2.4-2.9; FDA CSA February 2026 may inform risk-based assurance only for systems within its medical-device production/QMS scope.
questions.red_flags: Tool accepted because widely used; summarized result retained without raw log; script can be edited after execution; no induced-failure challenge; production-equivalent dependencies absent.

questions.audit_question: Explain how test data are designed to exercise GxP failure modes while preventing unauthorized use of live personal, patient, product, or confidential production records and preserving test reproducibility.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a test dataset derived from production and trace authorization, minimization, masking, re-identification risk, transfer, access, retention, deletion, and proof that masked values still support the intended test.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncontrolled test data can create privacy and confidentiality breaches, while over-sanitized data can miss real-world GxP defects.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: test-data strategy, source approval, classification, masking/synthetic-data method, access logs, transfer controls, retention/deletion records, and fitness assessment. Acceptance: use is authorized and minimized; masking is irreversible to unauthorized users; datasets remain traceable and fit for risk-based testing.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect three datasets across development and test environments; reconcile data catalogue, source authorization, masking output, access list, storage location, and deletion evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Test Lead; Privacy Officer; Information Security; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 7 and 12; 21 CFR 11.30 where an open system transmits regulated electronic records; NIST SP 800-53 supporting privacy/security guidance.
questions.red_flags: Production copy used by convenience; masking reversible; untracked downloads; shared test account; dataset retained indefinitely; test evidence exposes sensitive values.

questions.audit_question: Show how cloud infrastructure, platform services, network policy, identity, logging, storage, backup, and region settings are defined as controlled configuration and reconciled to the qualified deployed state.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one console change made outside infrastructure-as-code and trace how it was detected, risk-assessed, approved or reversed, tested, and incorporated into the baseline.
questions.rationale_risk: Cloud consoles and provider automation can change the effective GxP environment without an application release or visible configuration document.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: architecture, infrastructure-as-code repository, policy controls, provider configuration inventory, deployment plan/logs, drift detection, cloud audit logs, and exception records. Acceptance: critical resources and settings are versioned and reproducible; out-of-band changes are restricted and detected; provider/shared responsibilities are explicit.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare code, cloud inventory, policy scanner, audit log, CMDB, and validation baseline for production and one test environment; include a managed service.
questions.primary_roles: Cloud Platform Owner; DevOps Lead; Cybersecurity; System Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 4.3, 4.5, 10 and 12; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Console changes unrestricted; no drift alert; region/service differs from approved design; provider responsibility assumed but undocumented; cloud logs disabled or short-retained.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how low-code workflows, rules, forms, reports, dashboards, templates, and other administrator-configurable objects are treated as controlled software when they influence GxP records or decisions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one object changed through an administrator interface rather than the code repository and trace specification, version history, approval, test, promotion, rollback, and current production state.
questions.rationale_risk: Organizations often validate the platform but omit high-impact configurable objects that can change workflow, calculations, visibility, or record meaning.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: object inventory and criticality, configuration specification, native history/export, change workflow, independent review, tests, migration/promotion evidence, and baseline comparison. Acceptance: GxP objects are identifiable, versioned, traceable, tested, and protected from direct uncontrolled production editing.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample a workflow, calculation rule, report, notification, and template; compare native history, change ticket, exported definition, test result, and live version.
questions.primary_roles: Application Administrator; Business Process Owner; Configuration Manager; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.6, 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(g) and 11.10(k), where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Platform validation cited as sufficient; native objects lack inventory; production editing enabled; history can be overwritten; report or rule changed without regression assessment. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Walk me through how the IQ protocol scope was derived from the approved architecture, system description, risk assessment, supplier documentation, and prerequisite qualification status rather than from a generic installation template.
questions.follow_up_probe: Identify one prerequisite that was incomplete when IQ began and show the documented impact, conditional controls, authorization, subsequent verification, and effect on OQ release.
questions.rationale_risk: A protocol can pass while omitting a component, dependency, or prerequisite essential to the validated system.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved IQ protocol, scope rationale, architecture and system description, component inventory, risk assessment, prerequisite checklist, supplier instructions, approvals, and deviations. Acceptance: scope covers all GxP-relevant installed elements and dependencies; exclusions are risk-justified; prerequisites are objectively met before dependent testing.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile the IQ scope to architecture, bill of materials, CMDB/cloud inventory, and installed discovery for one application and its supporting stack.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Infrastructure Lead; Application Owner; Supplier; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 1.1-1.8, 2.4-2.10 and 3.8-3.9; EU GMP Annex 11 Principle and Section 4.3.
questions.red_flags: Template copied without system-specific rationale; unknown prerequisite status; missing cloud or middleware layer; IQ starts before approved design; exclusion has no risk assessment.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the as-installed inventory identifies each GxP-relevant hardware, virtual resource, operating system, database, middleware, application, agent, library, interface component, and managed service with version and ownership.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare automated discovery to the approved inventory and account for every unrecognized package, service, container, plugin, or provider-managed component on a sampled node or tenant.
questions.rationale_risk: Unrecorded components evade qualification, vulnerability management, backup, monitoring, change control, and periodic review.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: bill of materials, discovery output, CMDB/cloud inventory, version and support data, owner assignment, supplier documentation, and reconciliation. Acceptance: inventory is complete, uniquely identifies versions and dependencies, matches the installed state, and records justified provider-managed exceptions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Independently discover one server/cluster or SaaS tenant and reconcile to IQ, CMDB, architecture, licenses, vulnerability inventory, and monitoring scope.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Lead; Configuration Manager; Application Owner; Cybersecurity; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.8-3.9; EU GMP Annex 11 Principle and Sections 4.3 and 11.
questions.red_flags: Inventory is a manually typed list; version or owner missing; discovery reveals unknown agents; managed services omitted; support status not recorded.

questions.audit_question: Show how the installed physical and logical architecture, data flows, interfaces, prerequisites, and security boundaries were verified against the approved design and how every variance was dispositioned.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one as-built variance that was accepted and demonstrate its GMP, data-integrity, cybersecurity, capacity, recovery, and validation impact assessment.
questions.rationale_risk: Small as-built differences can invalidate threat models, interface assumptions, recovery design, or test coverage.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved and as-built diagrams, configuration exports, network routes, data-flow inventory, variance log, risk assessments, change records, and QA approval. Acceptance: installed topology is accurate and complete; variances are detected, justified, approved, and reflected in downstream testing and documentation.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Physically or technically trace one critical data flow across endpoint, network, middleware, database, and storage; compare logs and configuration to the diagram.
questions.primary_roles: Solution Architect; Infrastructure Lead; Integration Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.3; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.8-3.9 and 2.7-2.10.
questions.red_flags: Design and as-built diagrams identical without field verification; undocumented route or interface; variance closed as editorial; diagrams lack trust boundaries or data stores. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Explain how each installed environment is uniquely identified and segregated so that users, integrations, credentials, jobs, data, and deployment paths cannot be confused across development, test, qualification, training, and production.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace a non-production interface and credential to prove it cannot route to or act upon production; then show how environment cloning prevents production secrets and personal data from propagating.
questions.rationale_risk: Misrouted interfaces or shared credentials can corrupt production records or invalidate qualification evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: environment architecture, naming, network and identity segregation, endpoint inventories, secrets configuration, banners, data-cloning procedure, and connectivity tests. Acceptance: boundaries are technically enforced; endpoints and credentials are environment-specific; production data use is controlled; environment identity is obvious and logged.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect one user, service account, endpoint, scheduler, and database connection in each environment; reconcile configuration with network and identity logs.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Lead; Identity Manager; Integration Lead; Application Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Shared service credentials; test endpoint points to production; cloned production secrets; only naming convention provides segregation; users cannot identify environment.

questions.control_topic: Operating system, database, and middleware baselines
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how operating-system, database, middleware, runtime, and platform installations were verified against approved versions, options, patches, locale, services, and support prerequisites.
questions.follow_up_probe: For one layer, generate a fresh configuration and package export and reconcile every deviation from the approved baseline, including provider or vendor hotfixes.
questions.rationale_risk: Unsupported or differently configured platform layers can change application behavior, security, calculation, time, or data persistence.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved baseline, vendor compatibility matrix, installation output, package/version export, patch record, support statement, and variance assessment. Acceptance: installed versions and options are supported and approved; discrepancies are risk-assessed; evidence is reproducible and attributable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample application host, database, middleware, and client/runtime; compare discovery output, IQ result, vendor matrix, CMDB, and vulnerability records.
questions.primary_roles: Platform Engineers; Database Administrator; Application Owner; Supplier; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.8-3.9; EU GMP Annex 11 Principle and Section 4.3.
questions.red_flags: Unsupported version; baseline omits options or locale; evidence is screenshot only; patch applied after IQ without impact assessment; vendor compatibility unverified. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how the virtual-machine, hypervisor, cluster, container image, orchestration, and persistent-storage foundation supporting the application was qualified and tied to the application IQ boundary.
questions.follow_up_probe: Move or recreate a sampled workload on another permitted node and demonstrate that the qualified controls, time, storage, network, logging, and identity behavior remain equivalent.
questions.rationale_risk: Qualification limited to the guest application can overlook dynamic infrastructure that changes placement, image, network, or storage behavior.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: infrastructure qualification, approved images, cluster/node inventory, orchestration configuration, storage classes, placement rules, logs, and application dependency mapping. Acceptance: shared foundation is qualified for intended use; workload mobility does not bypass controls; image and persistent data versions are traceable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace one workload from declared configuration to image registry, running instance, node, network, storage, monitoring, and backup scope.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Platform Owner; Container/Virtualization Engineer; Application Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Principle and Sections 3, 4.3 and 4.5; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.8-3.9.
questions.red_flags: Shared platform declared out of scope; mutable latest-tag images; node movement unassessed; persistent storage not mapped; provider evidence accepted without regulated-user review.

questions.control_topic: Network routes, ports, and trust boundaries
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how installed network routes, ports, protocols, firewall rules, proxies, remote-access paths, and trust boundaries were verified against the minimum approved connectivity design.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select an apparently unused open port or broad rule discovered during verification and trace ownership, need, risk, approval, monitoring, and closure or compensating control.
questions.rationale_risk: Excess connectivity permits unauthorized access, data exfiltration, lateral movement, or bypass of application controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: network/data-flow diagram, approved rule set, rule owners, technical scan, connection tests, remote-access controls, and exception records. Acceptance: only justified routes and protocols exist; rules are specific and attributable; unapproved paths are removed; installed state matches design.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Scan one application segment and one remote/provider path; reconcile observed connections to firewall, cloud security group, application configuration, and logs.
questions.primary_roles: Network Security; Infrastructure Lead; Application Owner; Supplier; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3 and 12; 21 CFR 11.30 where open-system controls apply; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Any-any rules; temporary access never removed; design omits supplier path; scan conflicts with rule inventory; insecure protocol retained without formal control.

questions.audit_question: Show how authentication integration with the identity provider was installed and verified, including tenant or domain, protocol, claims, groups, fail-safe behavior, certificate trust, and prevention of unintended local-account fallback.
questions.follow_up_probe: Interrupt or misconfigure the identity-provider connection in a controlled environment and demonstrate what access remains, which accounts can bypass it, how the event is logged, and how recovery is controlled.
questions.rationale_risk: An application may appear federated while undocumented local accounts or fail-open behavior bypass centralized identity controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: identity architecture, federation configuration export, trust/certificate details, claim/group mapping, local-account inventory, failover design, connection tests, and logs. Acceptance: correct identity source and mappings are installed; bypass accounts are minimized and controlled; failure does not grant unintended access.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile three roles and one emergency account across identity provider, application configuration, account inventory, and authentication logs.
questions.primary_roles: Identity Architect; Application Administrator; Cybersecurity; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Uncontrolled local admins; fail-open authentication; claims mapped differently from design; expired trust certificate; shared break-glass credential.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how every installed service, integration, database, scheduler, and automation account is uniquely inventoried, owned, least-privileged, non-interactive where appropriate, and linked to a controlled secret.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose one high-privilege service account and trace its creation approval, target entitlements, secret storage, use in logs, rotation, dependency impact, and emergency revocation test.
questions.rationale_risk: Orphaned or shared technical identities provide durable, poorly monitored paths to alter regulated data or configuration.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: account inventory, owner, purpose, privilege mapping, identity-source record, vault reference, application configuration, authentication logs, and rotation/revocation procedure. Acceptance: accounts are attributable to accountable owners, privileges are justified, interactive use is prevented or controlled, and secrets are not embedded.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample accounts across application, database, interface, scheduler, backup, and monitoring; reconcile inventory to identity and target-system exports.
questions.primary_roles: Identity Manager; Application Owner; Database Administrator; Integration Lead; Cybersecurity
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Owner is generic IT; shared account; password in script; interactive login allowed without monitoring; privilege exceeds function; account absent from inventory.

questions.audit_question: Show how authoritative time synchronization, timezone, daylight-saving behavior, and drift monitoring were installed and verified across every system layer that creates or orders regulated events.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare simultaneous timestamps from application, database, operating system, middleware, identity provider, and a connected device; explain every offset and its effect on record sequence.
questions.rationale_risk: Unsynchronized layers make audit trails and business records non-contemporaneous or impossible to correlate.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: time architecture, source hierarchy, system settings, sync status, tolerance/alert thresholds, timezone rules, and IQ results. Acceptance: all critical components use approved sources and settings; drift is within justified tolerance; failures are alerted; offsets remain interpretable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Capture and compare current time and historical logs across at least five layers; include one isolated or intermittently connected component.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Lead; Application Owner; Integration Lead; Data Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e), where applicable; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Local clocks manually set; timezone not documented; drift monitoring absent; device time differs materially; administrators can change time without trace.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how installed certificates, trust stores, encryption settings, and keys match the approved security design and remain recoverable, monitorable, and attributable throughout their lifecycle.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one certificate from request and identity validation through installation, private-key protection, dependent endpoints, expiry alert, renewal, revocation, and recovery documentation.
questions.rationale_risk: Incorrect trust or key installation can expose data, interrupt service, invalidate signatures, or make retained records unreadable.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: certificate/key inventory, purpose and owner, approved algorithms/settings, installation export, vault/HSM controls, expiry monitoring, recovery procedure, and verification tests. Acceptance: identity and trust are correct; weak protocols are disabled; private keys are protected; renewal and recovery are controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect external, internal, database, interface, and signing certificates/keys; reconcile inventory to endpoint scans, vault, and monitoring.
questions.primary_roles: PKI/Key Custodian; Cybersecurity; Infrastructure Lead; Application Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7 and 12; 21 CFR 11.30 where open-system safeguards apply; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Expired or self-signed certificate without rationale; private key exported casually; inventory incomplete; recovery not tested; deprecated protocol enabled.

questions.audit_question: Show how database and storage installations were verified for location, capacity, redundancy, integrity protection, access, encryption, transaction/log settings, retention, and separation of regulated records from transient data.
questions.follow_up_probe: Map one critical record and its audit trail, attachment, index, and backup from logical schema to physical storage and demonstrate that no unprotected alternate copy is created.
questions.rationale_risk: Unqualified storage settings can lose, corrupt, expose, or prematurely purge regulated data despite correct application behavior.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: storage/database design, installation/configuration exports, access lists, encryption settings, capacity alerts, transaction/log configuration, retention jobs, redundancy checks, and IQ results. Acceptance: settings meet approved criteria; critical data locations are known and protected; capacity and integrity controls are active.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace primary data, audit data, attachments, logs, replicas, and temporary exports; compare design, actual configuration, access, monitoring, and backup scope.
questions.primary_roles: Database Administrator; Storage Engineer; Data Owner; Cybersecurity; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, 12 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(e), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Audit data on unprotected volume; retention job enabled without validation; encryption assumed from provider; capacity alerts absent; temporary exports uncontrolled.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how every required application, database, file, configuration, audit-trail, key, and scheduler component was enrolled in backup with the approved frequency, retention, protection, and monitoring.
questions.follow_up_probe: Starting from the recovery inventory, identify any component not visible in the backup console and prove how it is otherwise protected and recoverable at a consistent point.
questions.rationale_risk: A green backup dashboard can omit newly installed assets or essential non-database components.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: recovery inventory, backup configuration export, agent health, job schedule, retention policy, repository protection, alerts, and IQ checks. Acceptance: scope reconciles completely; successful status is monitored; failures escalate; backup access and immutability/offline controls match risk.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile architecture/CMDB to backup-console objects and recent job logs; include one new asset, one managed service, and one configuration repository.
questions.primary_roles: Backup Administrator; Application Owner; Database Administrator; Recovery Lead; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2 and Section 16; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Asset missing from console; backup scope inferred rather than reconciled; audit/configuration data excluded; failures notify an unowned mailbox; repository deletable by production admins.

questions.audit_question: Show how health monitoring, application and security logging, alerting, endpoint protection, integrity monitoring, and log forwarding were installed on every in-scope component and verified as active.
questions.follow_up_probe: Disable or isolate one agent in a controlled environment and demonstrate the health alert, ownership, incident creation, evidence retention, and restoration path.
questions.rationale_risk: Missing or unhealthy agents create blind spots that can persist until a batch, laboratory, or inspection problem exposes them.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: coverage inventory, installation/configuration exports, agent health dashboard, log-source list, alert routing, retention settings, and induced-failure test. Acceptance: all critical components report health and required logs; coverage gaps are detected; alerts reach accountable support; logs are protected and time-aligned.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare CMDB/architecture to monitoring, EDR, vulnerability, and log-management consoles; include a recently added or rebuilt component.
questions.primary_roles: Operations Monitoring; Cybersecurity; Infrastructure Lead; Application Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 11, 12 and 13; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Coverage dashboard not reconciled to inventory; agent unhealthy but green overall; critical logs local only; alert goes to no owner; retention shorter than investigation need.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that required audit trails and administrative logs were enabled before regulated configuration or data creation and that their storage, access, time source, and retention settings match the approved design.
questions.follow_up_probe: Identify the earliest configuration and user-management events after installation and prove they were captured; explain any activity predating audit-trail enablement.
questions.rationale_risk: A system may begin accumulating untraceable configuration or data before logging is activated.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: installation sequence, audit configuration export, first-event records, log storage/access, retention, time settings, and IQ verification. Acceptance: audit capability precedes GxP activity; required event categories are enabled; administrators cannot silently disable or purge it.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review earliest application, database, identity, and infrastructure audit events; reconcile installation timestamps, configuration changes, and first user/data records.
questions.primary_roles: Application Administrator; Database Administrator; Data Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e), where applicable; FDA data-integrity guidance.
questions.red_flags: Audit trail enabled after configuration; first-event gap; admin can toggle without alert; retention default not assessed; audit storage shared with editable business tables.

questions.audit_question: Show how identity, authentication, time, certificate, and record-linking dependencies required for electronic signatures were installed and verified before functional signature testing.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace a signed-record identifier through database keys, signature service, identity source, time source, and printable copy to prove the installed dependencies cannot detach or misattribute the signature.
questions.rationale_risk: Functional signature tests can pass while underlying identity, time, or linkage services are incorrectly installed.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: signature architecture, dependency inventory, identity/certificate/time configuration, database constraints, installation checks, and prerequisite approval. Acceptance: dependencies are uniquely identified and trusted; signature links persist; unauthorized local substitutes are absent; prerequisite status is approved.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect each installed dependency for one signature flow and compare configuration, trust, identity, timestamps, schema, and human-readable output.
questions.primary_roles: Identity Manager; Application Administrator; Database Administrator; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200 and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Signature service or trust not inventoried; local identity bypass; record linkage is editable; time source differs; certificate ownership/expiry unknown.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that every approved interface endpoint, queue, topic, connector, schema, route, certificate, service account, and error store was installed in the correct environment and version.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select an inactive or future interface and prove it cannot accept or transmit production records before authorization, while its configuration remains controlled and distinguishable.
questions.rationale_risk: Wrong endpoints, schemas, or credentials can silently route regulated records to the wrong system or environment.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: interface inventory, approved endpoint/schema specifications, middleware export, certificate/account references, route tests, environment markers, and variance log. Acceptance: installed objects match approved versions and destinations; dormant routes are disabled; ownership and error locations are defined.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile all critical interfaces to middleware configuration; trace two endpoints through DNS/network, certificate, service account, schema, and target connection.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Lead; Middleware Administrator; Application Owners; Cybersecurity; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3 and 5; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.8-3.9.
questions.red_flags: Endpoint maintained only in email; dormant route enabled; schema version unknown; test credential in production; error store excluded from backup/access control. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Cloud tenant, region, and managed-service verification
questions.audit_question: Show how the regulated user verified the correct cloud tenant, account, subscription, region, availability model, managed services, data locations, logging, backup features, and shared responsibilities for the qualified instance.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare supplier assertions to direct tenant evidence for one critical managed service and explain what the regulated user can verify, what remains supplier-controlled, and how residual risk is governed.
questions.rationale_risk: SaaS branding can conceal materially different tenants, regions, provider services, retention, or controls from those assessed and approved.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: subscription/order, tenant and region identifiers, service inventory, supplier agreement, shared-responsibility matrix, provider attestations, tenant configuration export, and regulated-user review. Acceptance: instance identity and location are unambiguous; services match assessment; responsibilities and evidence access are defined.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Verify tenant ID, region, service/version, encryption/logging, backup/retention, and administrator list through independent console/API evidence and contract records.
questions.primary_roles: Cloud/SaaS Service Owner; Supplier Manager; System Owner; Cybersecurity; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 4.3 and 4.5; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.6 and 3.8-3.9.
questions.red_flags: Tenant/region unknown; provider statement accepted without instance evidence; managed service omitted from assessment; data location conflicts with agreement; admin list unreconciled.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the qualified SaaS version, feature set, tenant configuration, enabled modules, extensions, and provider release channel were identified at IQ and protected from unnoticed change before OQ.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show one provider change that occurred between IQ execution and OQ approval and trace notification, impact assessment, baseline update, retest, and QA decision.
questions.rationale_risk: Continuously delivered services may change the tested object while qualification is still in progress.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: tenant version/build, feature/configuration export, module inventory, release-channel setting, provider notices, change freeze or monitoring, impact assessments, and updated tests. Acceptance: qualified object is uniquely identifiable; provider changes are detected and assessed; evidence remains contemporaneous.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare IQ timestamp/version to provider release history, tenant audit log, configuration export, OQ start state, and change records.
questions.primary_roles: SaaS Service Owner; Supplier Manager; Configuration Manager; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 4.1, 4.5, 10 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(k), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Version shown only in screenshot; provider changes not monitored; configuration export absent; automatic feature enablement uncontrolled; IQ and OQ tested different builds.

questions.audit_question: Show how connected instruments, controllers, terminals, scanners, printers, sensors, or other devices were uniquely identified, correctly installed, calibrated or qualified where required, and mapped to the computerized system.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one replaceable device and prove how identity, firmware, driver, calibration status, data path, time, and device-check behavior prevent an unapproved substitute from producing accepted data.
questions.rationale_risk: The application may be validated while an unqualified or misidentified device introduces erroneous source data or output.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: device inventory, serial/asset/firmware data, installation record, approved driver, calibration/qualification status, connection mapping, maintenance instructions, and device-check tests. Acceptance: devices match approved specifications; status is current; replacements are controlled; source identity and data path are verifiable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Physically reconcile two devices to inventory, calibration system, driver/configuration, system logs, and sample electronic records.
questions.primary_roles: Equipment Owner; Engineering; Metrology; Application Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.8-3.9; EU GMP Annex 11 Principle, Sections 4.3 and 6; 21 CFR 11.10(h), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Serial/firmware absent; calibration expired; generic driver substituted; device identity not recorded in data; replacement bypasses change control.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how current supplier operating instructions, maintenance requirements, compatibility information, installation records, and licenses were collected, reviewed for suitability, controlled, and handed to accountable owners.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose one vendor prerequisite or maintenance instruction not adopted verbatim and show the technical and GMP rationale, risk assessment, approval, and alternative control.
questions.rationale_risk: Missing or unreviewed supplier information leads to incorrect operation, unsupported maintenance, or inability to sustain the installed state.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: controlled manual inventory, version/effective date, regulated-user review, compatibility and maintenance requirements, license/support records, deviations, and owner handover. Acceptance: required documents are current, accessible, assessed, and linked to procedures/maintenance plans; departures are justified.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five critical components; compare installed version, supplier manual, maintenance plan, SOP, training material, and support entitlement.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Manager; Application Owner; Maintenance/Operations Lead; Document Control; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Section 3.9(iii); EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3.3-3.4 and 4.5; EU GMP Chapter 4.
questions.red_flags: Manual version unknown; documents stored only with departed contractor; support entitlement lapsed; vendor requirement ignored without rationale; SOP conflicts with manual.

questions.audit_question: Show how supplier installation scripts, checklists, certificates, and executed records were reviewed and independently confirmed by the regulated user before being accepted as IQ evidence.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one supplier check marked pass and reproduce the verification from raw system evidence; explain any difference between supplier result and current installation.
questions.rationale_risk: Supplier evidence can be generic, self-certified, or generated from a different build and does not transfer accountability from the regulated user.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: supplier protocol/version, executed raw records, script hashes, tester identities, deviations, regulated-user review, supplemental tests, and approval. Acceptance: evidence is system- and version-specific, attributable, complete, reviewed for suitability, and independently challenged for critical items.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reperform a stratified sample of supplier checks across versions, services, accounts, database, and interfaces; reconcile to protocol and system output.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Engineer; Validation Lead; System Owner; Infrastructure Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Section 2.6; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3 and 4.5-4.7.
questions.red_flags: Certificate without raw evidence; tester identity absent; script version differs; supplier result accepted without review; critical check not reproducible.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the installed hardening baseline is effective across application, operating system, database, middleware, cloud, and device layers and that every privileged access path is known and controlled.
questions.follow_up_probe: Run a configuration or vulnerability assessment against the installed instance and trace one exception through design need, exploitability, compensating control, validation impact, approval, and expiry.
questions.rationale_risk: A nominally correct installation can retain default accounts, weak services, broad privileges, or hidden support paths.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved hardening baseline, technical scan, privileged-path inventory, remote-support configuration, exceptions, monitoring, and IQ results. Acceptance: baseline is objectively verified; exceptions are specific and time-bound; privileged paths are least-privilege, attributable, and monitored.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect each technology layer and one supplier path; compare baseline, scan, account/rule export, vault/PAM, and access logs.
questions.primary_roles: Cybersecurity; Platform Engineers; Application Owner; Supplier; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable; NIST SP 800-53 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Checklist without technical scan; default/admin support account; broad remote access; exception has no expiry; hardening differs by node; critical finding deferred to operations.

questions.audit_question: Explain how IQ deviations, unexpected results, missing prerequisites, and as-built discrepancies were investigated for root cause and cumulative impact rather than closed individually as documentation issues.
questions.follow_up_probe: Group all IQ deviations by common component or control and demonstrate that aggregate risk, repeat failure, data-integrity impact, and need for protocol expansion were evaluated.
questions.rationale_risk: Many minor deviations can reveal a systemic installation or supplier-quality problem and undermine the suitability of proceeding to OQ.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: deviation log, investigations, impact/risk assessments, corrections, retests, trend review, protocol amendments, and QA decisions. Acceptance: each deviation is attributable and resolved or formally controlled; cumulative impact is assessed; retest is independent where appropriate; no unexplained result is overwritten.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all critical/high and a sample of minor deviations; compare raw test evidence, incident/change records, current configuration, and OQ prerequisites.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Technical SMEs; Supplier; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.7-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2 and 13; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Expected result changed after failure; deviation classified minor without rationale; repeated issue not trended; retest replaces original evidence; open prerequisite carried forward invisibly.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how responsible personnel concluded that the installed system and infrastructure were suitable to enter OQ, including treatment of open items, baseline lock, document approval, and confirmation that the object to be tested is unchanged.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select every open item at IQ approval and show the explicit impact on OQ, compensating controls, owner, due date, acceptance authority, and evidence of eventual closure.
questions.rationale_risk: A schedule-driven stage gate can move an unstable or incompletely installed system into testing and make later evidence uninterpretable.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: IQ report, acceptance-criteria summary, deviation/open-item register, risk assessment, baseline/version record, prerequisite checklist, formal authorization, and change log between IQ and OQ. Acceptance: results are summarized against criteria; unresolved items have no significant unaddressed impact; release is authorized; tested object remains identifiable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile IQ report totals to raw protocols/deviations, open-action tracker, configuration baseline, and first OQ execution timestamp/version.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; System Owner; Business Process Owner; Technical Owners; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.9-2.10 and 3.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2.
questions.red_flags: Approval predates final evidence; open items lack impact assessment; baseline changed before OQ without control; report totals do not reconcile; stage gate signed by unauthorized role.

questions.audit_question: Show how the OQ strategy converts documented GxP and data-integrity risks into test coverage for functions, limits, error handling, security, records, interfaces, and recovery without allowing low-risk labels to hide critical control interactions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose the highest residual risk and trace it to specific challenge tests, raw results, deviations, and final residual-risk acceptance; then identify which plausible failure mode was intentionally not tested and why.
questions.rationale_risk: A requirements-only protocol can verify intended functions while missing the failure modes that actually threaten patient safety, product quality, and data integrity.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved risk assessment, OQ plan, coverage matrix, test-design rationale, acceptance criteria, protocols/results, and residual-risk review. Acceptance: critical risks have direct positive and adverse challenge coverage; exclusions are justified; results are attributable and traceable; residual risk is approved by accountable roles.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select five critical risks across data, security, interfaces, calculations, and recovery; compare risk controls, OQ cases, defects, and final assessment.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Risk Owner; Test Lead; Business Process Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.1 and 4.7; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 1.7-1.8, 2.4 and 3.10-3.12; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Risk assessment written after tests; high-risk control covered only by happy path; excluded failure mode lacks rationale; residual risk accepted by project team without process/quality owner.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how tester competence, independence, environment access, and data preparation were controlled so OQ results provide an objective challenge rather than confirmation by the people who configured the function.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a critical test executed by a configurer or supplier and show the independence rationale, witnessed evidence, permission limits, raw output, and independent review that mitigated self-verification risk.
questions.rationale_risk: Testing by the implementer can normalize unexpected behavior, manipulate setup, or overlook defects familiar to the design team.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: tester qualification/training, role assignments, access records, independence assessment, protocol execution metadata, witness/reviewer evidence, and audit trail. Acceptance: testers are competent; conflicts are identified and controlled; results and test data are attributable; reviewers independently challenge anomalies.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample three testers and five critical cases; reconcile training, project role, environment entitlements, execution identity, timestamps, and review comments.
questions.primary_roles: Test Lead; Validation Lead; Training Coordinator; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 1.2-1.3 and 2.2; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2 and 4.7; 21 CFR 11.10(i), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Configurer self-tests without mitigation; generic training evidence; shared test account; reviewer signs without comments despite anomalies; tester has production privilege.

questions.audit_question: Walk me through how OQ proves that each critical functional control operates as specified, remains traceable to an approved requirement, and cannot be bypassed through alternate screens, APIs, imports, jobs, or administrator functions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one critical control and attempt the same prohibited action through every available entry path and privileged interface; reconcile the outcome and logs.
questions.rationale_risk: A function may work on the primary user path while alternate channels bypass the validated control.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: requirements/design, entry-path inventory, OQ cases/results, role setup, API/import/job tests, audit records, and defect closure. Acceptance: control is effective across all applicable paths; bypass attempts fail and are recorded; evidence identifies tested version and configuration.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select five critical controls and test UI, API, import, scheduled, and administrative paths as applicable; compare record and audit outcome.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Test Lead; Integration Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.4 and 4.7; EU GMP Annex 15 Section 3.11; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f) and 11.10(g), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Only UI tested; administrator path omitted; requirement marked pass by demonstration; alternative import bypasses validation; test version/configuration not recorded.

questions.audit_question: Show how upper and lower operating limits and credible worst-case combinations were derived from process knowledge and challenged in OQ, including behavior just inside and outside each accepted boundary.
questions.follow_up_probe: For the limit with greatest product or data impact, independently repeat below-limit, exact-limit, above-limit, and interacting-condition cases and explain any boundary asymmetry.
questions.rationale_risk: Nominal testing can miss off-by-one, precision, capacity, timeout, and combination failures that emerge only at operating extremes.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: limit rationale, risk assessment, configuration/specification, boundary/worst-case test data, raw results, alarms/rejections, and acceptance criteria. Acceptance: limits are scientifically or technically justified; both sides of boundaries are challenged; failure behavior is safe, visible, and recorded.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample limits for value, volume, timing, users, file size, and one interacting condition; compare configuration, raw data, output, and logs.
questions.primary_roles: Process SME; Test Lead; Performance Engineer; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.7; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.11 and 3.14; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Limits copied from screen labels; no outside-boundary tests; worst case means largest value only; interacting conditions ignored; unsafe failure accepted as user training issue.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how OQ challenges invalid data, missing prerequisites, unavailable dependencies, interrupted transactions, unauthorized sequence, and partial failure while proving no silent loss, corruption, or uncontrolled continuation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Interrupt a critical transaction after the first committed step and show rollback or controlled partial state, retained evidence, user/operations alert, reconciliation, and safe recovery.
questions.rationale_risk: The most consequential defects often occur when the system cannot complete the happy path and recovery logic is invoked.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: failure-mode analysis, negative cases, induced-failure setup, raw logs, alerts, transaction state, reconciliation, retry/recovery results, and deviations. Acceptance: failures are visible and attributable; original data remain protected; recovery is controlled and does not duplicate or obscure records.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Challenge application, database, interface, network, storage, identity, and scheduler failures; compare user result, technical logs, monitoring, and stored data.
questions.primary_roles: Test Lead; Development Lead; Operations Lead; Data Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.7, 5 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(f), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Negative cases simulated only on paper; success shown despite partial failure; error message without retained technical context; manual recovery untested; retry duplicates data.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ proves complete and accurate audit-trail capture for risk-relevant creation, modification, deletion, approval, invalidation, configuration, security, and administrative events.
questions.follow_up_probe: Execute one allowed and one denied action for each of three roles, then reconcile old/new value, actor, time, object, reason, event sequence, and underlying data without screenshots.
questions.rationale_risk: An enabled audit trail may omit event classes, record misleading identities, or lose prior values and reasons.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: event catalogue, risk mapping, OQ cases, raw audit export, source records, role setup, retention/protection checks, and review. Acceptance: required events and metadata are complete, secure, time-aligned, understandable, and retained; denied attempts are visible where risk requires.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test at least ten event types across business and admin functions; compare audit trail with source record, database or system log, and tester identity.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Test Lead; Application Administrator; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA data-integrity guidance; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Old value missing; shared/admin identity shown; critical event absent; reason editable later; denied attempts invisible; audit export differs from screen.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that authorized reviewers can retrieve, filter, sequence, interpret, annotate, and retain complete audit-trail evidence for a defined review period without relying on privileged database support.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reconstruct a complex record history containing corrections, failed actions, role changes, and configuration events using the review tool and compare it to the raw source.
questions.rationale_risk: Technically captured audit data do not support effective review if entries are incomplete, unreadable, unsortable, or detached from business context.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: review requirements, role configuration, audit review screen/export, completeness reconciliation, performance results, annotations/sign-off, and SOP draft. Acceptance: reviewers see all relevant events and context; filters do not omit data; exports are accurate; review evidence is retained and attributable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use three records with known histories; compare reviewer output to raw audit store, business record, user list, and configuration change log.
questions.primary_roles: Business Reviewer; Data Owner; Application Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 9; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(e); FDA data-integrity guidance.
questions.red_flags: Review needs DBA query; filters silently cap results; export drops reasons or old values; reviewer cannot link event to record; review evidence not retained.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ challenges the permitted and prohibited actions of each GxP role, including cross-role conflicts, privileged functions, inherited access, and direct data or configuration paths.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose the least obvious toxic combination and demonstrate whether one user can create, modify, approve, release, delete, and conceal the same regulated record across application and supporting layers.
questions.rationale_risk: Testing only positive role permissions misses excess privileges and cross-layer bypasses that defeat segregation of duties.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved role design, SoD rules, user/role test matrix, positive and negative results, direct-access tests, privileged logs, and exceptions. Acceptance: authority checks consistently enforce intended duties; prohibited combinations are prevented or independently controlled; results match configured entitlements.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test representative end user, reviewer, administrator, service, and emergency roles; reconcile application, database, identity-provider, and PAM evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Identity Manager; Test Lead; Application/Database Administrators; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Positive-only permission tests; database/file bypass omitted; inherited role unknown; administrator can alter records without audit; toxic combination accepted without monitoring. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how provisioning, modification, suspension, transfer, termination, recertification, and emergency-access workflows operate across all integrated identity and application layers.
questions.follow_up_probe: Execute a transfer that removes one role and grants another, then prove old sessions, cached entitlements, tokens, database access, and downstream permissions are revoked within the approved control point.
questions.rationale_risk: A workflow may close successfully while access persists in cached sessions, local stores, or downstream systems.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: lifecycle requirements, workflow configuration, test identities, approvals, timestamps, target-system exports, session/token evidence, alerts, and audit logs. Acceptance: changes are authorized, complete, timely, and traceable across all layers; rejected/failed requests do not leave partial access.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test joiner, mover, leaver, suspension, emergency, and failed-provisioning cases; reconcile identity source, workflow, targets, and logs.
questions.primary_roles: Identity Manager; Business Role Owner; Application Owner; Test Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 12.3; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Ticket closes before target confirmation; cached session survives termination; local account omitted; partial provisioning not alerted; self-approval possible.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ challenges authentication, failed attempts, lockout, timeout, re-authentication, concurrent sessions, token revocation, password or MFA controls, and emergency access according to risk.
questions.follow_up_probe: Test a privileged session across timeout, network interruption, password reset, account disablement, and token theft simulation; show when authority is actually withdrawn.
questions.rationale_risk: Configured values may look compliant while persistent sessions or tokens continue to authorize regulated actions.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: security requirements, configuration, identity-provider settings, OQ cases/results, authentication/session logs, and exception rationale. Acceptance: safeguards operate consistently; unauthorized attempts are blocked and alerted; revoked identity cannot continue regulated action; timeouts match risk.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test standard, privileged, service, remote, and break-glass access; compare application, identity-provider, gateway, and security logs.
questions.primary_roles: Identity and Access Manager; Cybersecurity; Application Owner; Test Lead; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1-12.3; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), 11.200 and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Token remains valid after disablement; lockout not monitored; privileged session never times out; break-glass access unlogged; security test excludes federated path.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate through adverse testing that electronic signatures remain unique, authenticated, meaning-specific, time-stamped, permanently linked, and non-transferable when records are copied, changed, exported, restored, or viewed later.
questions.follow_up_probe: Attempt signature reuse, copying, post-signature modification, signing under a different meaning, and signature with a disabled credential; reconcile all outcomes and audit events.
questions.rationale_risk: A signature can appear correctly on screen while failing record linkage, credential, meaning, or long-term-copy requirements.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: signature requirements, role/identity setup, adverse tests, signed record, audit trail, copy/export, restore result, and credential logs. Acceptance: unauthorized signatures fail; all required manifestations remain with the record; later change is visible; linkage survives export/restore.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test three signature meanings, two record types, two roles, and one restored/exported record; compare application, identity, audit, and human-readable evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Identity Manager; Test Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.red_flags: Signature reusable; meaning absent from copy; record editable without signature invalidation/history; restored signature detached; disabled account can sign.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ proves that human-readable and electronic copies are accurate, complete, intelligible, and suitable for inspection, including metadata, audit history, signatures, units, attachments, and context.
questions.follow_up_probe: Generate a copy of the most complex changed and signed record, independently reconcile it field-by-field to native data and audit history, and import or inspect the electronic format without the source application.
questions.rationale_risk: A report or PDF may omit metadata and history while appearing complete, and proprietary exports may be unusable during inspection or retention.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: copy requirements, representative records, human-readable output, electronic export and schema, reconciliation, signature/audit display, and readability test. Acceptance: content and meaning are preserved; changed data are evident where required; formats are usable and protected.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample records with edits, signatures, attachments, calculations, long text, nulls, and multiple time zones; compare source, copy, export, and audit trail.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Records Management; Test Lead; Application Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 8, 9, 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c) and 11.50.
questions.red_flags: Copy omits audit trail/signature meaning; export requires unavailable proprietary tool; units/timezone missing; changed record indistinguishable; attachments not reconciled.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how OQ challenges the full lifecycle of critical data so records remain attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original or true copy, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring, and available.
questions.follow_up_probe: Follow one record from acquisition through correction, calculation, review, signature, export, backup, restore, and retrieval, identifying the authoritative record and every transformation.
questions.rationale_risk: Point-function tests can pass while the end-to-end record lifecycle loses source context, metadata, or durable availability.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: data-lifecycle map, critical-data assessment, OQ chain, raw and processed records, metadata/audit trail, signatures, copy, backup/restore, and retrieval. Acceptance: authoritative source is defined; transformations are traceable; no stage obscures history or context; retention and availability are demonstrated.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace records from at least three data-origin types through all lifecycle states; reconcile system evidence to procedure and independent raw source.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Business Process Owner; Test Lead; Records Management; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5-9, 14 and 17; FDA data-integrity guidance; PIC/S PI 041-1; applicable predicate rules.
questions.red_flags: Authoritative record unclear; raw data discarded; metadata lost on transformation; correction overwrites original; restore/retrieval excluded from lifecycle test. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ verifies the configured additional accuracy check for critical manually entered data, including independence, source comparison, correction, override, and audit behavior.
questions.follow_up_probe: Attempt self-verification, copied entry, mismatched source, authorized override, and correction after verification; demonstrate what prevents false assurance.
questions.rationale_risk: A nominal second check can become a ceremonial click or compare two copies of the same erroneous entry.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: critical-data rationale, verification workflow/configuration, role separation, source-display design, OQ cases/results, audit trail, and exception handling. Acceptance: check is independent and source-based; self-check is prevented; discrepancy blocks or controls progression; corrections remain traceable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test multiple roles and five critical fields, including transcription, unit, decimal, and source mismatch; compare source, entry, verification, and audit trail.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Data Owner; Test Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 6 and Section 12; 21 CFR 211.68(b), as applicable.
questions.red_flags: Same user verifies; verifier cannot see source; workflow accepts mismatch; override unlogged; criticality rationale absent; correction erases original.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate under normal and adverse conditions that each critical interface preserves completeness, value, meaning, sequence, uniqueness, security, and end-to-end reconciliation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Inject a duplicate, missing sequence, invalid schema, transformed unit, delayed message, and target outage; show detection, quarantine, retry, reconciliation, and audit evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Connectivity success does not prove correct semantic processing or recovery from partial and duplicate transactions.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: interface mapping, test data, control totals, identifiers, raw source/target records, middleware logs, error queues, alerts, and reconciliation reports. Acceptance: failures and discrepancies are detected; transformations preserve meaning; retries are idempotent; unresolved items are owned and visible.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test source-to-target and reverse reconciliation across at least two critical interfaces; compare record, logs, queue, monitoring, and business report.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Lead; Data Owner; Application Owners; Test Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8 and 5; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f), 11.10(h) and 11.30, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Only successful cases; no control total; retry duplicates; value/meaning change not checked; error queue editable or unowned; alert lacks record identifier.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ independently verifies critical reports, dashboards, calculations, filters, totals, rounding, units, time periods, exports, and drill-down against authoritative source data.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reperform the report most likely to drive a quality decision using an independent query or calculation and explain every difference, including excluded, late, corrected, and duplicate records.
questions.rationale_risk: Plausible summaries can hide incorrect filters, joins, rounding, time cutoffs, or duplicate aggregation.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: report specification, query/rule version, independent oracle, test datasets, expected and actual output, filter/edge cases, export comparison, and traceability. Acceptance: every critical output reconciles to source; inclusion/exclusion and precision are explicit; exports preserve content and context.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use at least three periods and datasets containing corrections, nulls, duplicates, boundary dates, and role-based visibility; compare raw records, query, screen, and export.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Reporting/Data SME; Test Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.7, 6 and 8; 21 CFR 11.10(a)-11.10(b); applicable predicate-rule records such as 21 CFR 211.194.
questions.red_flags: Expected result generated by same report; filter logic undocumented; export differs from screen; corrected/late data omitted; precision or timezone not controlled.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate through OQ that backup and restore functions recover a consistent, readable, accurate, and complete system state, including configuration, audit trails, signatures, attachments, keys, and interface state.
questions.follow_up_probe: Restore a sampled point to an isolated environment and reconcile record counts, hashes or field values, audit chronology, signature linkage, configuration version, and pending transactions to the source point.
questions.rationale_risk: A successful restore status may produce an application that starts but contains incomplete, inconsistent, or unreadable regulated records.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: recovery scope, OQ protocol, backup identifiers, restore logs, source/target reconciliation, application verification, audit/signature checks, deviations, and approval. Acceptance: all critical components restore to a consistent point; integrity and accuracy are proven; recovery evidence is reproducible.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Include full and incremental/point-in-time methods as applicable; sample changed, signed, attached, and in-flight records across source, backup log, restore, and application.
questions.primary_roles: Backup/Recovery Lead; Database Administrator; Application Owner; Data Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Restore verified only by service start; audit/signature/configuration omitted; reconciliation count-only; test uses different backup method; keys unavailable; restore deviations unresolved. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ challenges component failure and failover while proving transaction consistency, controlled user experience, alerting, recovery timing, and return to normal service without untraceable manual intervention.
questions.follow_up_probe: Fail the active component during a critical transaction and reconstruct exactly what the user, database, interface, audit trail, monitor, and support team observed before and after failover.
questions.rationale_risk: High availability can duplicate or lose transactions and obscure which node or state became authoritative.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: continuity architecture, failure scenarios, OQ raw logs, transaction reconciliation, alerts, recovery timing, failback evidence, and deviations. Acceptance: failover is within justified tolerance; no silent loss/duplication occurs; authoritative state is clear; manual steps are controlled and documented.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Challenge application, database, network, storage, and provider-zone failure as applicable; correlate timestamps, records, logs, monitoring, and incident/runbook actions. Triangulation: the auditor selects at least one routine item and one exception from the source population and reconciles them to an independent record.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure/Recovery Lead; Application Owner; Integration Lead; Operations; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 16 and Sections 5 and 7; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Failover tested while idle only; in-flight records not reconciled; RTO claimed without timing evidence; split-brain risk untested; manual failback unapproved.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how OQ verifies scheduled and background jobs for correct sequence, dependencies, calendars, retries, duplicate prevention, late or missed execution, output reconciliation, and operator intervention.
questions.follow_up_probe: Create overlapping execution, dependency failure, clock change, and rerun conditions for one critical job and prove the resulting records remain complete and unique.
questions.rationale_risk: Unattended jobs can silently skip, duplicate, or reorder regulated processing outside normal user controls.
