questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: job inventory, schedules/dependencies, configuration, OQ scenarios, logs, alerts, output reconciliation, rerun procedure, and access controls. Acceptance: execution is attributable and monitored; failures/late jobs alert; reruns are controlled and idempotent; output reconciles.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test daily, period-end, event-driven, and recovery jobs; compare scheduler, application/database logs, monitoring, output records, and incident workflow.
questions.primary_roles: Batch/Scheduler Owner; Operations; Application Owner; Data Owner; Test Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.7, 5, 10 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(f)-11.10(g), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Missed jobs found manually; rerun duplicates data; calendars unversioned; operators edit schedules directly; success status not reconciled to business output.

questions.audit_question: Show how OQ proves that alerts detect loss of service, processing failure, data-integrity exceptions, capacity threats, security events, backup failures, and interface backlog with actionable context and accountable routing.
questions.follow_up_probe: Induce one condition below and one above each critical threshold and demonstrate detection latency, deduplication, escalation, ticket creation, evidence retention, and closure verification.
questions.rationale_risk: A configured dashboard provides false assurance if thresholds, routing, suppression, or health logic are not challenged.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: monitoring requirements, threshold rationale, configuration, induced-event tests, notifications, tickets, escalations, dashboards, and closure. Acceptance: risk-relevant conditions are detected timely; alerts identify affected process/record; owners receive and can act; suppressions are controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Challenge at least six alert families; compare source event, platform log, monitor, notification, ITSM ticket, operator action, and business impact.
questions.primary_roles: Operations Monitoring; Application Owner; Cybersecurity; Business Owner; Test Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 11, 13 and 16; NIST SP 800-53 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Threshold has no rationale; alert reaches unmonitored mailbox; suppression ungoverned; green dashboard despite failed transaction; no closure verification.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that OQ challenges anticipated peak load, data volume, concurrency, latency, storage growth, and long-running operations while preserving control effectiveness and record accuracy.
questions.follow_up_probe: At peak load, repeat a critical calculation, signature, audit-trail query, interface transaction, and timeout-sensitive workflow and reconcile results to baseline behavior.
questions.rationale_risk: Under load a system can time out, drop events, weaken sequence checks, delay audit capture, or return stale results without total outage.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: workload model, capacity assumptions, environment equivalence, performance protocol/raw metrics, error and data reconciliation, monitoring thresholds, and growth plan. Acceptance: justified limits are met; no record loss or control degradation occurs; bottlenecks and headroom are understood.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Run peak, burst, endurance, and near-capacity scenarios; compare application, database, interface, audit, infrastructure metrics, and record counts/results.
questions.primary_roles: Performance Engineer; Infrastructure Lead; Application Owner; Data Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.7 and 11; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.11-3.12; 21 CFR 11.10(a), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Workload arbitrary; test environment materially smaller; response time only metric; audit/interface completeness not checked; capacity margin unknown.

questions.control_topic: Time zone, daylight-saving, and sequence challenge
questions.audit_question: Show how OQ challenges time zones, daylight-saving transitions, clock drift, leap dates, offline events, and out-of-order messages while preserving unambiguous chronology and business-rule timing.
questions.follow_up_probe: Execute a record creation, correction, signature, interface transfer, and expiry rule across a simulated repeated or skipped hour and reconstruct the authoritative order.
questions.rationale_risk: Time edge cases can misorder audit events, apply the wrong effective date, or create duplicate/missing scheduled processing.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: time rules, authoritative source, OQ cases, raw timestamps with offsets, sequence identifiers, scheduler behavior, logs, and reconciliation. Acceptance: chronology and date-based rules remain correct; offsets are retained; ambiguous/late events are handled visibly; drift is alerted.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test at least two time zones, DST transition, offline reconciliation, and clock-source failure; correlate application, database, middleware, and infrastructure logs.
questions.primary_roles: Solution Architect; Test Lead; Integration Lead; Data Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e), where applicable; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: No DST/timezone test; local timestamps lack offset; scheduler duplicates/skips job; audit order differs across layers; manual clock correction unlogged.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate through OQ that migration and conversion routines preserve value and meaning across supported record types, metadata, relationships, signatures, audit histories, attachments, units, and character sets.
questions.follow_up_probe: Rerun a partial migration containing a corrected and signed record plus a rejected record; prove idempotency, exception disposition, and no loss of original history.
questions.rationale_risk: A routine that passes on nominal rows may corrupt complex historical records or duplicate data when restarted.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: mapping rules, versioned scripts, representative datasets, source/target reconciliation, field/relationship comparison, exceptions, rerun results, and approvals. Acceptance: completeness and semantic accuracy are demonstrated; unsupported records are controlled; reruns do not duplicate; source evidence remains available.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use stratified samples by age, type, status, correction, signature, attachment, language, null/boundary value, and rejected condition; independently compare source and target.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Owner; Test Lead; Business Process Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8 and Sections 7, 9, 14 and 17 as relevant; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c) and 11.70.
questions.red_flags: Nominal rows only; count-only reconciliation; signatures/audit history excluded; rerun duplicates; rejects manually edited without trace; source inaccessible after test. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Explain how OQ failures are preserved, investigated, corrected, impact-assessed, regression-tested, and independently reviewed without replacing the original evidence or narrowing acceptance criteria after seeing results.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a test that passed only after multiple attempts and reconstruct every execution, environment/data change, defect, correction, retest authorization, and regression decision.
questions.rationale_risk: Selective retesting and overwritten evidence can convert unexplained failures into apparent passes and hide systemic defects.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: immutable executions, deviations/defects, root cause, change records, impact analysis, retest and regression plan/results, traceability updates, and QA review. Acceptance: all attempts are retained and attributable; acceptance criteria remain pre-approved; root cause and scope are credible; closure precedes reliance on the result.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all critical/high failures and a sample of repeated passes; compare test tool history, logs, defect system, repository/configuration change, and report totals.
questions.primary_roles: Test Lead; Development Lead; Validation Lead; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.7-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2, 4.7 and 13.
questions.red_flags: Failed run deleted; screenshot replaced; expected result changed post hoc; retest lacks authorization; regression scope unexplained; recurring defect closed as tester error.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the OQ report establishes that the configured system operates as designed throughout its anticipated range and is suitable for PQ/UAT, including open defects, deviations, residual risks, baseline identity, and procedural readiness.
questions.follow_up_probe: For every open OQ item, show why realistic business-process testing can proceed without masking or worsening the risk and how the condition is constrained and monitored.
questions.rationale_risk: A stage-gate approval can be schedule-driven and move unresolved functional uncertainty into user testing or production readiness.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: OQ report, criteria/results reconciliation, traceability, defect/deviation register, residual-risk assessment, baseline/version, SOP/training/maintenance readiness, and formal authorization. Acceptance: conclusions are supported by complete evidence; unresolved items have justified non-significant impact or explicit controls; tested object is fixed and identifiable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile report totals to test-management data, defects, deviations, configuration baseline, open-action tracker, and first PQ/UAT execution.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Test Lead; System Owner; Business Process Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.9-2.10 and 3.12-3.13; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2 and 4.7.
questions.red_flags: Report approved before final data; totals do not reconcile; open defects lack business impact; baseline changed after OQ; procedural readiness asserted without evidence.

questions.audit_question: Walk me through how PQ/UAT demonstrates that the complete configured system supports its approved intended use within the real GxP business process, not merely that individual functions passed OQ.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the highest-risk intended-use statement and trace a representative record from initiating event through all users, interfaces, decisions, signatures, outputs, retention, and review to prove the process outcome.
questions.rationale_risk: Individually correct functions can fail when combined in a real process, creating gaps at handoffs, decisions, and accountability points.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: intended-use statement, approved business process, PQ/UAT strategy, end-to-end scripts and raw results, record/audit evidence, deviations, and process-owner acceptance. Acceptance: all critical process outcomes and handoffs work reproducibly in the approved configuration; the authoritative record and accountability are clear.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace at least three end-to-end scenarios, including a normal, changed, and exception record; compare process map, system records, audit trail, interfaces, and user testimony.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; End Users; Validation Lead; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Principle and Sections 4.4 and 4.7; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.13-3.14 where PQ applies; 21 CFR 11.10(a), where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: PQ duplicates OQ scripts; no intended-use trace; process tested in fragments; record handoffs not reconciled; process-owner acceptance is only a signature page.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the PQ/UAT environment is sufficiently equivalent to the production environment for the tested process, data volume, interfaces, security, devices, timing, and operational controls, and justify every material difference.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose the difference with greatest potential to alter behavior and show the technical/risk analysis, compensating test or production verification, acceptance authority, and residual uncertainty.
questions.rationale_risk: User acceptance in a simplified environment can miss production-only security, network, volume, timing, device, or integration failures.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: environment comparison, configuration/version exports, topology, interfaces, data and load profile, device inventory, difference/risk log, and supplemental tests. Acceptance: equivalence is objectively demonstrated; differences are risk-assessed and covered by alternative evidence; the tested baseline is identifiable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare application, database, middleware, identity, network, devices, jobs, monitoring, and provider services between PQ/UAT and planned production.
questions.primary_roles: Infrastructure Lead; System Owner; Validation Lead; Business Process Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.3 and 4.7; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.13-3.14 and 2.4.
questions.red_flags: Equivalence asserted without comparison; production-only interface/device omitted; security relaxed; data/volume unrealistic; differences accepted after testing. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how business and quality owners defined acceptance, selected representative scenarios, reviewed actual evidence, and accepted residual risk rather than delegating PQ/UAT judgment entirely to IT or the supplier.
questions.follow_up_probe: Ask the accepting process owner to explain one failed scenario, one open risk, and one excluded process variant using the underlying evidence and decision rationale.
questions.rationale_risk: A formal signature without informed business review cannot establish fitness for intended use or accountable risk acceptance.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: role assignment, pre-approved acceptance criteria, scenario-selection rationale, reviewer comments, deviations, residual-risk decisions, and signed acceptance. Acceptance: accountable owners demonstrate understanding; acceptance is evidence-based and contemporaneous; conditions and exclusions are explicit.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Interview process owner and QA; reconcile their stated decision to protocol evidence, defect register, risk assessment, and approval timestamps.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Data Owner; Quality Unit; Validation Lead; System Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1-2 and 4.1; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 1.2-1.3, 2.2 and 2.9-2.10; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Owner cannot explain evidence; approval is pre-dated or blanket; criteria defined after results; IT accepts business risk; conditions omitted from approval.

questions.control_topic: Representative users and segregation of duties
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that PQ/UAT used representative business, reviewer, quality, support, and administrator roles to prove both permitted work and practical segregation of duties in complete workflows.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace one record through creation, correction, review, approval, release, and invalidation, and show that no tester accumulated privileges that would be prohibited in production.
questions.rationale_risk: Testing with super-users can bypass real role constraints and conceal workflow dead ends or toxic access combinations.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: production role design, tester-role mapping, identity/access exports, workflow results, positive/negative actions, SoD analysis, and acceptance. Acceptance: testers use production-equivalent roles; duties and handoffs are workable; prohibited actions fail; excess test access does not distort conclusions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample at least five roles and three end-to-end records; reconcile assigned entitlements, actual actions, audit trail, and intended production access.
questions.primary_roles: Business Role Owners; Identity Manager; End Users; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: All testers use admin role; test roles differ from production; SoD not exercised end-to-end; prohibited actions untested; shared accounts obscure attribution.

questions.audit_question: Show how PQ/UAT data represent the actual range of record types, statuses, ages, languages, units, attachments, corrections, signatures, exceptions, and volumes expected in routine use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Identify the least frequent but highest-consequence data variant and demonstrate why it was included or what independent evidence supports excluding it.
questions.rationale_risk: Clean nominal datasets can conceal failures in legacy, exceptional, large, sparse, multilingual, or corrected records.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: production data profile or justified model, data-selection rationale, controlled test dataset, coverage matrix, results, privacy controls, and exception handling. Acceptance: data cover critical variability and worst cases; source/provenance is controlled; exclusions are justified; results remain reproducible.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare test-data distribution to expected production profile; inspect boundary, rare, corrected, signed, attached, historical, and high-volume records.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Business Process Owner; Test Lead; Privacy Officer; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.7 and 7; EU GMP Annex 15 Section 3.14; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Synthetic happy-path data only; no profile/rationale; complex historical records excluded; sensitive data uncontrolled; dataset changed without version trace.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that PQ/UAT covers the business handling of rejected, quarantined, corrected, cancelled, overdue, failed, and escalated records, including ownership and evidence through final disposition.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take one exception that crosses business, IT, and quality boundaries and trace every status, decision, signature, notification, timeout, and audit event to closure.
questions.rationale_risk: Systems often work for normal flow but leave exceptions stranded, silently bypassed, or resolved outside the regulated record.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: exception process and criteria, representative UAT scenarios, records/audit trails, notifications, tickets/deviations, disposition and approval. Acceptance: exceptions remain visible, owned, time-bound, and traceable; no status permits uncontrolled continuation; closure is reconciled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Execute at least five exception types; compare business record, audit trail, notification, ITSM/deviation record, and downstream status.
questions.primary_roles: End Users; Business Process Owner; Quality Unit; Support Lead; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 9 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e) and 11.10(f), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Exceptions handled in email; status can be bypassed; no owner/escalation; correction obscures original; downstream system remains inconsistent after closure.

questions.control_topic: Authoritative record through the business lifecycle
questions.audit_question: Show how users identify and preserve the authoritative GxP record as data move through capture, transformation, review, decision, reporting, correction, retention, and retrieval.
questions.follow_up_probe: For one record represented in several systems and reports, identify which copy controls the GxP decision at each stage and prove how discrepancies are detected and resolved.
questions.rationale_risk: Multiple plausible copies can lead users to act on stale, incomplete, or non-authoritative data.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: data-lifecycle map, source-of-truth rules, PQ/UAT record chain, interface/reconciliation evidence, audit trails, copies/reports, and discrepancy handling. Acceptance: authoritative status is explicit; transformations and copies are traceable; users cannot silently overwrite or confuse records; retention covers required context.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace three records across every system and output; compare identifiers, values, statuses, timestamps, audit history, and user explanation.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Business Process Owner; End Users; Integration Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5-9 and 17; FDA data-integrity guidance; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Users cannot identify source of truth; spreadsheet becomes controlling copy; reconciliation is manual/unrecorded; identifiers change without mapping; stale report used for decision.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate under representative operating conditions that the system, connected equipment or instruments, users, and procedures work together reproducibly to produce the intended GxP process outcome.
questions.follow_up_probe: Run the workflow with the most challenging permitted equipment state, material/product variant, or simulated substitute and reconcile source readings, system decisions, alarms, records, and operator actions.
questions.rationale_risk: A qualified application may fail at the human/equipment/process boundary or under actual operating conditions.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: process knowledge and operating range, equipment status, PQ protocol, representative inputs/materials or justified simulation, raw records, alarms, outputs, repeat runs, and acceptance. Acceptance: integrated process performs effectively and reproducibly across intended conditions; equipment identity/status and source data are retained.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Run multiple users, equipment/devices, and operating conditions; compare equipment logs/calibration, application record, audit trail, and final process output.
questions.primary_roles: Operations/Laboratory Users; Equipment Owner; Process SME; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.13-3.14 where PQ applies; EU GMP Annex 11 Principle and Sections 4.7 and 6; 21 CFR 11.10(h), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Equipment simulated without rationale; calibration/status not checked; single successful run; source data manually re-entered; process output not reconciled.

questions.audit_question: Show how PQ/UAT proves the complete business transaction across upstream and downstream systems, including ownership of failures, reconciliation, reprocessing, late data, and user visibility.
questions.follow_up_probe: Interrupt one cross-system transaction after the source user completes it and require business users to detect, investigate, recover, and verify the final state using approved procedures.
questions.rationale_risk: Interface technical tests may pass while business users cannot see or resolve transactions stranded between systems.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: end-to-end process/data-flow map, UAT scenarios, source/middleware/target records, control totals, alerts, error queue, recovery procedure, and business sign-off. Acceptance: users can determine status and ownership; no data are silently lost/duplicated; recovery preserves auditability and downstream consistency.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace normal, failed, duplicate, delayed, and reprocessed records across all systems, monitoring, ITSM, and business reconciliation.
questions.primary_roles: Business Users; Integration Lead; Application Owners; Support Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(f), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Only middleware evidence; users cannot see failures; manual reprocessing lacks approval; target and source disagree after recovery; reconciliation ownership unclear.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how representative users verified that critical reports, dashboards, calculations, alerts, and decision-support outputs are complete, understandable, timely, and correctly used in the intended GxP decision.
questions.follow_up_probe: Present a deliberately misleading but technically valid edge case and show whether users detect the limitation, access the underlying data, and follow the correct decision path.
questions.rationale_risk: Technically accurate outputs can still cause wrong decisions through ambiguous labels, hidden filters, stale data, or misunderstood limitations.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: intended decision and users, output requirements, UAT datasets/results, source reconciliation, freshness/limitation display, drill-down, SOP, and acceptance. Acceptance: output is accurate and interpretable; data currency and scope are visible; users can verify source and handle limitations.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use normal, boundary, stale, incomplete, corrected, and exception datasets; observe user decisions and reconcile output to source records.
questions.primary_roles: Business Decision Owners; Data Owner; Reporting SME; End Users; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 6, 8 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a)-11.10(b); applicable predicate-rule record requirements.
questions.red_flags: Users accept screenshots; filter/freshness hidden; no drill-down; same SME develops and accepts calculation; known limitation absent from procedure/interface.

questions.audit_question: Show how the people who will perform routine audit-trail review used representative records and risk-based review criteria during PQ/UAT to detect and evaluate meaningful events.
questions.follow_up_probe: Seed a plausible but significant unauthorized or anomalous change among routine events and demonstrate whether the reviewer identifies, interprets, escalates, and documents it.
questions.rationale_risk: A technically functional audit trail does not ensure that real reviewers can detect significant events within operational noise.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: review procedure/criteria, reviewer roles and training, representative audit datasets, seeded-event scenario, review output, escalation, and acceptance. Acceptance: reviewers retrieve complete data, distinguish significant events, document conclusions, and escalate correctly within a justified time.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use at least three record types and periods with normal, corrected, denied, and privileged events; compare reviewer findings to the known event set and raw audit data.
questions.primary_roles: Audit-Trail Reviewers; Data Owner; Quality Unit; Application Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 9; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA data-integrity guidance; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Review tested by administrator not reviewer; no detection criteria; seeded event missed; export omits context; reviewer signs without conclusion or escalation.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that users understand and correctly apply each electronic-signature meaning at the intended decision point and that the signed content, responsibility, and subsequent record state are unambiguous.
questions.follow_up_probe: Present a record with an unresolved exception and ask different roles to sign; show which signatures are blocked, what each permitted signature means, and how later change affects prior approval.
questions.rationale_risk: Technically compliant signatures can be misused if meanings, prerequisites, and responsibilities are ambiguous to users.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: signature matrix, process rules, role mapping, UAT scenarios, signed records/copies, audit trails, user explanation, and SOP. Acceptance: signature meaning and content are clear; prerequisites are enforced; unauthorized or premature signing is blocked; later changes remain visible and controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test at least three meanings and exception states with representative roles; compare user understanding, configured rule, signed record, copy, and audit trail.
questions.primary_roles: End Users; Business Process Owner; Quality Unit; Identity Manager; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70 and 11.200, where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Meaning is generic 'approved'; users cannot explain responsibility; premature signing allowed; later change leaves approval appearing current; signature absent from copy.

questions.audit_question: Show how representative users execute the approved manual or alternate process during system unavailability and reconcile all interim records back into the system without duplication, loss, or backdating.
questions.follow_up_probe: Run a timed outage scenario that crosses a shift or handoff, then restore service and trace every manual record, approval, correction, and reconciliation decision into the electronic record.
questions.rationale_risk: A documented workaround may be too slow, incomplete, or incapable of preserving contemporaneous and attributable records under real conditions.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: continuity procedure, activation criteria, controlled forms/alternate system, trained users, scenario results, timing, manual records, restoration/reconciliation, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance: critical process continues within justified time; records remain attributable and complete; reconciliation is controlled and independently verified.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Exercise at least one full critical workflow and shift handoff; compare manual source, user testimony, recovery log, electronic entry, audit trail, and reconciliation sign-off.
questions.primary_roles: Business Users; Business Continuity Owner; System Owner; Data Owner; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 16 and Sections 5-7; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Workaround tested as tabletop only; uncontrolled paper/forms; backdated entry; reconciliation count-only; shift handoff loses ownership; recovery exceeds process tolerance.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that representative business users can resume the intended process after restore and verify record completeness, workflow state, signatures, reports, interfaces, and pending work at the recovery point.
questions.follow_up_probe: Restore during an in-progress workflow and require users to identify which actions must be repeated, invalidated, or reconciled without consulting undocumented technical knowledge.
questions.rationale_risk: Technical restore success does not prove that the business process and regulated records are usable and trustworthy afterward.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: restore/PQ scenario, recovery point, user verification checklist, source/target reconciliation, pending work and interface status, signed/audit records, reports, and acceptance. Acceptance: users can determine authoritative state and safely resume; all critical records and controls remain intact; unresolved transactions are controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Include completed, in-progress, corrected, signed, interfaced, and scheduled records; compare pre-failure source, backup/restore log, restored system, and user verification.
questions.primary_roles: Business Users; Recovery Lead; Application Owner; Data Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Only DBA validates restore; pending state ignored; users cannot identify recovery point; interfaces resume unreconciled; signatures/reports not checked.

questions.audit_question: Show how PQ/UAT proves that draft operating, review, administration, exception, and continuity procedures accurately reflect the configured system and real user decisions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Ask a trained user to execute a complex exception using only the procedure and record every point where the document is ambiguous, impossible, or inconsistent with the system.
questions.rationale_risk: A system can be fit technically but unsafe operationally when procedures lag the final configuration or omit decision points.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: controlled draft procedures, UAT script referencing procedure steps, observed execution, usability comments, revisions, approvals, and trace to controls. Acceptance: procedures are accurate, executable, role-specific, and cover exceptions; corrections are completed before effective use or formally controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Walk through normal, correction, audit review, access, incident, and outage procedures; compare document steps, system behavior, training material, and user testimony.
questions.primary_roles: End Users; Procedure Owners; System Owner; Training Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 4.1 and 16; EU GMP Chapter 4; 21 CFR 11.10(i)-11.10(k), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Procedure copied from legacy system; UAT ignores SOP; critical step depends on tribal knowledge; screenshots show obsolete UI; exception path undocumented. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how PQ/UAT establishes that representative users and support personnel can competently perform assigned GxP tasks, recognize abnormal conditions, and obtain help without uncontrolled workarounds.
questions.follow_up_probe: Give a trained user an unfamiliar but credible exception and observe whether the person detects the issue, protects the record, escalates correctly, and avoids unauthorized improvisation.
questions.rationale_risk: Attendance-based training does not prove competent use of a complex regulated system or recognition of data-integrity threats.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: role/task analysis, training materials, prerequisite training, competency criteria, observed UAT performance, remediation/reassessment, and support/escalation model. Acceptance: users demonstrate task and exception competence; gaps are remediated before access/use; training matches final system and procedures.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Observe users from different roles, shifts/sites, and experience levels; reconcile training records, UAT actions, errors, help requests, and reassessment.
questions.primary_roles: Training Lead; Business Role Owners; End Users; Support Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 2; EU GMP Annex 15 Section 1.2; 21 CFR 11.10(i); 21 CFR 211.25.
questions.red_flags: Completion equals competence; users coached through UAT; final UI/procedure differs from training; failed user not reassessed; temporary staff/shift omitted.

questions.audit_question: Show how data owners and users verified migrated records for completeness, accuracy, meaning, usability, searchability, signatures, audit history, attachments, and process continuity before accepting the target.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one complex historical record that users initially could not find or interpret and trace investigation, mapping correction, remigration, regression scope, and final acceptance.
questions.rationale_risk: Technical reconciliation can pass while migrated records are unusable, misleading, or detached from the business context required for GxP decisions.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: migration acceptance plan, owner-approved sample, source/target records, reconciliation, usability/retrieval checks, exception log, remigration controls, and sign-off. Acceptance: data owners verify both values and meaning; required history/context is retained; exceptions are resolved; acceptance precedes source retirement.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use risk-stratified samples across record age/type/status/site/language/signature/attachment; independently compare source, target, report, and audit history.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Business Users; Migration Lead; Records Management; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 9, 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c) and 11.70.
questions.red_flags: IT signs for data owner; values checked but history/context omitted; hard-to-find records accepted; remigration overwrites evidence; source retired early. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate under representative concurrent use and data volume that critical business workflows complete within justified time and produce reproducible records and decisions without degraded controls.
questions.follow_up_probe: Repeat the same critical workflow across peak and normal load, different users or sites, and multiple runs; explain any variation in outcome, timing, alerts, or recorded metadata.
questions.rationale_risk: Acceptable technical response time does not prove reproducible process performance or control integrity under real use.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: business service/performance criteria, representative workload, PQ runs, raw timing and resource metrics, record/result comparison, errors, and user acceptance. Acceptance: critical tasks meet justified timing and reproducibility criteria; no audit, interface, or security control degrades; capacity supports intended use.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Run repeated normal, peak, shift-change, and long-duration scenarios; compare user timing, system metrics, record values, audit events, and interface completion.
questions.primary_roles: Business Users; Performance Engineer; Infrastructure Lead; System Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.7 and 11; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 3.13-3.14 where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Single-user run; technical metric only; inconsistent record metadata; peak load excludes interfaces/audit; acceptance threshold defined after result. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Explain how the number of users, runs, records, sites, roles, devices, variants, and operating conditions selected for PQ/UAT provides defensible assurance of effective and reproducible intended use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Challenge the smallest sampled dimension and show why an additional site, role, variant, or run would not reasonably reveal a different high-risk outcome.
questions.rationale_risk: Arbitrary sampling can exclude the variability most likely to expose process and human-system failures.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: population/variability analysis, risk and process knowledge, sample rationale, worst-case selection, protocol coverage, results, and limitations. Acceptance: sample spans critical variability and justified extremes; frequency/number supports reproducibility; exclusions and limitations are explicit and accepted.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare proposed sample to actual business population and risk drivers; verify selected cases were executed and not replaced by convenient examples.
questions.primary_roles: Process SME; Validation Lead; Data Owner; Business Process Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Section 3.14 and Sections 5.19-5.22 when process-validation sampling is relevant; ICH Q9(R1); EU GMP Annex 11 Section 1.
questions.red_flags: One run without rationale; worst case selected by convenience; high-risk site/role omitted; protocol case substituted silently; sample cannot support reproducibility.

questions.control_topic: Open defects and business residual risk
questions.audit_question: Show how every open defect, deviation, limitation, and workaround at PQ/UAT completion was evaluated in the actual business process and accepted by accountable business and quality owners.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take the defect rated below critical but closest to a release or data decision and demonstrate worst-case user impact, detectability, cumulative interactions, workaround effectiveness, and expiry/remediation.
questions.rationale_risk: Technical severity can understate business impact, and multiple low-severity defects can combine into a critical control gap.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: complete open-item register, business/GxP impact, risk assessment, workaround tests, user communication, owner and due date, cumulative review, and acceptance. Acceptance: no unresolved item creates unacceptable risk; compensating controls are effective and time-bound; acceptance is informed and authorized.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all open critical/high and a cross-domain sample of lower items; compare defect system, UAT evidence, risk register, procedures, training, and owner testimony.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; System Owner; Validation Lead; Product/Development Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.8-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.2 and 13; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: IT-only severity; workaround not tested by users; cumulative impact absent; risk acceptance has no expiry; known limitation omitted from procedure/training.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how PQ/UAT evaluates whether users can unambiguously select the correct record, unit, status, workflow action, and signature while the system prevents or detects predictable use errors.
questions.follow_up_probe: Present look-alike records, unit changes, stale data, concurrent edits, and an irreversible action to representative users and observe whether design controls prevent the wrong GxP outcome.
questions.rationale_risk: A technically correct system can systematically induce selection, transcription, confirmation, or interpretation errors.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: use-error/risk analysis, representative users, scenarios, observations, error rates, confirmations/guards, audit records, design or procedure changes, and acceptance. Acceptance: critical actions and data are distinguishable; predictable errors are prevented or promptly detected; residual reliance on training is justified.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Observe users from different roles/sites/experience levels under normal and time-pressure conditions; compare behavior, system guard, error, and audit evidence.
questions.primary_roles: End Users; Business Process Owner; Human-Factors/UX Lead; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Principle, Sections 1, 2, 5 and 6; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f) and 11.10(h), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Critical errors dismissed as training; only expert users tested; look-alike records indistinguishable; irreversible action lacks confirmation/context; concurrent update silently overwrites. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Show how the intended support model handled real PQ/UAT questions, incidents, access requests, interface failures, and data issues using production-like intake, triage, escalation, evidence, and closure.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the most complex UAT support case and trace handoffs between service desk, application, infrastructure, supplier, business, and QA, including whether troubleshooting altered evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: A system may be fit only while project experts are present and fail once operational support assumes responsibility.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: support model/RACI, service catalogue, UAT tickets, escalation paths, supplier SLA, troubleshooting logs, evidence-preservation rules, knowledge records, and acceptance. Acceptance: accountable support resolves or escalates within justified times; evidence is preserved; project-only dependencies are eliminated or controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace access, functional, interface, data-integrity, performance, and supplier cases; compare tickets, system logs, user confirmation, and knowledge/runbook updates.
questions.primary_roles: Service Desk; Application Support; Infrastructure/Integration Support; Supplier; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 3 and 13; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guidance.
questions.red_flags: Project team bypasses service desk; ticket lacks evidence/record impact; supplier escalation untested; troubleshooting changes data directly; user confirmation absent.

questions.control_topic: Business approval of production access model
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how business role owners verified that the proposed production access model is sufficient for work, restrictive for prohibited actions, maintainable through personnel changes, and compatible with independent review.
questions.follow_up_probe: Give role owners a full entitlement export rather than friendly role names and require them to identify one hidden excess privilege, inherited access path, or cross-system conflict.
questions.rationale_risk: Role-name approval without entitlement-level understanding can conceal toxic permissions and operational gaps.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: role catalogue and entitlements, SoD analysis, UAT role results, role-owner review comments, exception/compensating controls, provisioning model, and approval. Acceptance: owners understand actual permissions; roles support duties without excess; conflicts are prevented or independently monitored; ownership is assigned.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review critical roles and entitlements across application, database/reporting, identity groups, and interfaces; compare owner approval to tested actions and SoD results.
questions.primary_roles: Business Role Owners; Identity Manager; Application Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Friendly role name only; entitlement export not reviewed; cross-system conflict absent; inherited access unknown; role owner is IT administrator.

questions.audit_question: Show how trained users retrieve a complete, accurate, human-readable, and electronic inspection package for a representative regulated record within an operationally justified time.
questions.follow_up_probe: Request a record spanning archived and current data, corrections, signatures, attachments, and audit history without advance notice and observe the retrieval and completeness checks.
questions.rationale_risk: Records may be retained but practically unavailable, incomplete, or unintelligible when an inspector requests them.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: retrieval procedure, representative request, timing, native record, human-readable copy, electronic export, audit/signature/attachment package, completeness reconciliation, and user acceptance. Acceptance: authorized users retrieve all required context promptly; copies are accurate and usable; access and export remain controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use recent and historical records, multiple types and statuses, and one corrected/signed record; compare package to native source, audit trail, and retention requirements.
questions.primary_roles: Business Users; Records Management; Data Owner; Application Support; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 8, 9, 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c), 11.50 and 11.70.
questions.red_flags: Retrieval requires vendor/DBA; audit/signature/attachment omitted; export not readable independently; timing excessive; package assembled by uncontrolled manual copying.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the final PQ/UAT report concludes, from reconciled evidence, that the system performs effectively and reproducibly for intended use and is ready for controlled release, with every limitation and condition visible.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reconcile the report's pass conclusion to raw executions, failed attempts, defects, deviations, sample rationale, open risks, user competency, and environment baseline, and explain any inconsistency.
questions.rationale_risk: A narrative conclusion can obscure incomplete coverage, unreconciled failures, or acceptance of a different build than the one intended for release.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved report, criteria-to-result summary, traceability, all execution statuses, defects/deviations, residual risks, sample limitations, user/process-owner acceptance, baseline identity, and release recommendation. Acceptance: totals reconcile; evidence supports reproducibility and intended use; conditions are explicit, owned, time-bound, and approved.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile report metrics to test tool, defect/deviation systems, risk register, training, configuration baseline, and approval timestamps; spot-check ten claims to raw evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Validation Lead; System Owner; End-User Representatives; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.9-2.10 and 3.13-3.14 where applicable; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2 and 4.7; 21 CFR 11.10(a).
questions.red_flags: Conclusion predates evidence; report totals mismatch; failed attempts hidden; business acceptance absent; tested build differs from release candidate; limitations not carried to release.

questions.audit_question: Walk me through the integrated evidence used by accountable business, IT, validation, and quality leaders to decide that the exact production release was fit for controlled GxP use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reconstruct the decision as of the approval timestamp without later evidence and show how each approver knew the validation status, residual risk, data readiness, access, procedures, training, support, recovery, and supplier readiness.
questions.rationale_risk: A checklist can aggregate green statuses that are stale, conditional, or based on different versions and obscure the real release risk.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: go-live checklist/decision record, validation summary, PQ/UAT acceptance, baseline/artifact identity, open risks, migration reconciliation, access/training/SOP/support/recovery readiness, approvals, and conditions. Acceptance: evidence is current and version-consistent; accountable roles approve before use; conditions are explicit, owned, time-bound, and controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Verify ten critical readiness claims against their source systems and timestamps; compare decision pack, change/release record, validation evidence, access, training, and deployment.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; System Owner; Validation Lead; Release Manager; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.9-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 2 and 4.1-4.2; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Approval after first use; status copied from email; different build across evidence; conditional item hidden; QA not authorized/informed; decision pack cannot be reconstructed.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that final traceability reconciles approved intended use, requirements, risks, design/configuration, changes, tests, defects, procedures, and released components with no unexplained orphan or excluded GxP item.
questions.follow_up_probe: Start from a randomly selected production configuration object and trace backward and forward through the final lifecycle records; then repeat from a high-risk requirement to the deployed evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Project traceability may look complete while late changes, excluded objects, or release packaging break the link to the production system.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: final trace matrix, scope/inventory, risk controls, approved changes, configuration baseline, test/defect status, deployment manifest, orphan/coverage analysis, and approval. Acceptance: bidirectional trace is complete for GxP scope; exceptions are justified; released objects match validated evidence; late changes are included.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample five critical requirements, five production objects, two late changes, and two open risks; verify links in source repositories and target configuration.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Configuration Manager; Development/Test Leads; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.7 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Matrix frozen before final change; links not validated; production object absent; untested requirement marked not applicable without approval; released artifact hash missing.

questions.control_topic: Residual defects, deviations, and risk conditions
questions.audit_question: Show how all open defects, deviations, limitations, temporary controls, and accepted risks were evaluated collectively for go-live and converted into visible operational obligations.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the lowest-rated open item with plausible patient, product, or data impact and demonstrate worst-case consequences, detectability, interaction with other items, control effectiveness, owner, expiry, and governance after release.
questions.rationale_risk: Project closure can disperse residual risks across tools and allow temporary workarounds to become permanent, unmonitored controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: complete open-item/risk register, cumulative assessment, workaround/compensating-control tests, owner/due date, operating procedure and monitoring, CAPA/change linkage, and informed approvals. Acceptance: no unacceptable risk remains; conditions are effective, communicated, time-bound, and governed after handover.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all critical/high and a cross-domain sample of lower items; reconcile project tools, decision pack, procedures, training, monitoring, and operational trackers.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; System Owner; Validation Lead; Operations Owner; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.8-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.2 and 13; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Risks split across tools; temporary control untested; no operational owner; expiry absent; cumulative impact not assessed; known limitation not in SOP/training.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the production change and release record authorized the exact validated package, database/configuration changes, timing, implementers, verification, rollback criteria, and segregation of duties before execution.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare the approved manifest to pipeline, artifact repository, privileged session, database execution, and target-system evidence line by line; explain every manual or out-of-band action.
questions.rationale_risk: A generic release approval can permit substitution, untested manual changes, or execution by unauthorized personnel.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved change/release, risk and validation impact, artifact/script hashes, implementation plan, approvals, access assignments, deployment logs, verification, and rollback decision. Acceptance: approved and deployed content is identical; duties are segregated; execution is attributable; deviations trigger controlled assessment.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace the go-live release and one emergency correction across ITSM, repository, pipeline/PAM, database, target configuration, and validation record.
questions.primary_roles: Change Manager; Release Manager; Implementers; Validation Lead; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k) and 21 CFR 211.68(b), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Broad 'deploy application' scope; hashes absent; manual SQL not listed; approval after deployment; same person approves and implements; deviation handled outside change.

questions.control_topic: Production configuration baseline and drift check
questions.audit_question: Show how the final production configuration baseline was captured after deployment and independently reconciled to the tested/approved baseline before regulated use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Run a fresh export or drift scan and explain every difference across application, database, middleware, cloud, identity, scheduler, interface, audit, and retention settings.
questions.rationale_risk: Deployment success does not prove that production settings equal those validated, especially where environment-specific or manual configuration exists.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved baseline, target export, automated/manual comparison, deployment manifest, variance resolution, version/hash, approval, and ongoing drift control. Acceptance: no unexplained difference exists; production state is uniquely identifiable and protected; environment-specific values are pre-approved and tested as relevant.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare at least ten critical settings across source specification, test baseline, production export, deployment logs, and CMDB/cloud inventory.
questions.primary_roles: Configuration Manager; Application/Platform Administrators; Validation Lead; System Owner; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 10 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Baseline captured before deployment; comparison excludes environment settings; unexplained drift; screenshot-only evidence; administrators can change production without detection. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how the cutover sequence, dependencies, timing, decision points, communications, verification, abort criteria, and rollback were rehearsed under realistic conditions and updated from lessons learned.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the point of no return and show who has authority to stop, what objective indicators are available, how partial records are handled, and how rollback preserves data created during cutover.
questions.rationale_risk: A technically sound release can fail through sequencing, delayed decisions, or a rollback plan that cannot preserve newly created records.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: rehearsed cutover/rollback plans, timing and dependencies, roles, objective checkpoints, communications, rehearsal results/deviations, data handling, and final approval. Acceptance: critical steps and rollback are feasible within tolerances; decision authority is explicit; partial/new data are protected and reconciled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare rehearsal and actual cutover timestamps, actions, checks, deviations, communications, and system/data evidence; inspect one failed or delayed step.
questions.primary_roles: Cutover Manager; Release Manager; Business Owner; Technical Leads; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10 and 16; EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.7-2.10; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Rollback is theoretical; no point-of-no-return criteria; rehearsal omits data/interfaces; decision authority unclear; actual deviations not captured; new data would be lost.

questions.audit_question: Show how final production migration proves complete and accurate transfer of values, meaning, metadata, relationships, signatures, audit history, attachments, and exceptions before source restrictions or retirement.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a record changed after the rehearsal but before final cutover and trace incremental capture, transformation, target result, reconciliation, user acceptance, and prevention of double migration.
questions.rationale_risk: Final delta loads and cutover timing create risks not demonstrated by rehearsal, even when prior migration testing passed.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: final approved scripts/mappings, source freeze/delta controls, run logs, control totals and field/relationship comparisons, exception disposition, data-owner checks, signatures/audit verification, and approval. Acceptance: all populations and deltas reconcile; exceptions are closed or controlled; target meaning is preserved; source remains protected until acceptance.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use risk-stratified samples including final deltas, corrected/signed/historical/attached records and rejects; independently compare source, staging, target, and reconciliation.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Owner; Business Process Owner; Validation Lead; Records Management; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8 and Sections 7, 9, 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c) and 11.70.
questions.red_flags: Final delta untested; reconciliation count-only; source changed during load without capture; data owner absent; signatures/audit history omitted; source retired before approval.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how production users, administrators, service accounts, suppliers, and emergency roles were activated from approved sources at go-live and reconciled for least privilege and segregation of duties.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a user with multiple roles and a supplier administrator and reconstruct every entitlement, approval, activation time, privileged session, and post-go-live review across all layers.
questions.rationale_risk: Mass provisioning and cutover urgency can create excess, duplicate, shared, or prematurely active access.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved user/role list, role-owner approval, provisioning logs, target exports, SoD analysis, service/supplier access, PAM, emergency controls, and reconciliation. Acceptance: only authorized named identities are active; duties are separated; temporary access is time-bound; target access fully reconciles before GxP use.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile joiners, movers, admins, service accounts, supplier and emergency identities from HR/role approval through identity, application, database, cloud, and PAM.
questions.primary_roles: Identity Manager; Business Role Owners; Application Owner; Cybersecurity; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), 11.200 and 11.300, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Bulk access without owner approval; shared admin; supplier account always enabled; SoD checked only in application; target reconciliation incomplete; temporary access no expiry.

questions.audit_question: Show how production audit trails were confirmed active before GxP use and how trained reviewers, review scope, frequency, tools, escalation, and retained review evidence were operationally ready.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use the first production records and configuration events to perform an unscripted review, reconcile completeness to raw logs, and demonstrate escalation of one meaningful event.
questions.rationale_risk: Validated audit functionality provides no control if production logging starts late or routine review has no trained owner and actionable process.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: pre-use audit check, first events, risk-based review procedure/schedule, reviewer access/training, tool/export, escalation workflow, review form, and ownership. Acceptance: logging precedes GxP activity; review is executable and complete; findings link to incident/deviation; evidence is retained.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review first production day/records, admin/configuration events, user list, raw audit data, reviewer output, and incident/deviation linkage. Triangulation: the auditor selects at least one routine item and one exception from the source population and reconciles them to an independent record.
questions.primary_roles: Audit-Trail Reviewers; Data Owner; Application Owner; Quality Unit; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 9; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA data-integrity guidance; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: First GxP events precede logging; review procedure not effective; reviewer lacks access/training; export incomplete; review frequency not risk-based; findings stay in email.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that production electronic-signature identities, credentials, meanings, record linkage, time, human-readable copies, policies, and user certification obligations were ready before any regulated signing.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace the first production signature from identity verification and access activation through signed content, manifestation, audit trail, printable copy, and any subsequent record change.
questions.rationale_risk: A validated signature function can be noncompliant in production if identities, meanings, policies, or trust dependencies are not correctly activated.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: signature policy, identity verification, role/meaning matrix, production configuration, time/certificate status, first signed records, audit/copy, training, and applicable FDA certification record. Acceptance: unique authorized signers apply correct meanings; linkage and manifestations persist; first use is controlled and attributable.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect first signatures for each critical meaning and role; compare identity source, access approval, signed record, audit trail, copy, and policy/training.
questions.primary_roles: Business Process Owner; Identity Manager; Application Owner; Quality Unit; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200 and 11.300, where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Signing begins before identity/access approval; meaning misconfigured; first signatures use test account; copy omits manifestation; certificate/time dependency not checked.

questions.audit_question: Show how all procedures and work instructions required for operation, review, administration, access, change, incident, backup, continuity, retention, and inspection were approved, effective, accessible, and aligned to the released system.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the procedure most changed after UAT and have an operational user execute a critical exception using the effective version; reconcile any divergence from production behavior.
questions.rationale_risk: Users may enter regulated operation with obsolete or incomplete instructions despite successful validation.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: document inventory, effective versions, approval/effective dates, release/configuration references, distribution/access, obsolete-version withdrawal, UAT feedback, and readiness approval. Acceptance: required documents are effective before use, match production, define roles/exceptions, and are controlled against obsolete use.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample procedures across business, QA review, administration, incident, access, backup/restore, continuity, and record retrieval; compare system behavior and user access.
questions.primary_roles: Procedure Owners; Document Control; Business Users; System Owner; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 4.1 and 16; EU GMP Chapter 4; 21 CFR 11.10(i)-11.10(k), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Procedure effective after go-live; obsolete version accessible; steps conflict with production; critical exception absent; document references test screenshots or old roles.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that only personnel who completed role-specific training and any required competency assessment received production access before performing assigned GxP tasks.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the earliest production users, including a late joiner and support administrator, and reconcile training completion time, curriculum version, competency result, access activation, and first activity.
questions.rationale_risk: Schedule pressure can activate access before users understand final procedures, exceptions, data integrity, or signature responsibilities.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: role-training matrix, final materials/procedures, assignments, completion and assessment, exception approvals, access-gating logic/process, activation logs, and first-use audit trail. Acceptance: required training precedes access/use; content matches released system; failures are remediated and reassessed; exceptions are rare and controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile a stratified sample of end users, reviewers, admins, support, temporary and supplier personnel across LMS, identity/access, and system activity.
questions.primary_roles: Training Lead; Business Role Owners; Identity Manager; System Owner; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 2; EU GMP Annex 15 Section 1.2; 21 CFR 11.10(i); 21 CFR 211.25.
questions.red_flags: Access before training; curriculum based on prior build; competency absent; admin/support excluded; exception approved generically; first activity predates completion.

questions.audit_question: Show how project responsibilities were transferred to named process, system, data, service, security, supplier, validation, and quality owners with accepted obligations, records, access, and decision authority.
questions.follow_up_probe: Ask each owner to demonstrate one assigned control and locate its evidence without project-team assistance; resolve any conflicting RACI or unowned shared-service control.
questions.rationale_risk: Controls fail after project closure when ownership is nominal, fragmented, or dependent on departing experts.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved operational RACI, owner acceptance, control calendar, access, service/asset records, open actions, supplier responsibilities, knowledge transfer, and governance forum. Acceptance: every critical control has one accountable owner and capable performers; overlaps/gaps are resolved; records and authority are available.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test ownership for access review, audit-trail review, change, incident, backup/restore, periodic review, supplier oversight, and retention using interviews and source evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Process/System/Data Owners; Service Owners; Cybersecurity; Supplier Manager; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2-3 and 11-13; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guidance.
questions.red_flags: Owner named but unaware; shared-service control unowned; project account retains responsibility; conflicting RACIs; no calendar/evidence access; supplier responsibility assumed.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that production monitoring and alerts cover critical service, transaction, data-integrity, security, capacity, backup, interface, and job conditions and reach staffed, competent responders from the first regulated use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Induce or identify an early production alert and trace source event, threshold, notification, on-call acknowledgement, ticket, business/QA impact assessment, resolution, and closure verification.
questions.rationale_risk: A production system can operate unobserved during the most unstable period if monitoring, routing, or responder readiness lags go-live.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: coverage map, production configuration, alert tests, routing/on-call schedule, contacts/escalation, runbooks, ITSM integration, early alerts, and readiness approval. Acceptance: all critical assets/events are monitored; alerts are actionable and timely; accountable responders are staffed and trained; suppression is controlled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare architecture/CMDB to monitoring/log sources; trace alerts across application, interface, database, infrastructure, backup, and security to tickets and business status.
questions.primary_roles: Operations Monitoring; On-Call Support; Application Owner; Business Owner; Cybersecurity; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 11, 13 and 16; NIST SP 800-53 supporting guidance.
questions.red_flags: Coverage not reconciled; on-call begins later; alerts point to project mailbox; no business context; suppression left from testing; early failures not ticketed.

questions.control_topic: Production backup, restore, and recovery readiness
questions.audit_question: Show how production backup enrollment, first successful jobs, restore evidence, recovery runbook, keys, alternate infrastructure, recovery objectives, and responder readiness were confirmed before reliance on the system.
questions.follow_up_probe: Starting from the first production backup, prove that a recoverable, consistent point exists for all components and explain the exposure between first GxP transaction and confirmed protection.
questions.rationale_risk: Go-live may create regulated records before backup coverage or recovery capability is actually effective.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: production recovery inventory, backup configuration and first jobs, repository protection, recent representative restore, runbook, key/access readiness, RTO/RPO rationale, on-call contacts, and approval. Acceptance: protection precedes or safely coincides with GxP data creation; scope is complete; failures alert; recovery is tested and owned.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile production components to backup console and first logs; inspect application, database, configuration, audit, attachment, key, and interface-state recovery evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Backup/Recovery Lead; Application Owner; Database Administrator; Business Continuity Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: First records predate backup; asset missing; restore tested on different stack; recovery keys unavailable; RTO/RPO assumed; failure alert unowned.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that documented manual or alternate arrangements can be activated within the justified business tolerance from the first day of operation and preserve attributable, complete, and reconcilable records.
questions.follow_up_probe: Run an unannounced tabletop-plus-practical activation with the actual shift/on-call team and trace one critical transaction through manual capture, approval, handoff, restoration, and reconciliation.
questions.rationale_risk: Continuity plans often assume trained staff, forms, access, supplies, or alternate systems that are unavailable at launch.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: process impact/risk, activation criteria, approved plan/forms, contacts, training, practical exercise, timing, records, restoration/reconciliation, and lessons/actions. Acceptance: alternate arrangements start within tolerance; ownership and communication work; records remain controlled; reconciliation is defined and tested.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Exercise a critical workflow and shift handoff with actual users; compare plan, contact response, manual record, system recovery, electronic audit trail, and sign-off.
questions.primary_roles: Business Continuity Owner; Business Users; System Owner; Recovery Lead; Data Owner; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 16 and Sections 5-7; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Plan not exercised; contact list/project staff obsolete; controlled forms unavailable; activation exceeds tolerance; back-entry method encourages backdating or duplicates.

questions.audit_question: Show how hypercare distinguishes service issues, GxP incidents, data-integrity events, validation deviations, and change requests while preserving evidence and escalating quality impact without delay.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the first material post-release issue and reconstruct detection, evidence preservation, record/product impact, containment, QA notification, root cause, correction, validation impact, and closure.
questions.rationale_risk: High-volume launch support can treat regulated failures as ordinary defects and overwrite evidence during rapid troubleshooting.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: hypercare model, classification/escalation criteria, contacts, ticket/deviation linkage, evidence-preservation rules, early issues, metrics, root cause/CAPA/change, and exit criteria. Acceptance: GxP impact is assessed promptly; original evidence is preserved; fixes are controlled and verified; trends inform exit.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace early tickets across service desk, application logs, business records, deviation/CAPA, change/validation, supplier, and user closure; review trend and repeat issues.
questions.primary_roles: Hypercare Lead; Service Desk; System Owner; Business Owner; Validation Lead; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13 and Sections 4.2 and 10; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guidance.
questions.red_flags: GxP classification absent; issue fixed before evidence capture; QA notified late; repeated defect treated separately; direct data fix; hypercare exit ignores open trend.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that supplier and internal-provider support obligations, service levels, named contacts, escalation, remote access, evidence availability, patch/change notification, continuity, and exit responsibilities were operational at handover.
questions.follow_up_probe: Exercise a critical escalation and show response timing, identity/access control, evidence shared, decision authority, subcontractor involvement, and regulated-user oversight from open to verified closure.
questions.rationale_risk: Contract language provides little protection if operational contacts, access, evidence, and escalation do not work at launch.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: quality/service agreements, support entitlement, contact/escalation test, SLA/OLA, remote-access controls, change/security notification, evidence obligations, continuity/exit plan, and owner acceptance. Acceptance: responsibilities are unambiguous; support is reachable; access is controlled; evidence and notifications meet regulated-user needs.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Test one critical and one routine support path; compare contract, service portal, access/PAM logs, supplier response, internal ticket, and closure verification.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Manager; Service Owner; Application Support; Cybersecurity; System Owner; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3.1-3.4 and 16; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guidance.
