questions.red_flags: Support entitlement not active; generic contact; subcontractor unknown; remote access always on/shared; evidence rights missing; change notice arrives after release.

questions.audit_question: Show how the production release was assessed for known vulnerabilities, unsupported components, hardening gaps, exposed paths, and security exceptions, with explicit GxP and data-integrity impact before go-live.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the highest unresolved vulnerability or hardening exception and demonstrate deployed-version exposure, exploitability, compensating controls, monitoring, validation impact, owner, remediation date, and emergency response.
questions.rationale_risk: A validated release can enter service with exploitable weaknesses capable of altering or denying regulated records.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: release-specific scans/SBOM, hardening verification, penetration or security assessment as justified, risk decisions, compensating controls, monitoring, remediation/change plan, and approvals. Acceptance: no unacceptable exposure remains; exceptions are specific, time-bound, monitored, and linked to validated components.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare release artifact/SBOM and production scan to inventory, risk register, network/access controls, monitoring, and planned remediation; verify one control directly.
questions.primary_roles: Cybersecurity; Development/Platform Leads; System Owner; Validation Lead; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 10 and 12; NIST SP 800-53 and SP 800-218 supporting guidance; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: Scan not release-specific; critical vulnerability waived because system validated; no GxP impact; compensating control untested; exception no expiry; unsupported component.

questions.control_topic: Production interface, job, and scheduler verification
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that all production endpoints, credentials, certificates, routes, queues, schedules, calendars, dependencies, alerts, and reconciliations were activated and verified without creating uncontrolled test or duplicate records.
questions.follow_up_probe: Trace the first production transaction and first scheduled run end to end, including source authorization, middleware, target, control totals, alerts, retries, and business confirmation.
questions.rationale_risk: Environment-specific endpoints and schedules can differ from qualification and create immediate data loss, duplication, or misrouting.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: production interface/job inventory, approved configuration, endpoint/credential/certificate checks, activation plan, first-run records/logs, reconciliation, alerts, and approvals. Acceptance: destinations and timing are correct; test paths are disabled; first transactions reconcile completely; failures are visible and owned.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect every critical interface/job and sample routine ones; compare design, production configuration, source/target data, middleware/scheduler logs, monitoring, and business reconciliation.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Lead; Scheduler Owner; Application Owners; Data Owner; Operations; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5, 10 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f), 11.10(h) and 11.30, where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Test endpoint/credential remains; first run not reconciled; schedule manually edited; duplicate startup run; certificate unverified; monitoring not active.

questions.audit_question: Show how retention, legal/quality hold, archive, deletion, readability, integrity, and retrieval controls were configured and operational for each regulated record type before production records accumulated.
questions.follow_up_probe: For one record with the longest retention and one with attachments/audit history, trace configured lifecycle rules, storage, holds, access, archive format, retrieval test, and prevention of premature deletion.
questions.rationale_risk: Default retention or untested archive configuration can irreversibly delete, detach, or render regulated records unreadable.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: record inventory and retention requirements, configuration exports, archive design, holds, deletion controls, access, readability/integrity test, retrieval procedure, and owner approval. Acceptance: rules match approved requirements; related metadata/audit/signatures remain linked; deletion is authorized and traceable; retrieval is tested.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample record classes, longest/shortest retention, hold, signed/corrected/attached record, and archive retrieval; compare policy, configuration, native/archive output, and audit logs.
questions.primary_roles: Records Management; Data Owner; Application Owner; Infrastructure/Archive Owner; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c) and applicable predicate-rule retention requirements such as 21 CFR 211.180.
questions.red_flags: Vendor default retention; audit/attachments excluded; archive unreadable without source system; deletion job active before approval; hold not tested; owner unknown.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the GxP system inventory, system description, physical/logical arrangements, data flows, interfaces, prerequisites, security measures, owners, and validation status were updated to the production as-built state at handover.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a production component or data flow by direct discovery and trace it to the inventory, system description, CMDB/cloud record, owner, support, backup, monitoring, and validation evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: Incomplete inventory and system description create control gaps in change, security, recovery, periodic review, and inspection response.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved inventory/system description, as-built diagrams, data/interface inventory, component prerequisites, security and recovery controls, owners, validation status, CMDB/cloud reconciliation, and approval. Acceptance: records match production, are current and sufficiently detailed, and link all critical controls/owners.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Discover and trace at least five components/data flows across target system, architecture, CMDB, backup, monitoring, access, supplier, and validation records.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Solution Architect; Configuration Manager; Data Owner; Validation Lead; QA
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.3 and Sections 2, 3 and 11.
questions.red_flags: Inventory lists application only; diagram not as-built; data flows/interfaces omitted; owner/support mismatch; validation status stale; cloud/service component missing.

questions.control_topic: Validation summary and formal release authorization
questions.audit_question: Show how the validation summary report objectively reconciles planned and executed lifecycle evidence, deviations, changes, traceability, acceptance criteria, residual risk, and the precise released version before formal authorization for GxP use.
questions.follow_up_probe: Spot-check the report's most material conclusions against raw source records and explain any evidence created, revised, or approved after the stated release decision.
questions.rationale_risk: A polished summary can conceal incomplete execution, late evidence, inconsistent totals, or a release version not actually validated.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: approved validation summary, plan-to-actual reconciliation, traceability, protocol/report status, all deviations/defects/changes, residual risks, baseline/artifact identity, QA review, and formal release. Acceptance: claims reconcile to raw evidence; no unexplained gap exists; authorization precedes use; the released object is uniquely identified.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile all totals and status categories; trace ten conclusions to protocols, test tool, defect/deviation/change records, repository/deployment, and approval audit trail.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; System Owner; Business Process Owner; Release Manager; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.9-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2; 21 CFR 11.10(a), where applicable.
questions.red_flags: Summary approved after use; totals mismatch; raw failures hidden; late changes omitted; release version unclear; QA review superficial; conditional approval not visible.

questions.audit_question: Where the system supports batch certification, product disposition, laboratory release, or another regulated release decision, demonstrate that only authorized roles can act and that the decision, identity, time, meaning, source evidence, and record status are complete at go-live.
questions.follow_up_probe: Attempt release with an unauthorized role, incomplete prerequisite, unresolved exception, altered supporting result, and disconnected signature service; show enforced blocks, evidence, and escalation.
questions.rationale_risk: A release workflow defect can directly permit product disposition on incomplete or unauthorized evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: applicable release requirements, role/authority configuration, prerequisite/status rules, signature setup, production verification, audit trail, record copy, exception workflow, and responsible-owner acceptance. Acceptance: release is limited to authorized persons; prerequisites are enforced; decision and supporting evidence are attributable, complete, and retained.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use representative release roles and record states; compare identity/access, source results, workflow rules, signed release, audit trail, and printable/electronic record.
questions.primary_roles: Qualified Person or Authorized Release Role; Quality Unit; Business Process Owner; Application Owner; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 15 where batch certification/release applies, plus Sections 12 and 14; 21 CFR 11.10, 11.50 and 11.70 and applicable predicate rules such as 21 CFR 211.188/211.194.
questions.red_flags: Unauthorized role can release; prerequisites advisory only; signature meaning/record link absent; release ignores altered/incomplete source; exception bypass unlogged.

questions.control_topic: Post-go-live control calendar and periodic evaluation
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how handover established the first periodic evaluation, access and audit-trail reviews, backup/restore checks, supplier reviews, vulnerability/patch governance, metrics, open-risk follow-up, and hypercare exit based on system risk.
questions.follow_up_probe: For each recurring control, show the first due date, population/data source, acceptance criteria, accountable owner, escalation, retained evidence, and mechanism that prevents the control from being missed after project closure.
questions.rationale_risk: A valid release can rapidly lose control if lifecycle activities have no scheduled owner, criteria, data source, or escalation.
questions.expected_evidence: Evidence: operational control calendar, risk-based frequencies, procedures, owners/backups, system-generated reminders, evidence repositories, KPI/KRI baselines, periodic-review plan, hypercare exit criteria, and governance approval. Acceptance: all recurring controls are scheduled and resourced; criteria and evidence are defined; open obligations transfer; overdue items escalate.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Trace access review, audit review, backup/restore, incident trend, supplier, security, change/configuration and periodic evaluation from risk to calendar, owner, tool, and first execution plan.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Business Process Owner; Data Owner; Operations; Supplier Manager; Cybersecurity; Quality Unit
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 9, 11-13 and 16; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guidance; ICH Q9(R1).
questions.red_flags: First review date absent; owner is project role; frequency arbitrary; no population/criteria; reminder manual and unowned; hypercare closes with open trends; risks not transferred.

questions.audit_question: Reconstruct the most recent periodic evaluation from its source populations and show how the conclusion that the system remains fit for intended use, in a validated state, and compliant was reached.
questions.follow_up_probe: Identify the highest-risk unresolved item at the evaluation cut-off date, explain why it did not invalidate the conclusion, and show the approved interim control, accountable owner, due date, and subsequent status.
questions.rationale_risk: A summary-level review can conceal unresolved changes, incidents, security weaknesses, or validation gaps and produce an unsupported continued-use decision.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved periodic-evaluation procedure and report; frozen populations for changes, incidents, deviations, problems, access reviews, vulnerabilities, supplier changes, backup and recovery tests, performance, training, validation status, and open CAPA. Acceptance requires traceable source totals, documented scope and cut-off, risk-based conclusions, Quality approval, and controlled follow-up of every exception.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Auditor selects the latest evaluation and one prior evaluation; reconcile report totals to ServiceNow or equivalent ITSM, quality-management system, identity platform, vulnerability platform, backup console, supplier records, and validation repository; trace two carried-forward actions to closure or current escalation.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; IT Service Owner; Validation Lead; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.1, and 11; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Review based on curated summaries rather than complete populations; missing cut-off; overdue critical actions omitted; unapproved residual risk; conclusion copied from prior review; material conflicts between source systems and report.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the approved system inventory entry and system description represent the live physical and logical arrangement, GxP functions, interfaces, data flows, prerequisites, hosting locations, and security boundaries as of today.
questions.follow_up_probe: The auditor will select one live component or interface from monitoring and ask you to locate it in the inventory, architecture, configuration-management database, risk assessment, and support model; explain any discrepancy and its impact.
questions.rationale_risk: An inaccurate inventory or system description undermines validation scope, change impact assessment, security monitoring, backup coverage, incident response, and retirement planning.
questions.expected_evidence: Current approved inventory, system description, architecture and data-flow diagrams, interface register, CMDB records, hosting and supplier inventory, and reconciliation record. Acceptance requires all live GxP-relevant components and dependencies to be uniquely identified, owned, versioned, and periodically reconciled.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one application node, database, interface, scheduled job, service account, and storage location from live telemetry; reconcile each to approved documentation, CMDB, backup scope, access model, and monitoring coverage.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Solution Architect; Configuration Manager; Infrastructure Owner; Integration Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Undocumented live components or interfaces; shared dependencies outside scope; obsolete diagrams; conflicting versions; missing owner; component absent from backup, monitoring, validation, or security scope.

questions.audit_question: Using the complete current privileged-access population, demonstrate how each administrative entitlement is justified by job responsibility, independently approved, technically constrained, monitored, and periodically recertified.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the most powerful role and show whether its holder can create or alter GxP data, change audit-trail settings, delete records, modify security, and approve their own work; explain the preventive or independently operating compensating controls.
questions.rationale_risk: Excessive or conflicted administrative rights can permit undetectable alteration, deletion, or concealment of regulated records and configuration changes.
questions.expected_evidence: Role catalogue, privilege matrix, named-user export, approval records, recertification results, segregation-of-duties analysis, privileged-session or activity logs, and exception records. Acceptance requires unique identities, least privilege, independence from regulated activity where feasible, timely exception removal, and documented monitoring of unavoidable conflicts.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Auditor obtains the population directly from the application, operating system, database, cloud console, and identity provider; reconcile to HR roster and approval system; test one administrator, one vendor account, one emergency account, and one rejected or overdue review item.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Identity and Access Management Owner; Security Officer; Database or Platform Administrator; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(b) for drug CGMP systems.
questions.red_flags: Analysts or business users hold unrestricted administrator rights; shared admin credentials; unexplained local accounts; self-approval; incomplete technical population; overdue removal; audit logs unavailable or review performed by the same administrator.

questions.audit_question: Trace the joiner, mover, and leaver control from the authoritative HR event through identity-provider and application entitlements to prove that access is granted, changed, and removed within approved risk-based time limits.
questions.follow_up_probe: For an auditor-selected privileged leaver or mover, show every access path that survived the HR event, including local accounts, API tokens, remote-support accounts, cached credentials, group inheritance, and owned service accounts, and explain any activity after the effective time.
questions.rationale_risk: Incomplete deprovisioning or role change can leave unauthorized access paths capable of altering regulated data or configurations.
questions.expected_evidence: HR source record, IAM workflow, application and infrastructure account exports, group membership, token and remote-access inventory, activity logs, service-account ownership transfer, SLA metrics, and exceptions. Acceptance requires end-to-end completeness, timely execution, no unexplained post-termination activity, and risk-assessed exceptions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Use the HR population, not the access-review list, for the last 12 months; select one same-day leaver, one privileged leaver, one cross-functional mover, one contractor, and one delayed case; reconcile timestamps across HR, IAM, application, VPN, and SIEM.
questions.primary_roles: HR Data Owner; IAM Owner; System Administrator; System Owner; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 and 12.3; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Sampling only completed tickets; termination timestamp later than observed activity; unmanaged local or vendor accounts; inherited entitlements omitted; service accounts still owned by leavers; no retrospective impact assessment for delayed removal.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how every non-human identity is inventoried, uniquely purposed, least-privileged, credential-managed, monitored, and assigned to a current accountable owner throughout operation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose one high-privilege service account and show what prevents interactive use, credential sharing, unapproved secret extraction, and silent activity; then demonstrate the last credential rotation without disrupting or bypassing the validated process.
questions.rationale_risk: Long-lived or poorly owned non-human credentials can become persistent, weakly attributable paths for unauthorized data or configuration changes.
questions.expected_evidence: Service-account inventory, purpose and owner, entitlement mapping, vault records, rotation history, interactive-login restrictions, activity logs and alerts, dependency mapping, and exception approvals. Acceptance requires no orphaned identities, controlled secrets, attributable use, least privilege, and tested rotation or revocation.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile accounts discovered from application, database, operating system, cloud IAM, scheduler, API gateway, and secret vault to the approved inventory; select one dormant, one high-privilege, one supplier-controlled, and one recently rotated account.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; IAM Owner; Application Administrator; Integration Owner; Security Operations; Supplier Service Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls AC-2 and IA-5 as security guidance.
questions.red_flags: Unknown owner or purpose; shared credential in code or tickets; interactive login permitted without justification; no rotation; account activity outside expected jobs; inventory reconstructed manually for the audit.

questions.audit_question: Using an auditor-selected GxP record, demonstrate how audit-trail review identifies, evaluates, and resolves every material creation, modification, deletion, reprocessing, status change, and security event relevant to the quality decision.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show the complete event population for the same record directly from the system, including events not displayed in the routine review report, and explain how reviewers detect missing periods, disabled logging, administrator activity, clock differences, or repeated attempts that did not change the final value.
questions.rationale_risk: Checklist review or incomplete audit-trail extracts can miss selective testing, unauthorized changes, deleted data, or manipulation hidden behind a final acceptable result.
questions.expected_evidence: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Acceptance requires complete intelligible events, independent and timely review, documented reasons for GxP changes, and traceable resolution before the associated decision where required.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one released record, one corrected record, one invalidated or repeated activity, one administrator event, and one record associated with an incident; reconcile application audit trail to database or platform logs, user identity, source data, review record, and batch or quality disposition.
questions.primary_roles: Process Owner; Quality Reviewer; Data Owner; System Administrator; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Audit trail disabled, configurable by conflicted users, incomplete, unintelligible, or unavailable; review limited to final values; missing reasons; unexplained gaps; late review after batch or quality decision; admin actions excluded.

questions.audit_question: Select a completed electronic signature and prove from the live record and underlying controls that the signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, credential use, and permanent linkage to the exact signed record version remain unambiguous and non-transferable.
questions.follow_up_probe: Demonstrate what happens when the signed record is subsequently corrected, migrated, exported, or archived, and show that the signature cannot be excised, copied to another record, or displayed against a changed version without an attributable event.
questions.rationale_risk: Weak identity, manifestation, or linkage controls can allow repudiation, signature reuse, or a signature to appear to approve content the signer did not review.
questions.expected_evidence: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, preservation after record lifecycle events, and no shared credentials.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one approval, one rejection, one corrected signed record, and one archived or migrated signed record; reconcile application display, electronic copy, audit trail, identity provider, and underlying database identifiers or hashes.
questions.primary_roles: Process Owner; Quality Assurance; System Owner; IAM Owner; Records Manager; Validation Lead
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Signature not tied to a record version; missing meaning or timestamp; shared credentials; signature can be copied or detached; correction changes signed content without new signature; archive or export loses linkage.

questions.audit_question: Retrieve an auditor-selected record from the oldest active retention cohort and demonstrate that its content, context, critical metadata, audit trail, and associated signatures remain accurate, readable, intelligible, and available for review without relying on undocumented expert intervention.
questions.follow_up_probe: Repeat the retrieval for a record created before the latest major application, database, operating-system, or viewer change and explain how continued readability and meaning were verified when technology changed.
questions.rationale_risk: Records may exist physically yet become unreadable, incomplete, context-free, or inaccessible before the required retention period expires.
questions.expected_evidence: Retention schedule, record inventory, storage and archive architecture, retrieval procedure, periodic readability and integrity checks, sample record with metadata and audit trail, and technology-change impact assessments. Acceptance requires timely retrieval, complete content and context, verified integrity, controlled access, and documented remediation of failed checks.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Choose the oldest record, a record spanning a major technology change, a corrected record, and a legal-hold record; compare system display or archive output to original control totals, checksums where used, audit trail, and approved retention rule.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Data Owner; System Owner; Archive Administrator; Quality Assurance; Infrastructure Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
questions.red_flags: Old records cannot be retrieved promptly; proprietary viewer unavailable; metadata or audit trail omitted; integrity checks never performed; retention period guessed; technology changes not assessed; reliance on an unsupported production environment.

questions.audit_question: Reconcile the approved inventory of GxP data, metadata, audit trails, configurations, encryption material, and supporting components to the live backup job definitions and demonstrate that the backup scope remains complete after system changes.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one newly added or changed component and one apparently successful backup; prove that the required content was actually captured and usable rather than merely that the job ended with a success status.
questions.rationale_risk: A green backup dashboard can conceal omitted databases, audit trails, keys, attachments, configurations, or new components, making validated recovery impossible.
questions.expected_evidence: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconciliation after change, and no unapproved exclusions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile system description, CMDB, database catalogue, storage inventory, interface stores, secret or key dependencies, and backup console; sample latest success, last failure, newly commissioned component, and one excluded item.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Backup Administrator; Database Administrator; Infrastructure Owner; Security Officer; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.
questions.red_flags: Scope cannot be reconciled; successful status accepted without content verification; audit trails, attachments, or keys excluded; backup changes outside change control; failed jobs aged or suppressed; no protected off-system copy where risk requires it.

questions.audit_question: Reperform the evidence chain for the last recovery exercise and show that the recovered service met approved recovery time and recovery point objectives while preserving record completeness, data meaning, audit trails, interfaces, security, and business-process usability.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show the last failed or partially successful restore step, how the failure was detected, what data interval or functionality was at risk, and whether the retest proved the corrective action rather than repeating only the successful path.
questions.rationale_risk: Technical restoration alone does not prove that a regulated process can resume with complete, accurate, secure, and usable records within tolerable downtime.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires objectives achieved or deviations formally assessed with effective remediation and no unexplained data loss.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select the latest full exercise, one component-level restore, and the most recent real outage; reconcile backup timestamps, orchestration logs, monitoring, database recovery point, interface queues, user acceptance, incident record, and business resumption time.
questions.primary_roles: Business Continuity Owner; System Owner; Process Owner; Disaster Recovery Lead; Database Administrator; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
questions.red_flags: Restore never tested; test excludes audit trails, interfaces, keys, or business verification; RTO or RPO missed without risk acceptance; failed step omitted; recovered data not reconciled; exercise performed only on unlike infrastructure.

questions.audit_question: Trace a complete GxP data transfer from authoritative source through middleware to target and downstream report, demonstrating how completeness, accuracy, sequence, attribution, timestamps, and processing status are reconciled in routine operation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Use the last failed, duplicate, delayed, partial, or out-of-order transfer and show how the system prevented silent loss or double processing, preserved the original event, controlled reprocessing, and assessed downstream quality impact.
questions.rationale_risk: Interfaces can silently truncate, duplicate, transform, delay, or misattribute data while endpoints each appear healthy.
questions.expected_evidence: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. Acceptance requires end-to-end traceability, controlled error handling, no silent loss or duplication, and documented impact assessment.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one successful transaction, latest failure, reprocessed transaction, boundary-value record, and record crossing a time-zone or daylight-saving change; reconcile identifiers and timestamps across source, middleware, target, monitoring, ticketing, and final report.
questions.primary_roles: Integration Owner; System Owners for source and target; Data Owner; IT Operations; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: No end-to-end identifier or reconciliation; monitoring only transport availability; discarded error messages; uncontrolled replay; duplicate processing; manual correction outside audit trail; source and target totals disagree without investigation.

questions.audit_question: Starting from the full alert population, demonstrate how quality-relevant alarms are rationalized, prioritized, routed, acknowledged, investigated, and closed within defined limits, including periods when the primary responder is unavailable.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one suppressed, auto-closed, repeated, or missed alert and reconstruct what occurred in the regulated process during the blind period; explain how the impact population was identified and why recurrence is controlled.
questions.rationale_risk: Excessive, suppressed, or poorly routed alerts can normalize failure and allow quality or data-integrity conditions to persist undetected.
questions.expected_evidence: Alert catalogue and rationale, thresholds, routing and escalation rules, on-call coverage, raw alert history, acknowledgement and response records, suppression approvals, deviations or incidents, trend review, and effectiveness actions. Acceptance requires complete population visibility, risk-based response limits, controlled suppression, and impact assessment for missed alerts.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample latest critical alert, longest unacknowledged alert, one recurring alert, one suppression, and one after-hours event; reconcile monitoring timestamps to system logs, on-call notifications, ITSM, process records, and deviation system.
questions.primary_roles: IT Operations; System Owner; Process Owner; Monitoring Platform Owner; Quality Assurance; Information Security where applicable
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 211.68(a); ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
questions.red_flags: No complete alert population; alert floods or chronic recurrence; critical alert auto-closed; undocumented suppression; response SLA measured without quality impact; blind periods not assessed; no escalation outside business hours.

questions.audit_question: Show how the periodic evaluation derives and challenges incident, deviation, problem, and service-request trends from complete source populations rather than relying on ticket labels or manually selected quality events.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reclassify a sample of low-severity or non-GxP-labelled tickets against the system's intended use and data flows; explain any event that should have triggered a deviation, validation impact assessment, or broader retrospective review.
questions.rationale_risk: Misclassification at intake can systematically exclude weak signals from Quality oversight and periodic-review conclusions.
questions.expected_evidence: Incident and deviation taxonomy, linkage rules, complete ITSM and quality-event extracts, trend method, reclassification controls, management review, and actions. Acceptance requires reconciled populations, documented inclusion and exclusion logic, challenge of repeat events, and escalation of potential GxP impact.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one non-GxP-labelled outage, one data correction request, one recurring low-severity issue, one supplier ticket, and one closed-without-cause event; trace to logs, records affected, deviation system, problem record, and periodic review.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Incident Manager; Quality Assurance; Process Owner; Problem Manager; Service Desk Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
questions.red_flags: IT and Quality populations do not reconcile; GxP impact determined by service-desk category alone; recurring events fragmented; exclusions lack rationale; data corrections treated as requests rather than events; trend omits supplier cases.

questions.audit_question: For the highest-risk recurring problem, demonstrate that root cause and CAPA effectiveness were established with objective evidence and that recurrence was assessed across related systems, sites, records, and supplier services.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show the search logic used to declare no recurrence, then broaden it to synonyms, different ticket categories, similar error codes, manual corrections, and near misses; explain any events the original effectiveness check missed.
questions.rationale_risk: Narrow recurrence searches or completion-based effectiveness checks can close CAPA without proving that the causal mechanism was removed.
questions.expected_evidence: Problem investigation, causal evidence, CAPA plan, implementation records, cross-system applicability assessment, defined effectiveness measure and observation period, complete recurrence query, results, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires cause-specific measures, adequate time and population, no unexplained recurrence, and escalation when effectiveness is not demonstrated.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one closed CAPA and one overdue or failed CAPA; rerun the recurrence query against ITSM, deviation, monitoring, change, audit-trail exception, and supplier populations; trace identified events back to impact decisions.
questions.primary_roles: Problem Manager; CAPA Owner; System Owner; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
questions.red_flags: Root cause stated as human error without systemic analysis; CAPA effectiveness equals task completion; recurrence query undocumented or narrow; repeat events relabelled; no cross-system assessment; failed effectiveness check not reopened.

questions.audit_question: Using the complete change and release history since the previous evaluation, demonstrate how cumulative effects on intended use, data integrity, security, performance, interfaces, supplier dependencies, and validation status were assessed.
questions.follow_up_probe: Identify individually minor changes that touched the same critical function or control and explain why their combined effect did not require revised requirements, risk assessment, regression testing, or revalidation.
questions.rationale_risk: Repeated low-risk changes can collectively alter a critical function or erode validated controls without any single ticket triggering adequate assurance.
questions.expected_evidence: Complete change population, releases and supplier changes, affected-component mapping, cumulative-impact method, revised risk and traceability records, regression evidence, periodic-evaluation conclusion, and Quality approvals. Acceptance requires reconciliation to deployment and configuration history and explicit assessment of repeated changes to critical functions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Group changes by component, requirement, data element, interface, and control for the review period; sample one high-risk change, three related low-risk changes, one emergency change, and one supplier release; reconcile to repository, deployment, CMDB, incidents, and tests.
questions.primary_roles: Change Manager; System Owner; Validation Lead; Configuration Manager; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.
questions.red_flags: Deployment population exceeds approved changes; minor changes never aggregated; repeated changes to same control; supplier releases omitted; incidents rise after changes; validation documents and system description not updated.

questions.audit_question: Compare the live production configuration to the approved baseline and demonstrate how authorized differences, temporary settings, feature flags, emergency changes, and supplier-managed parameters are detected and governed.
questions.follow_up_probe: The auditor will select a security, audit-trail, retention, calculation, interface, or workflow parameter from the live system and ask for its last change, approver, test evidence, and current baseline entry.
questions.rationale_risk: Undetected drift can change intended performance, weaken audit trails or security, or alter regulated calculations and workflows outside validation.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved baseline, automated or controlled configuration export, comparison report, parameter ownership, authorized change records, temporary-change expiry, drift alerts, investigation, and re-baselining approval. Acceptance requires complete critical-parameter coverage and no unexplained production difference.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare current export with last approved baseline and deployment artifact; sample one critical parameter from each of security, audit trail, data retention, interface, and workflow; trace differences to change, test, and incident records.
questions.primary_roles: Configuration Manager; System Administrator; System Owner; Validation Lead; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: No approved baseline; comparison omits critical parameters; manual snapshots without provenance; unexplained drift; expired feature flags; supplier settings inaccessible; direct changes visible only in audit logs after the fact.

questions.audit_question: Trace the vulnerability population for the system to patch, mitigation, acceptance, or retirement decisions and demonstrate how product quality, data integrity, availability, exploitability, supplier constraints, and validation impact determine remediation priority.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the oldest high or critical vulnerability and show the actual affected asset and version, exposure path, compensating-control telemetry, accountable risk acceptance, reassessment cadence, and evidence that the control would detect exploitation.
questions.rationale_risk: Generic scoring or unsupported risk acceptance can leave exploitable pathways to regulated records and critical operations while appearing administratively closed.
questions.expected_evidence: Asset and software inventory, scanner and supplier advisories, vulnerability records, applicability validation, risk decisions, patch changes and tests, compensating controls and logs, exception expiry, and periodic review. Acceptance requires complete scope, timely risk-based action, approved and time-bound exceptions, and verified compensating controls.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile scanner results, SBOM or software inventory, CMDB, vendor notices, firewall or EDR telemetry, change records, and production versions; sample oldest critical, a false positive, a compensating-control case, and a recently patched item.
questions.primary_roles: Information Security; System Owner; Infrastructure Owner; Validation Lead; Change Manager; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 12; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SI and RA controls as nonbinding security guidance.
questions.red_flags: Assets missing from scan scope; risk accepted from CVSS alone; overdue critical vulnerabilities; compensating control asserted without telemetry; exception has no expiry; supplier constraint accepted indefinitely; patch not linked to validation impact.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that security logging covers the events capable of affecting regulated data or validated configuration and that detections remain effective when logs are delayed, malformed, tampered with, or unavailable.
questions.follow_up_probe: Generate or locate an auditor-selected high-risk event such as failed privileged access, audit-log disablement, mass export, configuration change, or unusual service-account use and trace it from source through collection, correlation, alert, investigation, and retention.
questions.rationale_risk: Logging may exist without complete coverage, tamper resistance, usable time correlation, or detections that reveal unauthorized activity affecting GxP controls.
questions.expected_evidence: Logging risk assessment, event and source inventory, time synchronization, retention, access controls, SIEM ingestion health, detection rules, alert tests, incident records, and gap monitoring. Acceptance requires coverage of critical events, protected and synchronized logs, tested detections, monitored collection failures, and retained evidence.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select events from application, database, operating system, identity provider, cloud platform, and audit-trail configuration; reconcile native logs with SIEM, alert, incident, user identity, and change records; include one ingestion outage.
questions.primary_roles: Security Operations; System Owner; Platform Administrator; IAM Owner; Incident Manager; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Detect and Respond functions as nonbinding guidance.
questions.red_flags: Critical log sources not onboarded; clocks not synchronized; administrators can alter logs; collection gaps invisible; alert never tested; retention shorter than record or investigation need; security events not assessed for GxP impact.

questions.audit_question: For one critical provider-managed control, demonstrate how the regulated company obtains sufficient ongoing assurance from contract obligations, service evidence, performance data, exceptions, and independent verification rather than relying solely on a certification.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the most recent supplier incident, control exception, subprocessor change, or forced release and show when you were notified, how GxP impact was assessed, what evidence the supplier supplied, and how your Quality unit challenged closure.
questions.rationale_risk: Outsourcing execution does not transfer the regulated company's responsibility; weak oversight can conceal control failure or unassessed provider change.
questions.expected_evidence: Quality or service agreement, shared-responsibility matrix, supplier qualification and reassessment, audit or assurance reports with bridge coverage, SLA and control metrics, incident and change notices, exceptions and CAPA, subprocessor inventory, and exit provisions. Acceptance requires clear accountability, timely evidence access, evaluated exceptions, and risk-based independent checks.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one provider-managed backup or restore control, privileged-access control, security incident, release, and subprocessor change; reconcile contract, supplier portal or reports, internal monitoring, tickets, validation impact, and periodic evaluation.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Manager; System Owner; Cloud Service Owner; Information Security; Legal or Procurement; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 11, 12, 13, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10 where applicable remains the regulated user's responsibility; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SR controls as nonbinding guidance.
questions.red_flags: Certification treated as complete evidence; expired bridge period; agreement omits GxP records or inspection access; supplier changes not notified; subprocessor unknown; exceptions not assessed; responsibility gap for backup, logs, incidents, or data return.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how capacity, response time, job completion, error rate, queue depth, storage growth, and availability trends are converted into risk-based actions before degraded service affects data completeness or regulated decisions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the period with worst performance and show which records, interfaces, calculations, users, or batch decisions were exposed; explain why thresholds and forecasts detected the condition early enough.
questions.rationale_risk: Performance degradation can create delayed, incomplete, duplicated, or manually reconstructed records without a clear system failure.
questions.expected_evidence: Service objectives, capacity model, monitoring data, threshold rationale, forecasts, performance incidents, data-impact checks, scaling or remediation changes, and management review. Acceptance requires critical-process linkage, defined action thresholds, reliable data, timely actions, and assessment of any excursion.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review at least 12 months or one full business cycle; sample peak load, worst response, storage threshold breach, long-running job, and capacity change; reconcile monitoring to transaction counts, interface queues, tickets, and process records.
questions.primary_roles: IT Service Owner; Capacity Manager; System Owner; Process Owner; Infrastructure Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(a) for applicable drug CGMP systems.
questions.red_flags: Only uptime reported; thresholds lack business basis; capacity breach accepted without data-impact review; recurring peak failures; monitoring gaps; manual workarounds unrecorded; forecast action repeatedly deferred.

questions.audit_question: For each role capable of creating, reviewing, administering, changing, recovering, or investigating GxP records, demonstrate that current procedures and task-specific competence were effective before the person performed unsupervised work.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a person involved in the last deviation, emergency change, failed restore, or audit-trail exception and compare their actual actions with training content, effective procedure version, access grant date, and demonstrated competence.
questions.rationale_risk: Completion records alone do not establish competence, and outdated or generic training can allow incorrect actions that compromise data or validated state.
questions.expected_evidence: Role and curriculum mapping, effective SOPs and work instructions, training assignments and completion, competency assessment, access prerequisites, supervised qualification where needed, retraining after change or deviation, and effectiveness evidence. Acceptance requires no unsupervised activity before qualification and procedures aligned to current system behavior.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample one business user, reviewer, administrator, vendor engineer, incident responder, and recovery operator; reconcile HR role, training system, procedure version, access history, activity log, and event records.
questions.primary_roles: Training Owner; System Owner; Functional Manager; Process Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier Manager
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 2; 21 CFR 11.10(i) where Part 11 applies; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6.5 and 6.6.
questions.red_flags: Access granted before training; training only attendance-based; obsolete procedure; vendor personnel omitted; deviation reveals procedure-content gap; recurring retraining without system or process correction; no competency evidence for critical tasks.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate through the most recent exercise or outage that the manual or alternative process can be activated within the approved time and produces complete, attributable, controlled records that are accurately reconciled when the system returns.
questions.follow_up_probe: Extend the scenario beyond the planned exercise duration and explain how blank forms, identifiers, calculations, approvals, duplicate prevention, backlog, storage, and later transcription remain controlled when staff, network, or identity services are also unavailable.
questions.rationale_risk: A nominal workaround may fail under sustained outage or generate uncontrolled hybrid records, duplicate transactions, transcription errors, and undocumented decisions.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved continuity procedure, activation criteria, controlled forms or alternate system, role and contact lists, exercise records, source and reconciliation logs, deviation handling, Quality and business acceptance, and improvement actions. Acceptance requires timely activation, ALCOA+ records, controlled backlog, verified reconciliation, and tested extended or compound scenarios commensurate with risk.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review latest exercise and actual outage; select records created during downtime and trace them from controlled issuance through approval, storage, system entry, duplicate check, reconciliation, and archival; compare timing with RTO.
questions.primary_roles: Process Owner; Business Continuity Owner; Operations Users; System Owner; Records Manager; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 16; PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle and hybrid-record principles; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
questions.red_flags: Workaround untested or only tabletop; uncontrolled blank forms or spreadsheets; no unique identifiers; backlog exceeds capacity; duplicate prevention absent; reconciliation incomplete; exercise ignores compound failure or long outage.

questions.audit_question: Produce an accurate and complete human-readable copy and electronic copy of an auditor-selected record and demonstrate that both preserve the content, context, metadata, audit trail, signatures, units, calculations, and relationships needed for independent review.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare the copies to the live source at field level and show how hidden fields, attachments, deleted or superseded values, dynamic report logic, and linked records are represented; explain every difference.
questions.rationale_risk: A visually acceptable PDF or report can omit metadata, prior values, attachments, audit trails, or machine-readable relationships and therefore be incomplete for inspection.
questions.expected_evidence: Copy-generation procedure, validated or verified export function, sample human-readable and electronic copies, field and record mapping, completeness checks, audit trail and signature output, and reviewer evidence. Acceptance requires accurate, complete, intelligible, reproducible copies suitable for inspection and no unexplained omission or transformation.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one simple record, one corrected record, one signed record, one record with attachments, and one archived record; compare source display, database or API extract, human-readable output, electronic package, and checksums or control totals where used.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; System Owner; Data Owner; Process Owner; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: 21 CFR 11.10(b); EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 8, 9, 14, and 17.
questions.red_flags: Only screenshots or summary PDF available; audit trail or metadata omitted; electronic copy proprietary and unusable; export changes units, precision, timestamps, or record relationships; copy function unverified after change. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how hardware, operating-system, database, application, integration, certificate, and supplier-support obsolescence is identified early and converted into funded, time-bound risk controls or replacement decisions.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the component nearest or beyond end of support and show the credible failure and threat scenarios, unavailable patches or expertise, recovery and archive dependencies, compensating-control effectiveness, and executive and Quality acceptance of continued use.
questions.rationale_risk: Unsupported technology can make security remediation, recovery, record retrieval, validation maintenance, and supplier support unreliable while business dependence persists.
questions.expected_evidence: Technology and support lifecycle inventory, supplier notices, risk assessment, vulnerabilities, spares and skills plan, recovery and archive testing, compensating controls with monitoring, replacement roadmap, funding and milestones, and periodic approvals. Acceptance requires no unmanaged end-of-support component and evidence that interim controls are effective and temporary.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile CMDB and software inventory to vendor lifecycle notices and vulnerability data; select the oldest component, one unsupported dependency, and one expiring certificate or license; trace to risk, budget, change roadmap, and recovery test.
questions.primary_roles: System Owner; Enterprise Architect; Infrastructure Owner; Information Security; Business Sponsor; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 7, 11, 12, 16, and 17; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
questions.red_flags: End-of-support status unknown; risk acceptance repeatedly extended; no funded exit plan; recovery depends on unavailable media, keys, hardware, or skills; vulnerabilities cannot be mitigated; archive readability tied to failing platform.

questions.audit_question: Show how accountable business, system, and Quality owners converted the periodic-review evidence into a defensible continued-use, restricted-use, remediation, replacement, or retirement decision with explicit residual risks and patient, product, data, and availability consequences.
questions.follow_up_probe: Take the strongest counter-evidence to the approved conclusion and explain how it was challenged, who had authority to reject continued use, what risk-reducing action was required before the next GxP transaction, and what trigger would suspend the system.
questions.rationale_risk: Governance can become a ceremonial approval that normalizes unresolved systemic risk and leaves no clear threshold for restricting or stopping use.
questions.expected_evidence: Periodic-review evidence package, residual-risk register, decision criteria, dissent or challenge records, accountable approvals, restrictions and interim controls, funded actions, escalation and suspension triggers, and follow-up monitoring. Acceptance requires transparent rationale, authority independent enough to challenge business pressure, time-bound actions, and traceability to evidence.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare latest decision with prior review, open critical actions, incident and vulnerability trends, failed controls, business-criticality assessment, and roadmap funding; trace one accepted risk to operational monitoring and one closed risk to effectiveness evidence.
questions.primary_roles: Process Owner; System Owner; Quality Assurance; Business Sponsor; Risk Owner; Information Security
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1 and 11; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3, 4.4, 4.5, and 4.6.
questions.red_flags: Approval lacks explicit decision or residual risk; unresolved critical evidence ignored; no independent Quality challenge; actions lack funding or dates; accepted risk has no monitoring or expiry; no defined suspend-use trigger.

questions.audit_question: Build the complete population of production changes for the review period from deployment, repository, infrastructure, database, cloud, and supplier sources and reconcile it to approved change records.
questions.follow_up_probe: Explain every production artifact, configuration timestamp, feature-flag transition, schema update, emergency action, or supplier release that lacks a one-to-one approved change reference, including why it was not detected earlier.
questions.rationale_risk: Testing only approved tickets cannot reveal unauthorized or unrecorded changes; population completeness must be established independently from the production estate.
questions.expected_evidence: Change procedure, ITSM extract, deployment and orchestration logs, repository history, database change logs, cloud audit logs, supplier release notices, configuration comparisons, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires all production changes to be authorized, uniquely traceable, correctly classified, and investigated when unmatched.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Define the population from at least two independent production sources; reconcile to ITSM for the last 12 months and since the last major release; sample unmatched events, weekend changes, supplier changes, failed deployments, and rollbacks.
questions.primary_roles: Change Manager; System Owner; Configuration Manager; DevOps or Release Lead; Supplier Manager; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(b).
questions.red_flags: Production activity exceeds ticket population; manual or supplier changes absent; mismatches closed without investigation; cloud feature flags omitted; direct database edits; deployment logs unavailable; repeated after-the-fact ticket creation.

questions.audit_question: For an auditor-selected change, demonstrate how the classification was derived from affected intended uses, critical data, records, interfaces, security controls, infrastructure dependencies, and regulated decisions rather than from the requestor's label.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reassess a change classified as standard, low risk, or non-GxP after following its dependency chain; show what evidence proves that no indirect effect on a GxP function or record was overlooked.
questions.rationale_risk: Superficial classification can reduce testing and Quality oversight for changes whose indirect dependencies affect validated state or data integrity.
questions.expected_evidence: Change classification criteria, system and data-flow documentation, dependency mapping, impact assessment, risk assessment, affected requirement and control list, review and approval. Acceptance requires evidence-based scope, consideration of indirect and cumulative effects, and documented rationale for reduced controls.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one high-risk, one low-risk, one standard, one infrastructure, and one supplier change; compare classification with actual files, services, data objects, roles, and interfaces changed and with post-change incidents.
questions.primary_roles: Change Owner; System Owner; Validation Lead; Solution Architect; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.2, 4.3, and 10; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
questions.red_flags: Classification copied from requestor; dependencies not assessed; infrastructure declared non-GxP by default; no data-flow impact; testing reduced without rationale; post-change incident contradicts low-risk conclusion.

questions.audit_question: Reperform the risk assessment for the highest-risk recent change and show how foreseeable failure modes, affected decisions, uncertainty, detectability, and existing control performance determined assurance and rollback activities.
questions.follow_up_probe: Replace the assumed successful detection with a silent-failure scenario and explain which independent control would reveal corrupt, incomplete, unauthorized, or delayed data before use or release.
questions.rationale_risk: Risk assessments can be reverse-engineered to justify a preferred test scope and may overestimate detectability or ignore uncertainty.
questions.expected_evidence: Defined risk question, multidisciplinary assessment, prior incident and defect data, failure modes and consequences, control effectiveness evidence, uncertainty and assumptions, residual risk, assurance plan, rollback criteria, and approvals. Acceptance requires scientific rationale and effort commensurate with patient, product, and data risk.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare the risk assessment with prior related failures, production monitoring, defect history, actual changed components, tests, and post-implementation evidence; challenge one high-detectability rating and one accepted residual risk.
questions.primary_roles: Risk Facilitator; System Owner; Process Owner; Validation Lead; Technical SME; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1 and 4.1; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3, 4.2, 4.3, and 5.
questions.red_flags: Risk completed after implementation; no failure modes; detectability assumed; prior failures ignored; severity reduced by controls; single assessor; residual risk accepted by conflicted owner; test scope decided before risk analysis.

questions.audit_question: Trace one changed GxP function from the approved business need through revised requirement, risk, design or configuration, test evidence, defect resolution, release, and updated lifecycle documentation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Identify behavior that changed without a revised requirement or a requirement marked unaffected despite changed code or configuration, and explain how unintended effects were made visible and tested.
questions.rationale_risk: A change can pass selected tests while breaking lifecycle traceability and leaving altered behavior, controls, or records undocumented.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved change need, revised requirement and acceptance criteria, affected risk and design records, trace matrix, configuration or code reference, tests and results, defects, validation summary or release decision, and updated system documentation. Acceptance requires bidirectional traceability and no unexplained changed behavior.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one critical function and trace forward and backward; compare requirement revisions with repository diff, configuration diff, test cases, user documentation, and production release; inspect orphan changed objects and orphan tests.
questions.primary_roles: Business Analyst; Process Owner; Validation Lead; Developer or Configurator; Tester; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Behavior changed without requirement; trace matrix updated mechanically; tests not linked to risk; obsolete design remains approved; orphan code or configuration; open defect absent from release decision.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that request, technical implementation, verification, production deployment, and Quality or business approval for a change were performed by appropriately independent and authorized roles.
questions.follow_up_probe: For a small team or supplier-managed service, show how one person could not create, approve, deploy, and conceal the same change; demonstrate the operating evidence for each compensating control where independence was structurally limited.
questions.rationale_risk: Conflicted change roles enable unauthorized or inadequately verified modifications and weaken accountability for production impact.
questions.expected_evidence: Role and authorization matrix, workflow configuration, repository and deployment permissions, approval and deployment logs, privileged-access monitoring, exception records, and compensating-control reviews. Acceptance requires enforced independence or documented, effective, and independently reviewed compensating controls.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one normal, one emergency, one supplier, and one database change; reconcile named actors across ITSM, repository, CI/CD, privileged session, deployment, and Quality records.
questions.primary_roles: Change Manager; System Owner; Release Manager; IAM Owner; Quality Assurance; Supplier Service Owner
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 10, and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b).
questions.red_flags: Same person requests, approves, deploys, and verifies; workflow bypass; generic deployment account; supplier self-certification without user oversight; compensating review after long delay; admin activity not monitored.

questions.control_topic: Approved baseline and version source of truth
questions.audit_question: Show how the pre-change and post-change approved baselines identify every version and critical configuration needed to reproduce, support, recover, and audit the released system.
questions.follow_up_probe: Rebuild the production version statement from live components rather than the release document and explain any difference in code, package, database object, parameter, report, interface map, dependency, or security setting.
questions.rationale_risk: An incomplete or manually asserted baseline prevents reliable impact assessment, rollback, recovery, drift detection, and reconstruction of the validated state.
questions.expected_evidence: Baseline procedure, pre- and post-change configuration records, live automated inventory or signed exports, package and dependency manifests, hashes where used, approved differences, and CMDB updates. Acceptance requires complete, immutable or controlled provenance and exact reconciliation to production.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Compare release manifest, repository tag, artifact store, database version, cloud or infrastructure configuration, application about page, and CMDB; sample one hidden dependency and one parameter outside the application UI.
questions.primary_roles: Configuration Manager; Release Manager; System Administrator; Developer or Configurator; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b).
questions.red_flags: Baseline is a manually edited spreadsheet without source reconciliation; dependencies omitted; production differs from tag; no pre-change state; hashes unavailable; CMDB stale; rollback package cannot be identified.

questions.audit_question: Reconcile the approved change to the exact repository commit, peer review, automated build, dependency set, signed or hashed artifact, deployment execution, and live production version.
questions.follow_up_probe: Demonstrate that the artifact deployed to production could not have been modified after test approval and that a rebuild from the approved source would produce an equivalent artifact; explain any manual step.
questions.rationale_risk: Broken provenance permits unreviewed source, altered binaries, environment-specific manual edits, or different dependencies to reach production.
questions.expected_evidence: Repository history, branch protections, review record, build logs, dependency lock or manifest, artifact-store metadata, checksum or signing evidence, deployment logs, and production verification. Acceptance requires immutable traceability, authorized promotion, reproducible or otherwise controlled build, and no direct production edits.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one production artifact and trace backward to source and forward from approval to production; compare test and production artifact hashes, dependency versions, build identity, and deployment account; include one failed build or deployment.
questions.primary_roles: Developer; Peer Reviewer; Build or DevOps Engineer; Release Manager; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 4.6, 4.7, and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Mutable artifact repository; build from unreviewed branch; dependency drift; test and production artifacts differ; manual copying; generic deployment identity; inability to map binary or report to source. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how regression scope covered not only the changed function but every critical upstream, downstream, shared, and negative behavior whose control effectiveness could be altered by the change.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show a critical function excluded from regression and provide objective evidence for the exclusion, then compare that rationale with code or configuration dependency analysis and recent defect history.
questions.rationale_risk: Happy-path testing of the requested feature can miss unintended effects on audit trails, signatures, calculations, reports, interfaces, permissions, error handling, or recovery.
questions.expected_evidence: Change and dependency analysis, risk-control trace, regression rationale, test cases and results, automated-test adequacy assessment where used, defects and deviations, and approvals. Acceptance requires coverage proportionate to risk, documented exclusions, representative environments and data, and resolution of failures before release.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select highest-risk changed function; trace dependencies to regression tests; inspect excluded tests, failed tests, reruns, and production incidents; compare automated-test report to raw execution logs and tool version.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Test Lead; Developer or Configurator; Process Owner; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.7, and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(a); ICH Q9(R1) Section 3.
questions.red_flags: Regression chosen by developer alone; audit trail or security omitted; failed test overwritten; rerun lacks deviation; test tool or environment changed without assessment; exclusions unsupported; production defect matches omitted scenario. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Negative and boundary assurance after change
questions.audit_question: Challenge the changed control with invalid, missing, duplicate, out-of-order, oversized, unauthorized, and boundary data and demonstrate that the system rejects, contains, or clearly flags each condition without corrupting the retained record.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show the raw evidence for a failed negative test and the resulting database, audit trail, queue, or file state; explain how partial processing and residual test data were detected and removed under control.
questions.rationale_risk: A change may work for valid inputs yet silently accept malformed or partial data, create duplicates, or leave inconsistent records under foreseeable error conditions.
questions.expected_evidence: Data-risk assessment, boundary definitions, negative test design, raw inputs and outputs, audit trails and logs, database or interface state verification, cleanup controls, deviations, and retest. Acceptance requires deterministic error handling, preserved original data, no silent partial commit, and traceable exception messages.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select critical data elements and one interface or calculation; compare requirement limits with test values; inspect application output, database state, audit trail, middleware log, and monitoring alert for each negative case.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Test Lead; Integration Owner; Database Administrator; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.red_flags: Only positive tests; boundary not based on specification; partial data remains; error silently retried; original input lost; audit trail absent; failed case deleted without deviation; database not inspected.

questions.audit_question: Prove that test evidence was generated in the approved environment against the approved build and data set by authorized testers, and that results, screenshots, logs, timestamps, deviations, and reruns form a complete contemporaneous record.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one screenshot or summary result and trace it to native system logs, test-data identifiers, build version, tester identity, and execution timestamp; identify evidence created or edited after execution and explain why.
questions.rationale_risk: Manually curated test packages can conceal wrong builds, undocumented reruns, altered evidence, unrepresentative environments, or failed steps.
questions.expected_evidence: Environment qualification and equivalence, build deployment record, tester authorization, test-data control, raw execution logs, contemporaneous evidence, deviations and rerun links, electronic approvals, and evidence-retention controls. Acceptance requires attributable and complete evidence tied to exact build and environment with no unexplained post-execution alteration.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one passed, one failed, and one rerun case; reconcile protocol metadata, application and infrastructure logs, audit trail, artifact version, tester access, defect ticket, and approval timestamps.
questions.primary_roles: Test Lead; Validation Lead; Environment Manager; Tester; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, and 4.7; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(i) where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Screenshots lack context; evidence edited later; wrong build or environment; shared tester account; failed step absent; rerun overwrites original; test data untraceable; environment materially unlike production without justification.

questions.audit_question: For the most severe open or deferred defect at release, demonstrate how actual and potential effects on product, patient, data, security, and operations were bounded and how the release decision controlled residual risk.
questions.follow_up_probe: Reproduce or simulate the defect under the most adverse credible condition and explain why the workaround or compensating control is reliable for every affected user, record, site, and shift until permanent correction.
questions.rationale_risk: Defects may be downgraded or deferred to meet schedule without adequately bounding population, worst-case impact, or workaround effectiveness.
questions.expected_evidence: Defect record, reproduction and causal evidence, affected requirement and risk, population and impact assessment, workaround test and communication, residual-risk approval, release restriction, CAPA or fix plan, and monitoring. Acceptance requires no unresolved defect that invalidates intended use and time-bound controls for accepted defects.
