questions.red_flags: Archive is only file storage; proprietary viewer dependency unaddressed; audit trails or signatures excluded; no integrity monitoring; original identity context lost; retention and deletion manual; archive recovery absent.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how migration scope, sequencing, freeze periods, coexistence, transformation, reconciliation, exception handling, rollback, source preservation, and final cutover were derived from data and process risk.
questions.follow_up_probe: Assume the source must be shut down after a partially successful migration and explain how rejected records, late transactions, interfaces, manual workarounds, and rollback or forward recovery remain controlled without creating two conflicting systems of record.
questions.rationale_risk: Migration plans often cover bulk transfer but not transitional transactions, rejects, cutover ambiguity, or source preservation after partial failure.
questions.expected_evidence: Approved migration plan and risk assessment, source and target scopes, freeze and cutover design, data ownership, transformation rules, validation strategy, reconciliation, reject handling, rollback or forward-fix plan, source preservation, responsibilities, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires one authoritative record at each point and controlled exception paths.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review dry run, final run, and one failed or exception cycle; reconcile source transaction cutoff, interface queues, manual records, extract, load, rejects, target activation, and source read-only status.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Owner; System Owners; Process Owner; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c) and 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
questions.red_flags: No authoritative-system rule during coexistence; late transactions omitted; rejects handled informally; rollback ignores new records; source altered or destroyed before acceptance; migration risk generic; Quality not involved.

questions.audit_question: Trace every transformation of critical data and metadata from source representation to target and demonstrate that value, precision, units, code meaning, relationships, null semantics, status, chronology, and attribution remain unchanged or are explicitly approved.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one defaulted, concatenated, split, rounded, truncated, recoded, unmapped, or deprecated value and show how its original meaning and downstream use can still be reconstructed.
questions.rationale_risk: Row counts can match while clinical, manufacturing, laboratory, or quality meaning changes through subtle transformation.
questions.expected_evidence: Source and target dictionaries, approved mapping, transformation specifications, code and unit crosswalks, precision rules, relationship handling, scripts under control, test evidence, exceptions, and business or Quality sign-off. Acceptance requires no unapproved change of value or meaning and retained provenance for approved transformations.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Risk-rank fields and sample minimum, maximum, null, multibyte, obsolete code, maximum precision, historical status, and linked records; compare source, extract, transformation log, target, reports, and archive copy.
questions.primary_roles: Data Architect; Data Owner; Migration Developer; Process SME; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(b); PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle principles.
questions.red_flags: Mapping inferred from code; unit or precision changes undocumented; nulls converted to zero; obsolete codes dropped; relationship broken; transformation script differs from approved version; downstream report not reconciled.

questions.audit_question: Reconcile the full source population to extracted, transformed, loaded, rejected, quarantined, duplicated, and excluded populations using immutable cut-off criteria and independent control totals.
questions.follow_up_probe: Explain how matching total row counts could still hide missing child records, duplicated parents, changed amounts, null fields, attachment loss, or status shifts and show the additional checks that reveal each risk.
questions.rationale_risk: Single aggregate totals can mask offsetting errors and incomplete relational, file, or metadata transfer.
questions.expected_evidence: Frozen source population, extraction logs, staged and target counts, field totals, relational counts, hash or checksum evidence where appropriate, reject and exclusion logs, duplicate checks, attachments and audit-trail totals, independent review, and approved reconciliation. Acceptance requires every source item accounted for exactly once or formally dispositioned.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reperform totals from source and target; stratify by record class, date, site, status, parent-child relationship, attachment, audit event, and signature; inspect zero-count and low-volume categories and all exceptions.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Analyst; Database Administrator; Data Owner; Independent Reviewer; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8 and 7; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c); FDA Data Integrity Q&A.
questions.red_flags: Only row count used; source not frozen; excludes and rejects netted out; child or attachment counts absent; duplicate detection weak; reconciliation prepared by migration developer only; unexplained variance accepted.

questions.audit_question: For an auditor-selected critical record, trace the complete source-to-target chain and prove preservation of content, context, metadata, audit trail, signatures, attachments, calculations, relationships, and inspection copies.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a corrected, signed, rejected, or reopened record with multiple versions and explain how the target distinguishes original, prior, current, and superseded states without flattening history.
questions.rationale_risk: Population totals do not prove that complex records and their history remain complete and intelligible.
questions.expected_evidence: Source record and native history, extract and transformation trace, target record and versions, metadata, audit trail, signature links, attachments, related records, calculation or report output, and copy. Acceptance requires field-level equivalence or approved transformation with complete provenance.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Auditor selects high-risk records across oldest and newest dates, sites, statuses, corrections, signatures, attachments, and edge values; compare native source, migration logs, target UI, target database or API, and export package.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; Process SME; Migration Lead; System Owners; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.red_flags: History flattened; only current value migrated; attachments or links missing; signatures displayed without version; calculations differ; target copy omits context; sample chosen by migration team only.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how every migration exception is uniquely identified, preserved, investigated, risk-assessed, corrected under control, independently verified, reprocessed once, and included in final reconciliation.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select the oldest or repeatedly failed exception and show why it did not reveal a broader mapping or source-quality problem; search the accepted population for the same causal pattern.
questions.rationale_risk: Exception queues can become a hidden population where records are manually altered, excluded, duplicated, or accepted without systemic impact assessment.
questions.expected_evidence: Immutable exception log, original rejected payload, error and cause, affected-record and broader-scope assessment, controlled correction, approval, reprocessing logs, duplicate prevention, independent check, and final disposition. Acceptance requires zero unexplained exceptions at release and systemic action for recurring causes.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review all critical and high-risk exceptions plus samples of each error type; reconcile extract, quarantine, correction tool, target, audit trail, deviation, and final control totals; rerun pattern search in accepted records.
questions.primary_roles: Migration Lead; Data Owner; Technical SME; Independent Reviewer; Deviation Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 4.8, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
questions.red_flags: Exception log mutable; original payload lost; manual fix unapproved; repeated errors treated individually; rejected records excluded from totals; reprocessing creates duplicates; open critical exceptions at shutdown.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that the migration or archive preserves every required audit event, prior value, new value, actor, timestamp, action, reason, record linkage, and review status in an intelligible and reviewable form.
questions.follow_up_probe: Compare a raw source audit-trail export with the target or archive for events created by administrators, failed actions, deletions, configuration changes, and periods where user-facing reports normally filter events.
questions.rationale_risk: Audit history may be reduced to a report or subset that omits privileged, failed, or contextual events and no longer supports reconstruction.
questions.expected_evidence: Source audit schema and configuration, full event population, mapping, transformation rules, target or archive events, intelligible display and electronic copy, event and record linkage, review capability, reconciliation, and access control. Acceptance requires complete history and no loss of meaning or reviewability.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select corrected and deleted records, admin activity, failed transactions, reason entries, signature events, and configuration changes; compare native source events, migration logs, target display, database or API, and copy output.
questions.primary_roles: Data Owner; System Administrator; Migration Lead; Quality Reviewer; Validation Lead; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
questions.red_flags: Only audit-trail PDF retained; prior values or reasons omitted; admin or failed events filtered; record linkage broken; timestamps transformed without trace; audit events not searchable or reviewable; source destroyed before reconciliation.

questions.audit_question: Select a migrated or archived signed record and prove that signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, signed record version, and permanent linkage remain intact and cannot be reassigned or detached.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show how signer identity is resolved after the user account, directory, or original application has been removed and how later corrections or format conversions avoid making the original signature appear to approve changed content.
questions.rationale_risk: Migration can preserve a visual signature string while losing the authoritative link to signer and exact approved content.
questions.expected_evidence: Source signed record and signature logs, identity reference, mapping, target or archive record version, manifestation, permanent linkage, correction behavior, copy output, and verification. Acceptance requires durable, unambiguous, non-transferable linkage independent of active user accounts.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select approval, rejection, corrected signed record, inactive signer, and multi-signature record; compare source, identity directory snapshot, migration package, target, audit trail, and human-readable or electronic copy.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; IAM Owner; Data Owner; Migration Lead; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, and 11.200.
questions.red_flags: Signature preserved only as image or text; signer unresolved after account removal; version linkage lost; correction changes signed content without new signature; multiple signatures collapsed; export detaches signature. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate preservation of time-zone and clock context, attachments, images, file properties, external references, annotations, units, display rules, and paper-electronic relationships required to interpret each retained record.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a record crossing a daylight-saving change or site time zone and one whose attachment has the same filename as another record; show unambiguous chronology, association, integrity, and retrieval.
questions.rationale_risk: Contextual metadata and hybrid links can be lost even when primary field values migrate correctly, making the record ambiguous or incomplete.
questions.expected_evidence: Metadata inventory and mapping, time conversion rules, attachment identifiers and hashes where used, MIME and format handling, link and annotation mapping, hybrid-record index, test evidence, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires preserved association, meaning, chronology, and integrity.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample multiple time zones, daylight-saving boundary, duplicate filenames, large and unusual file types, annotated records, external links, images, and hybrid-paper references; compare source metadata, files, target, and archive copies.
questions.primary_roles: Data Architect; Records Manager; Data Owner; Migration Lead; Site Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 8, 9, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b), 11.10(c), and 11.10(e); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance Section 5.1 as nonbinding guidance.
questions.red_flags: Timestamps normalized without original zone; attachments matched by filename only; links broken; unsupported files skipped; annotations omitted; paper-electronic index lost; duplicate files overwrite; hash or size not reconciled.

questions.audit_question: Reconstruct the cutover and prove which system was authoritative for each process, site, record class, and time interval, including how late transactions, backlogs, manual records, and interface queues were controlled.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a record created near the cutover boundary and show how duplicate creation, update in the wrong system, clock difference, and delayed interface delivery were detected and reconciled.
questions.rationale_risk: Parallel systems and timing ambiguity can create conflicting originals, lost late transactions, and duplicate regulated decisions.
questions.expected_evidence: Cutover plan, freeze and authority matrix, synchronized timeline, user and interface controls, queue and backlog inventory, communication, boundary reconciliation, duplicate checks, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance requires one unambiguous authoritative record for every interval and resolved transition exceptions.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Sample records immediately before, at, and after each cutover wave; reconcile source and target audit trails, interface queues, user access changes, manual logs, monitoring, and business reconciliation.
questions.primary_roles: Cutover Manager; Source and Target System Owners; Process Owner; Integration Owner; Data Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(f).
questions.red_flags: Authority rule unclear; both systems writable; boundary times differ; late queue omitted; user access not aligned to freeze; duplicate records; manual backlog unreconciled; source changed after final extract.

questions.audit_question: Trace archive or migration risks and requirements to test scenarios, raw evidence, deviations, reconciliation, acceptance, and release, including boundary, negative, failure, recovery, and long-term retrieval cases.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show the highest-risk requirement with reduced or no scripted testing and demonstrate why other objective evidence provides sufficient assurance; then present the last failed test and its full resolution chain.
questions.rationale_risk: A large migration can generate extensive documentation while leaving critical exception, failure, and long-term usability risks inadequately challenged.
questions.expected_evidence: Validation or assurance plan, risk and requirement trace, test strategy, controlled tools and environments, positive and negative tests, raw execution evidence, deviations and defects, reconciliation, retrieval and recovery tests, summary, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires assurance commensurate with risk and no unexplained failed requirement.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select highest-risk record class, one excluded test, one failed test, one automated tool output, and one archive retrieval after environment change; trace to source requirement, risk, raw logs, deviation, and final approval.
questions.primary_roles: Validation Lead; Test Lead; Migration or Archive Lead; Data Owner; Process Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.7, 4.8, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 3.
questions.red_flags: Testing focused on counts only; long-term retrieval omitted; failed test overwritten; automated tool unassessed; deviations open at release; traceability mechanical; excluded requirements unsupported; source destroyed before approval. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Retrieve an auditor-selected archived record without production-system access and demonstrate timely search, access, readability, integrity, intelligibility, audit history, signature linkage, and accurate human-readable and electronic copies.
questions.follow_up_probe: Repeat the retrieval for the oldest cohort and for a record created before a major format, viewer, operating-system, or archive-platform change; explain every manual or specialist step required.
questions.rationale_risk: Archive success at migration does not prove records remain usable and inspection-ready throughout retention as technology changes.
questions.expected_evidence: Archive search and retrieval procedure, access authorization, native or preserved representation, metadata and audit history, signature linkage, copies, integrity verification, retrieval SLA, platform-change tests, and exception handling. Acceptance requires reproducible timely retrieval with complete meaning and no dependence on the retired production environment.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Auditor selects oldest, corrected, signed, attached, and legal-hold records; compare archive UI or API, storage object, integrity evidence, human-readable output, electronic package, access logs, and retention rule.
questions.primary_roles: Records Manager; Archive Administrator; Data Owner; Process Owner; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c).
questions.red_flags: Retrieval requires retired application; oldest records unreadable; metadata or audit trail absent; signatures unresolved; electronic copy proprietary or incomplete; manual reconstruction undocumented; SLA missed without action.

questions.control_topic: Ongoing archive integrity and technology refresh
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how periodic checks prove archive accessibility, readability, integrity, security, backup, recovery, capacity, and viewer compatibility and how results trigger controlled technology refresh before records become at risk.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show the last failed integrity, retrieval, or compatibility check, identify every potentially affected object, and demonstrate correction, retrospective scope, retest, and trend action.
questions.rationale_risk: Latent corruption and technology obsolescence may remain undetected for years until records are requested for inspection or investigation.
questions.expected_evidence: Periodic-check procedure and risk-based frequency, complete archive population, integrity and retrieval results, access and security reviews, backup and recovery tests, capacity and lifecycle monitoring, exceptions, remediation, refresh plan, and Quality review. Acceptance requires complete monitored coverage and effective response to failures.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Review multiple check cycles; sample oldest cohort, infrequently accessed format, encrypted object, large attachment, and changed viewer; reconcile integrity tool, storage, backup, access logs, incidents, and technology roadmap.
questions.primary_roles: Archive Service Owner; Records Manager; Infrastructure Owner; Information Security; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 7.2, 11, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP and SI controls as nonbinding guidance.
questions.red_flags: Only storage availability monitored; integrity check samples too narrow; failed object scope unknown; viewer lifecycle ignored; no restore test; archive exceptions aged; refresh occurs after support expiry; Quality not reviewing trends.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how post-retirement access is limited to current authorized roles, remains attributable, is periodically reviewed, and prevents alteration, bulk extraction, or administrator circumvention of retained GxP records.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one legacy administrator, former project member, vendor account, and service identity and prove termination or current justification across archive, storage, cloud, database, key vault, and backup layers.
questions.rationale_risk: Retired systems receive less operational attention while retaining high-value regulated and personal data and stale privileged access.
questions.expected_evidence: Archive role design, named-user and service-account populations, approvals and reviews, leaver cleanup, privileged-access restrictions, immutable or write-protected controls, access and export logs, alerts, and exceptions. Acceptance requires least privilege, unique attribution, timely revocation, and independent monitoring.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Extract access directly from every archive layer; reconcile to HR, IAM, supplier roster, key vault, storage ACLs, backup platform, and SIEM; sample dormant, privileged, vendor, and rejected access.
questions.primary_roles: Archive Administrator; IAM Owner; Records Manager; Information Security; Supplier Manager; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c), 11.10(d), 11.10(e), and 11.10(g); GDPR Article 32 where personal data apply.
questions.red_flags: Project accounts remain; archive access not reviewed; shared administrator; write access unnecessary; exports unlogged; former supplier access active; lower storage or backup layer omitted; leaver process excludes archive.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how encryption keys, signing certificates, trust chains, secrets, tokens, algorithms, and recovery material needed to access or verify retained records remain available, protected, attributable, and replaceable throughout retention.
questions.follow_up_probe: Simulate loss or expiry of the primary key or certificate and show the tested recovery, escrow, re-encryption, verification, and audit path without weakening access control or losing proof of historical signature validity.
questions.rationale_risk: Records can become permanently unreadable or signatures unverifiable when cryptographic dependencies expire, are destroyed, or rely on a retired service.
questions.expected_evidence: Cryptographic dependency inventory, ownership, key and certificate lifecycle, escrow and backup, algorithm and expiry monitoring, recovery or re-encryption tests, access controls and logs, destruction rules, and technology-refresh plan. Acceptance requires tested continuity and no single undocumented key dependency.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select oldest encrypted record, expired certificate chain, rotated key, backup key, and supplier-managed secret; trace vault, archive object, recovery test, access log, and lifecycle plan.
questions.primary_roles: Cryptographic or Key Management Owner; Archive Administrator; Information Security; Records Manager; Supplier; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(d); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SC and CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
questions.red_flags: Key owner unknown; single key copy; certificate expiry unmonitored; recovery untested; vendor key unavailable after contract; re-encryption changes provenance without control; destruction occurs before retention ends. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate how personal data is minimized and deleted or anonymized when no longer lawfully required while regulated records, legal holds, audit trails, and evidentiary integrity remain protected.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one deletion request or expired personal-data class that intersects a GxP record and show the legal basis, field-level disposition, propagation to replicas and exports, and proof that the retained record remains complete and meaningful.
questions.rationale_risk: Uncoordinated privacy deletion can damage regulated records, while blanket GxP retention can justify unnecessary indefinite storage of personal data.
questions.expected_evidence: Data inventory and classification, lawful-basis and retention mapping, minimization and deletion rules, legal-hold checks, field-level design, anonymization validation where used, propagation to archives, replicas, and suppliers, execution logs, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires lawful, consistent, and auditable disposition without loss of required GxP evidence.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select one fulfilled and one rejected deletion request, one expired record class, one legal hold, and one supplier copy; reconcile privacy case, source, archive, backup policy, supplier response, and record-integrity verification.
questions.primary_roles: Data Protection Officer; Records Manager; Data Owner; Legal; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: GDPR Articles 5, 17, 25, 30, and 32 where applicable; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, and 17; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
questions.red_flags: All data retained indefinitely as GxP; deletion breaks audit trail or attribution; replicas and supplier copies ignored; anonymization reversible or unvalidated; legal hold not checked; deletion evidence unavailable.

questions.audit_question: Account for every backup, replica, snapshot, export, staging area, test copy, disaster-recovery environment, and removable medium and demonstrate its approved retention, access restriction, migration, expiry, or destruction.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select a copy outside the primary production account or data center and prove who can restore it, which keys and software it needs, when it expires, how legal holds apply, and how destruction is verified.
questions.rationale_risk: Residual copies can outlive the system, retain broad access, conflict with legal or privacy disposition, and reintroduce obsolete or uncontrolled data.
questions.expected_evidence: Copy topology and inventory, backup and snapshot catalogues, DR and test environments, exports and media register, retention and hold rules, access, key dependencies, expiration or destruction jobs, certificates, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires complete accounting and no restorable uncontrolled copy.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile production storage, backup console, cloud snapshots, DR account, file-transfer locations, data-lake feeds, test environments, removable media, and supplier copies; sample oldest and off-site copies.
questions.primary_roles: Backup Administrator; Infrastructure Owner; Cloud Owner; Records Manager; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 211.68(b); GDPR Articles 5 and 32 where personal data apply; NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 as nonbinding sanitization guidance.
questions.red_flags: Copy inventory incomplete; snapshots in personal or supplier account; no expiry; restore access retained broadly; legal hold not propagated; test copies forgotten; destruction claimed without verification; keys persist after data destruction.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate the controlled sequence used to stop interfaces, jobs, APIs, file transfers, notifications, monitoring, user accounts, service accounts, certificates, tokens, remote support, and network routes without losing late data or leaving unauthorized pathways.
questions.follow_up_probe: Show live telemetry after the claimed shutdown and explain any authentication attempt, network connection, scheduled execution, queue item, file arrival, or data write, including how it was contained and reconciled.
questions.rationale_risk: Partial shutdown can silently discard late transactions or leave dormant credentials and network paths into retained data and infrastructure.
questions.expected_evidence: Shutdown plan and dependency order, cut-off and queue reconciliation, interface partner confirmation, job and account inventories, revocation and route changes, monitoring period, live telemetry, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires zero unresolved traffic, active identity, or late data after final cut-off.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Inspect application, API gateway, middleware, scheduler, IAM, vault, certificate manager, VPN, firewall, DNS, monitoring, and file-transfer logs before and after shutdown; sample each identity and interface class.
questions.primary_roles: Decommission Lead; Integration Owner; IAM Owner; Network and Security Owners; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 10, 12, 13, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
questions.red_flags: Interfaces stopped before queues reconcile; service accounts active; certificates or tokens valid; late files discarded; network route remains; monitoring removed before observation period; partner not notified; live writes after shutdown.

questions.audit_question: Trace the supplier exit from contract obligations through complete data and metadata return, format usability, transition support, subprocessor coverage, access revocation, residual-copy destruction, evidence availability, and final service termination.
questions.follow_up_probe: Ask the supplier to account for primary, backup, replicated, support, telemetry, log, analytics, and subprocessor copies and compare the response with the shared-responsibility model and your own data-flow evidence.
questions.rationale_risk: A provider may return only business data while retaining logs, backups, replicas, or subprocessor copies or using proprietary formats that impede inspection and continuity.
questions.expected_evidence: Contract and Quality agreement exit clauses, data and copy inventory, export specification and reconciliation, transition and retrieval test, subprocessor attestations, access revocation, deletion or destruction certificate with scope and method, evidence and audit rights, and internal acceptance. Acceptance requires usable complete return and verified disposition of all residual copies.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Reconcile contract, supplier architecture and subprocessor list, tenant exports, support portal, cloud logs, backup and telemetry statements, deletion certificate, internal archive, and access records; sample one nonprimary copy and one subprocessor.
questions.primary_roles: Supplier Manager; System Owner; Records Manager; Legal or Procurement; Information Security; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) to 11.10(d) where Part 11 applies; GDPR Articles 28 and 32 where personal data apply.
questions.red_flags: Contract lacks usable export or deletion terms; proprietary format; audit trails or logs excluded; subprocessor copies unknown; deletion certificate generic; supplier access persists; transition support ends before acceptance; evidence inaccessible after termination. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

questions.control_topic: Sanitization, asset closure, and post-shutdown access
questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that every retired asset and storage location was uniquely identified, removed from service and monitoring inventories at the correct time, sanitized or destroyed with verified results, and did not eliminate required archive or inspection access.
questions.follow_up_probe: Select one reused or cloud-abstracted asset and show the sanitization method, validation or verification, residual-data risk, chain of custody, CMDB update, and proof that no required record or recovery dependency was destroyed.
questions.rationale_risk: Asset disposal can expose residual data or, conversely, destroy the only usable copy, viewer, key, configuration, or evidence needed for retention and inspection.
questions.expected_evidence: Asset and media inventory, disposition authorization, archive and dependency clearance, sanitization method and verification, chain of custody, destruction certificate, cloud provider evidence, CMDB and license updates, and post-shutdown retrieval test. Acceptance requires verified sanitization commensurate with sensitivity and preserved required access.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Select physical disk, virtual volume, cloud resource, removable medium, and reused asset; reconcile asset tag or resource ID, storage map, backup and archive clearance, sanitization record, provider evidence, CMDB, and retrieval test.
questions.primary_roles: Asset Manager; Infrastructure or Cloud Owner; Information Security; Records Manager; System Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, 16, and 17; GDPR Article 32 where personal data apply; NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 as nonbinding current sanitization guidance.
questions.red_flags: Asset list incomplete; generic destruction certificate; sanitization not verified; cloud resource identity unclear; chain of custody gap; required viewer or key destroyed; CMDB still active or removed before shutdown evidence; archive retrieval fails afterward.

questions.audit_question: Demonstrate that final decommissioning approval was based on complete migration or archive acceptance, reconciled records, resolved exceptions, terminated dependencies and access, governed residual copies, preserved inspection capability, updated inventories, and explicit long-term ownership.
questions.follow_up_probe: Choose the strongest unresolved exception or retained dependency at closure and show who accepted the residual risk, how it is monitored, when it expires, what event triggers reopening, and who funds corrective action after the project team disbands.
questions.rationale_risk: Project closure can leave orphaned archives, open exceptions, active accounts, residual copies, and unfunded long-term obligations with no accountable owner.
questions.expected_evidence: Final decommissioning report, evidence index, source and target reconciliation, deviations and CAPA, retrieval and recovery acceptance, access and interface termination, supplier exit, backup and asset disposition, CMDB and inventory updates, residual-risk register, long-term owner and review schedule, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires no hidden critical dependency and durable governance after project closure.
questions.sampling_triangulation: Verify every closure statement against source repositories and live telemetry; select one archive record, one former user and service account, one interface, one backup, one supplier copy, one asset, and one residual action; confirm current ownership.
questions.primary_roles: Decommission Lead; System Owner; Process Owner; Records Manager; Long-Term Service Owner; Quality Assurance
questions.regulatory_alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 lifecycle principle and Sections 4.2, 7, 10, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) to 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.5 and 4.6.
questions.red_flags: Final approval predates evidence; open critical exceptions hidden; archive owner or budget absent; access or interface still active; inventory not updated; residual risk has no expiry or monitoring; source destroyed before verified retrieval; project disbands with open CAPA.
